\chapter{Introduction}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:introduction}}\label{\detokenize{intro/index::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL (Light and Versatile Graphics Library) is a free and open\sphinxhyphen{}source graphics library providing everything you need to create an embedded GUI with easy\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}use graphical elements, beautiful visual effects and a low memory footprint.


\section{Key features}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:key-features}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Powerful building blocks such as buttons, charts, lists, sliders, images, etc.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Advanced graphics with animations, anti\sphinxhyphen{}aliasing, opacity, smooth scrolling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Various input devices such as touchpad, mouse, keyboard, encoder, etc.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multi\sphinxhyphen{}language support with UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 encoding

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multi\sphinxhyphen{}display support, i.e. use multiple TFT, monochrome displays simultaneously

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fully customizable graphic elements with CSS\sphinxhyphen{}like styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hardware independent: use with any microcontroller or display

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Scalable: able to operate with little memory (64 kB Flash, 16 kB RAM)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
OS, external memory and GPU are supported but not required

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Single frame buffer operation even with advanced graphic effects

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Written in C for maximal compatibility (C++ compatible)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Simulator to start embedded GUI design on a PC without embedded hardware

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Binding to MicroPython

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tutorials, examples, themes for rapid GUI design

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Documentation is available online and as PDF

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Free and open\sphinxhyphen{}source under MIT license

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{intro/index:requirements}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Basically, every modern controller which is able to drive a display is suitable to run LVGL. The minimal requirements are:




\section{License}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:license}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LVGL project (including all repositories) is licensed under \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/blob/master/LICENCE.txt}{MIT license}.
This means you can use it even in commercial projects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It's not mandatory, but we highly appreciate it if you write a few words about your project in the \sphinxhref{https://forum.lvgl.io/c/my-projects/10}{My projects} category of the forum or a private message to \sphinxhref{https://lvgl.io/\#contact}{lvgl.io}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Although you can get LVGL for free there is a massive amount of work behind it. It's created by a group of volunteers who made it available for you in their free time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To make the LVGL project sustainable, please consider {\hyperref[\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{contributing}}}} to the project.
You can choose from {\hyperref[\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{many different ways of contributing}}}} such as simply writing a tweet about you using LVGL, fixing bugs, translating the documentation, or even becoming a maintainer.

\label{\detokenize{intro/index:repository-layout}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All repositories of the LVGL project are hosted on GitHub: https://github.com/lvgl

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/blog}{blog} Source of the blog's site (https://blog.lvgl.io)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/sim}{sim} Source of the online simulator's site (https://sim.lvgl.io)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl?q=lv\_port\&type=\&language=}{lv\_port\_...} LVGL ports to development boards or environments

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl?q=lv\_binding\&type=\&language=l}{lv\_binding\_..} Bindings to other languages

\end{itemize}


\section{Release policy}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:release-policy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The core repositories follow the rules of \sphinxhref{https://semver.org/}{Semantic versioning}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Major versions for incompatible API changes. E.g. v5.0.0, v6.0.0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Minor version for new but backward\sphinxhyphen{}compatible functionalities. E.g. v6.1.0, v6.2.0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Patch version for backward\sphinxhyphen{}compatible bug fixes. E.g. v6.1.1, v6.1.2

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tags like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vX.Y.Z}} are created for every release.


\subsection{Release cycle}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:release-cycle}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bug fixes: Released on demand even weekly

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Minor releases: Every 3\sphinxhyphen{}4 months

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Major releases: Approximately yearly

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Branches}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:branches}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The core repositories have at least the following branches:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{master}} latest version, patches are merged directly here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{release/vX.Y}} stable versions of the minor releases

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fix/some\sphinxhyphen{}description}} temporary branches for bug fixes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feat/some\sphinxhyphen{}description}} temporary branches for features

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Changelog}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:changelog}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The changes are recorded in {\hyperref[\detokenize{CHANGELOG::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{CHANGELOG.md}}}}.


\subsection{Version support}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:version-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before v8 the last minor release of each major series was supported for 1 year.
Starting from v8, every minor release is supported for 1 year.




\section{FAQ}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:faq}}

\subsection{Where can I ask questions?}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:where-can-i-ask-questions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can ask questions in the forum: \sphinxurl{https://forum.lvgl.io/}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
We use \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/issues}{GitHub issues} for development related discussion.
You should use them only if your question or issue is tightly related to the development of the library.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before posting a question, please ready this FAQ section as you might find answer to your issue here too.


\subsection{Is my MCU/hardware supported?}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:is-my-mcu-hardware-supported}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every MCU which is capable of driving a display via parallel port, SPI, RGB interface or anything else and fulfills the {\hyperref[\detokenize{intro/index:requirements}]{\emph{Requirements}}} is supported by LVGL.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This includes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
"Common" MCUs like STM32F, STM32H, NXP Kinetis, LPC, iMX, dsPIC33, PIC32, SWM341 etc.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bluetooth, GSM, Wi\sphinxhyphen{}Fi modules like Nordic NRF and Espressif ESP32

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Linux with frame buffer device such as /dev/fb0. This includes Single\sphinxhyphen{}board computers like the Raspberry Pi

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Anything else with a strong enough MCU and a peripheral to drive a display

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Is my display supported?}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:is-my-display-supported}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL needs just one simple driver function to copy an array of pixels into a given area of the display.
If you can do this with your display then you can use it with LVGL.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some examples of the supported display types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
TFTs with 16 or 32 bit color depth

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Monitors with an HDMI port

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Small monochrome displays

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Gray\sphinxhyphen{}scale displays

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
even LED matrices

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
or any other display where you can control the color/state of the pixels

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/display::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Porting}}}} section to learn more.


\subsection{LVGL doesn't start, randomly crashes or nothing is drawn on the display. What can be the problem?}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:lvgl-doesn-t-start-randomly-crashes-or-nothing-is-drawn-on-the-display-what-can-be-the-problem}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Try increasing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_MEM\_SIZE}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be sure \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_drv\_t}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_indev\_drv\_t}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fs\_drv\_t}} are global or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{static}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be sure your display works without LVGL. E.g. paint it to red on start up.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable {\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/log::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Logging}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable asserts in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_ASSERT\_...}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you use an RTOS
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
increase the stack size of the task which calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_timer\_handler()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be sure you used a mutex as {\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/os::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{described here}}}}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{My display driver is not called. What have I missed?}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:my-display-driver-is-not-called-what-have-i-missed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be sure you are calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tick\_inc(x)}} in an interrupt and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_timer\_handler()}} in your main \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{while(1)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/tick::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Tick}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/timer-handler::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Timer handler}}}} sections.


\subsection{Why is the display driver called only once? Only the upper part of the display is refreshed.}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:why-is-the-display-driver-called-only-once-only-the-upper-part-of-the-display-is-refreshed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be sure you are calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_flush\_ready(drv)}} at the end of your "\sphinxstyleemphasis{display flush callback}".

\subsection{Why do I see nonsense colors on the screen?}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:why-do-i-see-nonsense-colors-on-the-screen}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Probably LVGL's color format is not compatible with your display's color format. Check \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH}} in \sphinxstyleemphasis{lv\_conf.h}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are using 16\sphinxhyphen{}bit colors with SPI (or another byte\sphinxhyphen{}oriented interface) you probably need to set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_16\_SWAP  1}} in \sphinxstyleemphasis{lv\_conf.h}.
It swaps the upper and lower bytes of the pixels.


\subsection{How to speed up my UI?}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:how-to-speed-up-my-ui}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Turn on compiler optimization and enable cache if your MCU has it

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Increase the size of the display buffer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use two display buffers and flush the buffer with DMA (or similar peripheral) in the background

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Increase the clock speed of the SPI or parallel port if you use them to drive the display

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If your display has an SPI port consider changing to a model with a parallel interface because it has much higher throughput

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep the display buffer in internal RAM (not in external SRAM) because LVGL uses it a lot and it should have a fast access time

\end{itemize}


\subsection{How to reduce flash/ROM usage?}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:how-to-reduce-flash-rom-usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can disable all the unused features (such as animations, file system, GPU etc.) and object types in \sphinxstyleemphasis{lv\_conf.h}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are using GCC/CLANG you can add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}fdata\sphinxhyphen{}sections \sphinxhyphen{}ffunction\sphinxhyphen{}sections}} compiler flags and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}gc\sphinxhyphen{}sections}} linker flag to remove unused functions and variables from the final binary. If possible, add the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}flto}} compiler flag to enable link\sphinxhyphen{}time\sphinxhyphen{}optimisation together with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Os}} for GCC or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Oz}} for CLANG.


\subsection{How to reduce the RAM usage}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:how-to-reduce-the-ram-usage}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower the size of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Display buffer}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduce \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_MEM\_SIZE}} in \sphinxstyleemphasis{lv\_conf.h}. This memory is used when you create objects like buttons, labels, etc.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To work with lower \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_MEM\_SIZE}} you can create objects only when required and delete them when they are not needed anymore

\end{itemize}


\subsection{How to work with an operating system?}
\label{\detokenize{intro/index:how-to-work-with-an-operating-system}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To work with an operating system where tasks can interrupt each other (preemptively) you should protect LVGL related function calls with a mutex.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/os::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Operating system and interrupts}}}} section to learn more.

\sphinxstepscope

\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include} \PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}../../lv\PYGZus{}examples.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}LABEL \PYGZam{}\PYGZam{} LV\PYGZus{}BUILD\PYGZus{}EXAMPLES}

\PYG{c+cm}{/**}
\PYG{c+cm}{ * Create a fake text shadow}
\PYG{c+cm}{ */}
\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{lv\PYGZus{}example\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}2}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a style for the shadow*/}

    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}shadow}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}shadow}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}black}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a label for the shadow first (it\PYGZsq{}s in the background)*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{shadow\PYGZus{}label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{shadow\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}shadow}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Create the main label*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{main\PYGZus{}label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{main\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{A simple method to create}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
                      \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{shadows on a text.}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
                      \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{It even works with}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
                      \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{newlines     and spaces.}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set the same text for the shadow label*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{shadow\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{main\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Position the main label*/}

\PYG{n}{win} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{win}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{60}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{btn1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{win}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{SYMBOL}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{LEFT}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{40}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{event\PYGZus{}handler}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{EVENT}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{ALL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{win}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}title}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{A title}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{btn2}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{win}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{SYMBOL}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{RIGHT}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{40}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{btn2}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{event\PYGZus{}handler}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{EVENT}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{ALL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}

\chapter{Get started}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/index:get-started}}\label{\detokenize{get-started/index::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are several ways to get your feet wet with LVGL. Here is one recommended order of documents to read and things to play with when you are learning to use LVGL:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check the \sphinxhref{https://lvgl.io/demos}{Online demos} to see LVGL in action (3 minutes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read the \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/latest/en/html/intro/index.html}{Introduction} page of the documentation (5 minutes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read the \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/get-started/quick-overview.html}{Quick overview} page of the documentation (15 minutes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set up a \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/get-started/platforms/pc-simulator.html}{Simulator} (10 minutes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Try out some \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/examples.html}{Examples}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check out the Platform\sphinxhyphen{}specific tutorials. (in this section below). (10 minutes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Port LVGL to a board. See the \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/porting/index.html}{Porting} guide or check the ready to use \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl?q=lv\_port\_\&type=\&language=}{Projects}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read the \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/overview/index.html}{Overview} page to get a better understanding of the library. (2\sphinxhyphen{}3 hours)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check the documentation of the \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/widgets/index.html}{Widgets} to see their features and usage

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have questions got to the \sphinxhref{http://forum.lvgl.io/}{Forum}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read the \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/CONTRIBUTING.html}{Contributing} guide to see how you can help to improve LVGL (15 minutes)

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Quick overview}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:quick-overview}}\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here you can learn the most important things about LVGL.
You should read this first to get a general impression and read the detailed {\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/index::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Porting}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/index::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Overview}}}} sections after that.


\subsection{Get started in a simulator}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:get-started-in-a-simulator}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead of porting LVGL to embedded hardware straight away, it's highly recommended to get started in a simulator first.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL is ported to many IDEs to be sure you will find your favorite one.
Go to the \sphinxhref{/get-started/pc-simulator}{Simulators} section to get ready\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}use projects that can be run on your PC.
This way you can save the time of porting for now and get some experience with LVGL immediately.


\subsection{Add LVGL into your project}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:add-lvgl-into-your-project}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you would rather try LVGL on your own project follow these steps:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/archive/master.zip}{Download} or clone the library from GitHub with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{git clone https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl.git}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copy the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} folder into your project.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copy \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl/lv\_conf\_template.h}} as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} next to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} folder, change the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#if 0}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} to enable the file's content and set the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH}} defines.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Include \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl/lvgl.h}} in files where you need to use LVGL related functions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tick\_inc(x)}} every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} milliseconds in a Timer or Task (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} should be between 1 and 10). It is required for the internal timing of LVGL.
Alternatively, configure \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TICK\_CUSTOM}} (see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}) so that LVGL can retrieve the current time directly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_init()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a draw buffer: LVGL will render the graphics here first, and send the rendered image to the display.
The buffer size can be set freely but 1/10 screen size is a good starting point.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}buf\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}buf}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{buf1}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{DISP\PYGZus{}HOR\PYGZus{}RES} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{DISP\PYGZus{}VER\PYGZus{}RES} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}                        \PYG{c+cm}{/*Declare a buffer for 1/10 screen size*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}buf\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}buf}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{buf1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{MY\PYGZus{}DISP\PYGZus{}HOR\PYGZus{}RES} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{MY\PYGZus{}DISP\PYGZus{}VER\PYGZus{}SER} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}  \PYG{c+cm}{/*Initialize the display buffer.*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Implement and register a function which can copy the rendered image to an area of your display:

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}drv\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{disp\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{;}        \PYG{c+cm}{/*Descriptor of a display driver*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}drv\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{disp\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}          \PYG{c+cm}{/*Basic initialization*/}
\PYG{n}{disp\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{flush\PYGZus{}cb} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}flush}\PYG{p}{;}    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set your driver function*/}
\PYG{n}{disp\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}buf} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}buf}\PYG{p}{;}        \PYG{c+cm}{/*Assign the buffer to the display*/}
\PYG{n}{disp\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{hor\PYGZus{}res} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{MY\PYGZus{}DISP\PYGZus{}HOR\PYGZus{}RES}\PYG{p}{;}   \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set the horizontal resolution of the display*/}
\PYG{n}{disp\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ver\PYGZus{}res} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{MY\PYGZus{}DISP\PYGZus{}VER\PYGZus{}RES}\PYG{p}{;}   \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set the vertical resolution of the display*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}drv\PYGZus{}register}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{disp\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}      \PYG{c+cm}{/*Finally register the driver*/}

\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{my\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}flush}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}drv\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{disp}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k}{const} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}area\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{area}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{color\PYGZus{}p}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{k+kt}{int32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{c+cm}{/*It\PYGZsq{}s a very slow but simple implementation.}
\PYG{c+cm}{     *`set\PYGZus{}pixel` needs to be written by you to a set pixel on the screen*/}
    \PYG{k}{for}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{area}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{y1}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{n}{y} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{area}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{y2}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{k}{for}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{x} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{area}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{x1}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{n}{x} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{area}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{x2}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
            \PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}pixel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{color\PYGZus{}p}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
            \PYG{n}{color\PYGZus{}p}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{;}
        \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}flush\PYGZus{}ready}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{disp}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}         \PYG{c+cm}{/* Indicate you are ready with the flushing*/}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Implement and register a function which can read an input device. E.g. for a touchpad:

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}drv\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{indev\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{;}           \PYG{c+cm}{/*Descriptor of a input device driver*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}drv\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{indev\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}             \PYG{c+cm}{/*Basic initialization*/}
\PYG{n}{indev\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{type} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}INDEV\PYGZus{}TYPE\PYGZus{}POINTER}\PYG{p}{;}    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Touch pad is a pointer\PYGZhy{}like device*/}
\PYG{n}{indev\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{read\PYGZus{}cb} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}touchpad\PYGZus{}read}\PYG{p}{;}      \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set your driver function*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}drv\PYGZus{}register}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{indev\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}         \PYG{c+cm}{/*Finally register the driver*/}

\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{my\PYGZus{}touchpad\PYGZus{}read}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{indev}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}data\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{c+cm}{/*`touchpad\PYGZus{}is\PYGZus{}pressed` and `touchpad\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}xy` needs to be implemented by you*/}
    \PYG{k}{if}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{touchpad\PYGZus{}is\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
      \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}INDEV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{;}
      \PYG{n}{touchpad\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}xy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{point}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{point}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
      \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}INDEV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}RELEASED}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_timer\_handler()}} periodically every few milliseconds in the main \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{while(1)}} loop or in an operating system task.
It will redraw the screen if required, handle input devices, animation etc.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a more detailed guide go to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/index::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Porting}}}} section.


\subsection{Learn the basics}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:learn-the-basics}}

\subsubsection{Widgets}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:widgets}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The graphical elements like Buttons, Labels, Sliders, Charts etc. are called objects or widgets. Go to {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/index::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Widgets}}}} to see the full list of available widgets.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every object has a parent object where it is created. For example, if a label is created on a button, the button is the parent of label.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The child object moves with the parent and if the parent is deleted the children will be deleted too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Children can be visible only within their parent's bounding area. In other words, the parts of the children outside the parent are clipped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A Screen is the "root" parent. You can have any number of screens.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To get the current screen call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_scr\_act()}}, and to load a screen use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_scr\_load(scr1)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can create a new object with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_<type>\_create(parent)}}. It will return an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_t *}} variable that can be used as a reference to the object to set its parameters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{slider1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}slider\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set some basic attributes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_<parameter\_name>(obj, <value>)}} functions can be used. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{30}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}y}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{200}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Along with the basic attributes, widgets can have type specific parameters which are set by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_<widget\_type>\_set\_<parameter\_name>(obj, <value>)}} functions. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}slider\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{slider1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{70}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}ANIM\PYGZus{}ON}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To see the full API visit the documentation of the widgets or the related header file (e.g. \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/blob/master/src/widgets/lv\_slider.h}{lvgl/src/widgets/lv\_slider.h}).


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Events are used to inform the user that something has happened with an object.
You can assign one or more callbacks to an object which will be called if the object is clicked, released, dragged, being deleted, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A callback is assigned like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{btn\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}CLICKED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*Assign a callback to the button*/}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n}{btn\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{printf}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Clicked}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_ALL}} can be used instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CLICKED}} to invoke the callback for any event.

\sphinxAtStartPar
From \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_t * e}} the current event code can be retrieved with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}code\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{code} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}code}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The object that triggered the event can be retrieved with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{obj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}target}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To learn all features of the events go to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Event overview}}}} section.


\subsubsection{Parts}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:parts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Widgets might be built from one or more \sphinxstyleemphasis{parts}. For example, a button has only one part called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}}.
However, a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/slider::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Slider}}}} has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_KNOB}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By using parts you can apply different styles to sub\sphinxhyphen{}elements of a widget. (See below)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Read the widgets' documentation to learn which parts each uses.


\subsubsection{States}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:states}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL objects can be in a combination of the following states:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}}  Normal, released state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_CHECKED}}  Toggled or checked state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUSED}} Focused via keypad or encoder or clicked via touchpad/mouse

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUS\_KEY}}  Focused via keypad or encoder but not via touchpad/mouse

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_EDITED}} Edit by an encoder

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_HOVERED}} Hovered by mouse (not supported now)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_PRESSED}} Being pressed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_SCROLLED}} Being scrolled

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DISABLED}} Disabled

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, if you press an object it will automatically go to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUSED}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_PRESSED}} states and when you release it the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_PRESSED}} state will be removed while focus remains active.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To check if an object is in a given state use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_has\_state(obj, LV\_STATE\_...)}}. It will return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if the object is currently in that state.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To manually add or remove states use:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}clear\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Styles}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A style instance contains properties such as background color, border width, font, etc. that describe the appearance of objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles are represented with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_t}} variables. Only their pointer is saved in the objects so they need to be defined as static or global.
Before using a style it needs to be initialized with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_init(\&style1)}}. After that, properties can be added to configure the style. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hex}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mh}{0xa03080}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}border\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the full list of properties \sphinxhref{/overview/style.html\#properties}{here}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles are assigned using the ORed combination of an object's part and state. For example to use this style on the slider's indicator when the slider is pressed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{slider1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}INDICATOR} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{part} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} it can be omitted:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*Equal to LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}MAIN | LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarly, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}} can be omitted too:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{slider1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}INDICATOR}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*Equal to LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}INDICATOR | LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} simply write \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*Equal to LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}MAIN | LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles can be cascaded (similarly to CSS). It means you can add more styles to a part of an object.
For example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style\_btn}} can set a default button appearance, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style\_btn\_red}} can overwrite the background color to make the button red:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style1\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a property is not set on for the current state, the style with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}} will be used. A default value is used if the property is not defined in the default state.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some properties (typically the text\sphinxhyphen{}related ones) can be inherited. This means if a property is not set in an object it will be searched for in its parents too.
For example, you can set the font once in the screen's style and all text on that screen will inherit it by default.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Local style properties also can be added to objects. This creates a style which resides inside the object and is used only by the object:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{slider1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hex}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mh}{0x2080bb}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}INDICATOR} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To learn all the features of styles see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Style overview}}}} section.


\subsubsection{Themes}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:themes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Themes are the default styles for objects. Styles from a theme are applied automatically when objects are created.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The theme for your application is a compile time configuration set in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:examples}}

\subsubsection{A button with a label and react on click event}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:a-button-with-a-label-and-react-on-click-event}}


\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}


\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include} \PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}../lv\PYGZus{}examples.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}BUILD\PYGZus{}EXAMPLES \PYGZam{}\PYGZam{} LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}BTN}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{btn\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}code\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{code} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}code}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{btn} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}target}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{k}{if}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{code} \PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}CLICKED}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{uint8\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{cnt} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
        \PYG{n}{cnt}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{;}

        \PYG{c+cm}{/*Get the first child of the button which is the label and change its text*/}
        \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}child}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
        \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text\PYGZus{}fmt}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Button: \PYGZpc{}d}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{cnt}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+cm}{/**}
\PYG{c+cm}{ * Create a button with a label and react on click event.}
\PYG{c+cm}{ */}
\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{lv\PYGZus{}example\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}started\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{btn} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}     \PYG{c+cm}{/*Add a button the current screen*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}pos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}                            \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set its position*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{120}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}                          \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set its size*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{btn\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}ALL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}           \PYG{c+cm}{/*Assign a callback to the button*/}

    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}          \PYG{c+cm}{/*Add a label to the button*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Button}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}                     \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set the labels text*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}center}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{endif}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}


\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{class} \PYG{n+nc}{CounterBtn}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{def} \PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{cnt} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}
        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a button with a label and react on click event.}
        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}

        \PYG{n}{btn} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}                               \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add a button the current screen}
        \PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}pos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}                                      \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set its position}
        \PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{120}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}                                    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set its size}
        \PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{ALIGN}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{CENTER}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{btn\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{EVENT}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{ALL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Assign a callback to the button}
        \PYG{n}{label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{)}                                    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add a label to the button}
        \PYG{n}{label}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Button}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}                                 \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set the labels text}
        \PYG{n}{label}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{center}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{k}{def} \PYG{n+nf}{btn\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{evt}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get the first child of the button which is the label and change its text}
        \PYG{n}{label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}child}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n}{label}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Button: }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n+nb}{str}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{cnt}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}


\PYG{n}{counterBtn} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{CounterBtn}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\end{sphinxuseclass}



\subsubsection{Create styles from scratch for buttons}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/quick-overview:create-styles-from-scratch-for-buttons}}

\section{Platforms}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/index:platforms}}\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/index::doc}}
\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Simulator on PC}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:simulator-on-pc}}\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can try out LVGL \sphinxstylestrong{using only your PC} (i.e. without any development boards). LVGL will run on a simulator environment on the PC where anyone can write and experiment with real LVGL applications.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the simulator on a PC has the following advantages:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hardware independent \sphinxhyphen{} Write code, run it on the PC and see the result on a monitor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform \sphinxhyphen{} Any Windows, Linux or macOS system can run the PC simulator.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Portability \sphinxhyphen{} The written code is portable, which means you can simply copy it when migrating to embedded hardware.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Easy Validation \sphinxhyphen{} The simulator is also very useful to report bugs because it provides a common platform for every user. So it's a good idea to reproduce a bug in the simulator and use that code snippet in the \sphinxhref{https://forum.lvgl.io}{Forum}.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Select an IDE}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:select-an-ide}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The simulator is ported to various IDEs (Integrated Development Environments). Choose your favorite IDE, read its README on GitHub, download the project, and load it to the IDE.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_sim\_eclipse\_sdl}{Eclipse with SDL driver}: Recommended on Linux and Mac

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_sim\_codeblocks\_win}{CodeBlocks}: Recommended on Windows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_sim\_visual\_studio\_sdl}{VisualStudio}: For Windows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_sim\_vscode\_sdl}{VSCode with SDL driver}: Recommended on Linux and Mac

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_platformio}{PlatformIO with SDL driver}: Recommended on Linux and Mac

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_port\_an547\_cm55\_sim}{MDK with FastModel}: For Windows

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
External project not maintained by the LVGL organization:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/Varanda-Labs/lvgl-qt-sim}{QT Creator}: Cross platform

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can use any IDE for development but, for simplicity, the configuration for Eclipse CDT is what we'll focus on in this tutorial.
The following section describes the set\sphinxhyphen{}up guide of Eclipse CDT in more detail.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Note: If you are on Windows, it's usually better to use the Visual Studio or CodeBlocks projects instead. They work out of the box without requiring extra steps.}


\subsubsection{Set\sphinxhyphen{}up Eclipse CDT}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:set-up-eclipse-cdt}}

\paragraph{Install Eclipse CDT}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:install-eclipse-cdt}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://eclipse.org/cdt/}{Eclipse CDT} is a C/C++ IDE.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Eclipse is a Java\sphinxhyphen{}based tool so be sure \sphinxstylestrong{Java Runtime Environment} is installed on your system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On Debian\sphinxhyphen{}based distros (e.g. Ubuntu): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sudo apt\sphinxhyphen{}get install default\sphinxhyphen{}jre}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note: If you are using other distros, then please install a 'Java Runtime Environment' suitable to your distro.
Note: If you are using macOS and get a "Failed to create the Java Virtual Machine" error, uninstall any other Java JDK installs and install Java JDK 8u. This should fix the problem.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can download Eclipse's CDT from: \sphinxurl{https://www.eclipse.org/cdt/downloads.php}. Start the installer and choose \sphinxstyleemphasis{Eclipse CDT} from the list.


\paragraph{Install SDL 2}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:install-sdl-2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The PC simulator uses the \sphinxhref{https://www.libsdl.org/download-2.0.php}{SDL 2} cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform library to simulate a TFT display and a touchpad.


\subparagraph{Linux}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:linux}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On \sphinxstylestrong{Linux} you can easily install SDL2 using a terminal:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find the current version of SDL2: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apt\sphinxhyphen{}cache search libsdl2 (e.g. libsdl2\sphinxhyphen{}2.0\sphinxhyphen{}0)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install SDL2: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sudo apt\sphinxhyphen{}get install libsdl2\sphinxhyphen{}2.0\sphinxhyphen{}0}} (replace with the found version)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install SDL2 development package: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sudo apt\sphinxhyphen{}get install libsdl2\sphinxhyphen{}dev}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If build essentials are not installed yet: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sudo apt\sphinxhyphen{}get install build\sphinxhyphen{}essential}}

\end{enumerate}


\subparagraph{Windows}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:windows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are using \sphinxstylestrong{Windows} firstly you need to install MinGW (\sphinxhref{http://mingw-w64.org/doku.php/download}{64 bit version}). After installing MinGW, do the following steps to add SDL2:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download the development libraries of SDL.
Go to \sphinxurl{https://www.libsdl.org/download-2.0.php} and download \sphinxstyleemphasis{Development Libraries: SDL2\sphinxhyphen{}devel\sphinxhyphen{}2.0.5\sphinxhyphen{}mingw.tar.gz}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decompress the file and go to \sphinxstyleemphasis{x86\_64\sphinxhyphen{}w64\sphinxhyphen{}mingw32} directory (for 64 bit MinGW) or to \sphinxstyleemphasis{i686\sphinxhyphen{}w64\sphinxhyphen{}mingw32} (for 32 bit MinGW)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copy \_...\sphinxstyleemphasis{mingw32/include/SDL2} folder to \sphinxstyleemphasis{C:/MinGW/.../x86\_64\sphinxhyphen{}w64\sphinxhyphen{}mingw32/include}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copy \_...\sphinxstyleemphasis{mingw32/lib/} content to \sphinxstyleemphasis{C:/MinGW/.../x86\_64\sphinxhyphen{}w64\sphinxhyphen{}mingw32/lib}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copy \_...\sphinxstyleemphasis{mingw32/bin/SDL2.dll} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{\{eclipse\_workspace\}/pc\_simulator/Debug/}.  Do it later when Eclipse is installed.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note: If you are using \sphinxstylestrong{Microsoft Visual Studio} instead of Eclipse then you don't have to install MinGW.


\subparagraph{OSX}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:osx}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On \sphinxstylestrong{OSX} you can easily install SDL2 with brew: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{brew install sdl2}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If something is not working, then please refer \sphinxhref{http://lazyfoo.net/tutorials/SDL/01\_hello\_SDL/index.php}{this tutorial} to get started with SDL.


\paragraph{Pre\sphinxhyphen{}configured project}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:pre-configured-project}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A pre\sphinxhyphen{}configured graphics library project (based on the latest release) is always available to get started easily.
You can find the latest one on \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_sim\_eclipse\_sdl}{GitHub}.
(Please note that, the project is configured for Eclipse CDT).


\paragraph{Add the pre\sphinxhyphen{}configured project to Eclipse CDT}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:add-the-pre-configured-project-to-eclipse-cdt}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run Eclipse CDT. It will show a dialogue about the \sphinxstylestrong{workspace path}. Before accepting the path, check that path and copy (and unzip) the downloaded pre\sphinxhyphen{}configured project there. After that, you can accept the workspace path. Of course you can modify this path but in that case copy the project to the corresponding location.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Close the start\sphinxhyphen{}up window and go to \sphinxstylestrong{File\sphinxhyphen{}>Import} and choose \sphinxstylestrong{General\sphinxhyphen{}>Existing project into Workspace}. \sphinxstylestrong{Browse the root directory} of the project and click \sphinxstylestrong{Finish}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On \sphinxstylestrong{Windows} you have to do two additional things:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copy the \sphinxstylestrong{SDL2.dll} into the project's Debug folder

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Right\sphinxhyphen{}click on the project \sphinxhyphen{}> Project properties \sphinxhyphen{}> C/C++ Build \sphinxhyphen{}> Settings \sphinxhyphen{}> Libraries \sphinxhyphen{}> Add ... and add \sphinxstyleemphasis{mingw32} above SDLmain and SDL. (The order is important: mingw32, SDLmain, SDL)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Compile and Run}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator:compile-and-run}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Now you are ready to run LVGL on your PC. Click on the Hammer Icon on the top menu bar to Build the project. If you have done everything right, then you will not get any errors. Note that on some systems additional steps might be required to "see" SDL 2 from Eclipse but in most cases the configuration in the downloaded project is enough.

\sphinxAtStartPar
After a successful build, click on the Play button on the top menu bar to run the project. Now a window should appear in the middle of your screen.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Now you are ready to use LVGL and begin development on your PC.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{NXP}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:nxp}}\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
NXP has integrated LVGL into the MCUXpresso SDK packages for general purpose and crossover microcontrollers, allowing
easy evaluation and migration into your product design.
\sphinxhref{https://www.nxp.com/design/software/embedded-software/littlevgl-open-source-graphics-library:LITTLEVGL-OPEN-SOURCE-GRAPHICS-LIBRARY?\&tid=vanLITTLEVGL-OPEN-SOURCE-GRAPHICS-LIBRARY}{Download an SDK for a supported board}
today and get started with your next GUI application.


\subsubsection{Creating new project with LVGL}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:creating-new-project-with-lvgl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Downloading the MCU SDK example project is recommended as a starting point. It comes fully configured with LVGL (and
with PXP/VGLite support if the modules are present), no additional integration work is required.


\subsubsection{HW acceleration for NXP iMX RT platforms}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:hw-acceleration-for-nxp-imx-rt-platforms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Depending on the RT platform used, the acceleration can be done by NXP PXP (PiXel Pipeline) and/or the Verisilicon GPU
through an API named VGLite. Each accelerator has its own context that allows them to be used individually as well
simultaneously (in LVGL multithreading mode).


\paragraph{PXP accelerator}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:pxp-accelerator}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Several drawing features in LVGL can be offloaded to the PXP engine. The CPU is available for other operations while the
PXP is running. RTOS is required to block the LVGL drawing thread and switch to another task or suspend the CPU for
power savings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Supported draw callbacks are available in "src/draw/nxp/pxp/lv\_draw\_pxp.c":

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
    \PYG{n}{pxp\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}decoded} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}pxp\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}decoded}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{pxp\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{blend} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}pxp\PYGZus{}blend}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{pxp\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{wait\PYGZus{}for\PYGZus{}finish} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}pxp\PYGZus{}wait\PYGZus{}for\PYGZus{}finish}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{pxp\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{buffer\PYGZus{}copy} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}pxp\PYGZus{}buffer\PYGZus{}copy}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Features supported:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:features-supported}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{All} \PYG{n}{operations} \PYG{n}{can} \PYG{n}{be} \PYG{n}{used} \PYG{n}{in} \PYG{n}{conjunction} \PYG{n}{with} \PYG{n}{optional} \PYG{n}{transparency}\PYG{p}{.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RGB565 and ARGB8888 color formats

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Area fill with color

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
BLIT (BLock Image Transfer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Screen Rotation (90, 180, 270 degree)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Color keying

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recoloring (color tint)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Image Rotation (90, 180, 270 degree)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Buffer copy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RTOS integration layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default FreeRTOS and bare metal code provided

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combination of recolor and/or rotation + color key/alpha blend/transparency is supported.
That is achieved by PXP in two steps:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
First step is to recolor/rotate the image to a temporary buffer (statically allocated)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Second step is required to handle color keying, alpha channel or to apply transparency

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Known limitations:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:known-limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rotation is not supported for images unaligned to blocks of 16x16 pixels.
PXP is set to process 16x16 blocks to optimize the system for memory bandwidth and image processing time.
The output engine essentially truncates any output pixels after the desired number of pixels has been written.
When rotating a source image and the output is not divisible by the block size, the incorrect pixels could be truncated
and the final output image can look shifted.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Basic configuration:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:basic-configuration}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select NXP PXP engine in lv\_conf.h: Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_GPU\_NXP\_PXP}} to 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable default implementation for interrupt handling, PXP start function and automatic initialization:
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_GPU\_NXP\_PXP\_AUTO\_INIT}} to 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SDK\_OS\_FREE\_RTOS}} symbol is defined, FreeRTOS implementation will be used, otherwise bare metal code will be
included

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Basic initialization:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:basic-initialization}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_GPU\_NXP\_PXP\_AUTO\_INIT}} is enabled, no user code is required; PXP is initialized automatically in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_init()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For manual PXP initialization, default configuration structure for callbacks can be used. Initialize PXP before
calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_init()}}

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
      \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}GPU\PYGZus{}NXP\PYGZus{}PXP}
        \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include} \PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}src/draw/nxp/pxp/lv\PYGZus{}gpu\PYGZus{}nxp\PYGZus{}pxp.h\PYGZdq{}}
      \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{endif}
      \PYG{p}{.} \PYG{p}{.} \PYG{p}{.}
      \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}GPU\PYGZus{}NXP\PYGZus{}PXP}
        \PYG{n}{PXP\PYGZus{}COND\PYGZus{}STOP}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{!}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}gpu\PYGZus{}nxp\PYGZus{}pxp\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{PXP init failed.}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
      \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{endif}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Project setup:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:project-setup}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add PXP related files to project:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/pxp/lv\_draw\_pxp.c{[}.h{]}: draw context callbacks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/pxp/lv\_draw\_pxp\_blend.c{[}.h{]}: fill and blit (with optional transformation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/pxp/lv\_gpu\_nxp\_pxp.c{[}.h{]}: init, uninit, run/wait PXP device

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/pxp/lv\_gpu\_nxp\_pxp\_osa.c{[}.h{]}: OS abstraction (FreeRTOS or bare metal)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
optional, required only if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_GPU\_NXP\_PXP\_AUTO\_INIT}} is set to 1

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PXP related code depends on two drivers provided by MCU SDK. These drivers need to be added to project:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fsl\_pxp.c{[}.h{]}: PXP driver

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fsl\_cache.c{[}.h{]}: CPU cache handling functions

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Logging:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:logging}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GPU\_NXP\_PXP\_LOG\_ERRORS}} is enabled so that any PXP error will be seen on SDK debug console

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GPU\_NXP\_PXP\_LOG\_TRACES}} is disabled. Enable it for tracing logs (like PXP limitations)

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Advanced configuration:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:advanced-configuration}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Implementation depends on multiple OS\sphinxhyphen{}specific functions. The struct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_nxp\_pxp\_cfg\_t}} with callback pointers is
used as a parameter for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_gpu\_nxp\_pxp\_init()}} function. Default implementation for FreeRTOS and bare metal is
provided in lv\_gpu\_nxp\_pxp\_osa.c
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pxp\_interrupt\_init()}}: Initialize PXP interrupt (HW setup, OS setup)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pxp\_interrupt\_deinit()}}: Deinitialize PXP interrupt (HW setup, OS setup)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pxp\_run()}}: Start PXP job. Use OS\sphinxhyphen{}specific mechanism to block drawing thread. PXP must finish drawing before
leaving this function.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Area threshold (size limit) is configurable and used to decide whether the area will be processed by PXP or not.
Areas smaller than the defined value will be processed by CPU and those bigger than the threshold will be processed by
PXP. The threshold is defined as a macro in lv\_draw\_pxp.c
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GPU\_NXP\_PXP\_SIZE\_LIMIT}}: size threshold for fill/blit (with optional transformation)

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{VGLite accelerator}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:vglite-accelerator}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extra drawing features in LVGL can be handled by the VGLite engine. The CPU is available for other operations while the
VGLite is running. An RTOS is required to block the LVGL drawing thread and switch to another task or suspend the CPU
for power savings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Supported draw callbacks are available in "src/draw/nxp/vglite/lv\_draw\_vglite.c":

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
    \PYG{n}{vglite\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{init\PYGZus{}buf} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}vglite\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}buf}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{vglite\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}line} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}vglite\PYGZus{}line}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{vglite\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}arc} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}vglite\PYGZus{}arc}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{vglite\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}rect} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}vglite\PYGZus{}rect}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{vglite\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}decoded} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}vglite\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}decoded}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{vglite\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{blend} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}vglite\PYGZus{}blend}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{vglite\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{wait\PYGZus{}for\PYGZus{}finish} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}vglite\PYGZus{}wait\PYGZus{}for\PYGZus{}finish}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{vglite\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}ctx}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}draw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{buffer\PYGZus{}copy} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}vglite\PYGZus{}buffer\PYGZus{}copy}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Features supported:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{All} \PYG{n}{operations} \PYG{n}{can} \PYG{n}{be} \PYG{n}{used} \PYG{n}{in} \PYG{n}{conjunction} \PYG{n}{with} \PYG{n}{optional} \PYG{n}{transparency}\PYG{p}{.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RGB565 and ARGB8888 color formats

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Area fill with color

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
BLIT (BLock Image Transfer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Image Rotation (any degree with decimal)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Image Scale

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw rectangle background with optional radius or gradient

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Blit rectangle background image

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw rectangle border/outline with optional rounded corners

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw arc with optional rounded ending

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw line or dashed line with optional rounded ending

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Buffer copy

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Known limitations:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:id2}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Source image alignment:
The byte alignment requirement for a pixel depends on the specific pixel format. Both buffer address and buffer stride
must be aligned. As general rule, the alignment is set to 16 pixels. This makes the buffer address alignment to be
32 bytes for RGB565 and 64 bytes for ARGB8888.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For pixel engine (PE) destination, the alignment should be 64 bytes for all tiled (4x4) buffer layouts.
The pixel engine has no additional alignment requirement for linear buffer layouts (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VG\_LITE\_LINEAR}}).

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Basic configuration:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:id3}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select NXP VGLite engine in lv\_conf.h: Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_GPU\_NXP\_VG\_LITE}} to 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SDK\_OS\_FREE\_RTOS}} symbol needs to be defined so that the FreeRTOS implementation will be used

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Basic initialization:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:id4}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize VGLite before calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_init()}} by specifying the width/height of tessellation window. Value should be
a multiple of 16; minimum value is 16 pixels, maximum cannot be greater than the frame width. If less than or equal
to 0, then no tessellation buffer is created, in which case VGLite is initialized only for blitting.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
      \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}GPU\PYGZus{}NXP\PYGZus{}VG\PYGZus{}LITE}
        \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include} \PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}vg\PYGZus{}lite.h\PYGZdq{}}
      \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{endif}
      \PYG{p}{.} \PYG{p}{.} \PYG{p}{.}
      \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}GPU\PYGZus{}NXP\PYGZus{}VG\PYGZus{}LITE}
        \PYG{n}{VG\PYGZus{}LITE\PYGZus{}COND\PYGZus{}STOP}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{vg\PYGZus{}lite\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{64}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{64}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{!}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{VG\PYGZus{}LITE\PYGZus{}SUCCESS}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{VGLite init failed.}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
      \PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{endif}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Project setup:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:id5}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add VGLite related files to project:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/vglite/lv\_draw\_vglite.c{[}.h{]}: draw context callbacks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/vglite/lv\_draw\_vglite\_blend.c{[}.h{]}: fill and blit (with optional transformation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/vglite/lv\_draw\_vglite\_rect.c{[}.h{]}: draw rectangle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/vglite/lv\_draw\_vglite\_arc.c{[}.h{]}: draw arc

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/vglite/lv\_draw\_vglite\_line.c{[}.h{]}: draw line

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/vglite/lv\_vglite\_buf.c{[}.h{]}: init/get vglite buffer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
src/draw/nxp/vglite/lv\_vglite\_utils.c{[}.h{]}: function helpers

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Logging:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:id6}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GPU\_NXP\_VG\_LITE\_LOG\_ERRORS}} is enabled so that any VGLite error will be seen on SDK debug console

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GPU\_NXP\_VG\_LITE\_LOG\_TRACES}} is disabled. Enable it for tracing logs (like blit split workaround or
VGLite fallback to CPU due to any error on the driver)

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Advanced configuration:}
\label{\detokenize{get-started/platforms/nxp:id7}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Area threshold (size limit) is configurable and used to decide whether the area will be processed by VGLite or not.
Areas smaller than the defined value will be processed by CPU and those bigger than the threshold will be processed by
VGLite. The threshold is defined as a macro in lv\_draw\_vglite.c
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GPU\_NXP\_VG\_LITE\_SIZE\_LIMIT}}: size threshold for fill/blit (with optional transformation)

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}
