This is an internal mechanism and doesn't matter much as you use LVGL. However, there is one case in which you need to be aware of the implementation. If the style(s) of an object are removed by

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}remove\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}all}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
or

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}remove\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}MAIN}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
the earlier set coordinates will be removed as well.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cm}{/*The size of obj1 will be set back to the default in the end*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{200}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}  \PYG{c+cm}{/*Now obj1 has 200;100 size*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}remove\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}all}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}    \PYG{c+cm}{/*It removes the set sizes*/}


\PYG{c+cm}{/*obj2 will have 200;100 size in the end */}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}remove\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}all}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{200}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Position}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:position}}

\subsubsection{Simple way}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:simple-way}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To simply set the x and y coordinates of an object use:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}        \PYG{c+c1}{//Separate...}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}y}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}pos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} 	\PYG{c+c1}{//Or in one function}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the x and y coordinates are measured from the top left corner of the parent's content area.
For example if the parent has five pixels of padding on every side the above code will place \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{obj}} at (15, 25) because the content area starts after the padding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Percentage values are calculated from the parent's content area size.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}pct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+c1}{//x = 10 \PYGZpc{} of parent content area width}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Align}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:align}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In some cases it's convenient to change the origin of the positioning from the default top left. If the origin is changed e.g. to bottom\sphinxhyphen{}right, the (0,0) position means: align to the bottom\sphinxhyphen{}right corner.
To change the origin use:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{align}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To change the alignment and set new coordinates:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{align}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following alignment options can be used:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_TOP\_LEFT}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_TOP\_MID}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_TOP\_RIGHT}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_BOTTOM\_LEFT}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_BOTTOM\_MID}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_BOTTOM\_RIGHT}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_LEFT\_MID}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_RIGHT\_MID}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_CENTER}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It's quite common to align a child to the center of its parent, therefore a dedicated function exists:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}center}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{//Has the same effect}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}ALIGN\PYGZus{}CENTER}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the parent's size changes, the set alignment and position of the children is updated automatically.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The functions introduced above align the object to its parent. However, it's also possible to align an object to an arbitrary reference object.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}align\PYGZus{}to}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}align}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reference\PYGZus{}obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{align}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Besides the alignments options above, the following can be used to align an object outside the reference object:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_TOP\_LEFT}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_TOP\_MID}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_TOP\_RIGHT}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_BOTTOM\_LEFT}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_BOTTOM\_MID}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_BOTTOM\_RIGHT}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_LEFT\_TOP}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_LEFT\_MID}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_LEFT\_BOTTOM}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_RIGHT\_TOP}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_RIGHT\_MID}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_RIGHT\_BOTTOM}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example to align a label above a button and center the label horizontally:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}align\PYGZus{}to}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}ALIGN\PYGZus{}OUT\PYGZus{}TOP\PYGZus{}MID}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, unlike with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_align()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_align\_to()}} can not realign the object if its coordinates or the reference object's coordinates change.


\subsection{Size}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:size}}

\subsubsection{Simple way}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:id1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The width and the height of an object can be set easily as well:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{200}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}       \PYG{c+c1}{//Separate...}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{200}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} 	\PYG{c+c1}{//Or in one function}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Percentage values are calculated based on the parent's content area size. For example to set the object's height to the screen height:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}pct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The size settings support a special value: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}}. It means the object's size in the respective direction will be set to the size of its children.
Note that only children on the right and bottom sides will be considered and children on the top and left remain cropped. This limitation makes the behavior more predictable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Objects with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_HIDDEN}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_FLOATING}} will be ignored by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} calculation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The above functions set the size of an object's bounding box but the size of the content area can be set as well. This means an object's bounding box will be enlarged with the addition of padding.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}content\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+c1}{//The actual width: padding left + 50 + padding right}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}content\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{30}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+c1}{//The actual width: padding top + 30 + padding bottom}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The size of the bounding box and the content area can be retrieved with the following functions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}coord\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{w} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}coord\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{h} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}coord\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{content\PYGZus{}w} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}content\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}coord\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{content\PYGZus{}h} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}content\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Using styles}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:using-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Under the hood the position, size and alignment properties are style properties.
The above described "simple functions" hide the style related code for the sake of simplicity and set the position, size, and alignment properties in the local styles of the object.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, using styles to set the coordinates has some great advantages:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It makes it easy to set the width/height/etc. for several objects together. E.g. make all the sliders 100x10 pixels sized.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It also makes possible to modify the values in one place.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The values can be partially overwritten by other styles. For example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style\_btn}} makes the object \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{100x50}} by default but adding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style\_full\_width}} overwrites only the width of the object.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The object can have different position or size depending on state. E.g. 100 px wide in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}} but 120 px in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_PRESSED}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Style transitions can be used to make the coordinate changes smooth.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are some examples to set an object's size using a style:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{btn} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}MAIN}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As you will see below there are some other great features of size and position setting.
However, to keep the LVGL API lean, only the most common coordinate setting features have a "simple" version and the more complex features can be used via styles.


\subsection{Translation}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:translation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Let's say the there are 3 buttons next to each other. Their position is set as described above.
Now you want to move a button up a little when it's pressed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One way to achieve this is by setting a new Y coordinate for the pressed state:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}y}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}y}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{80}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This works, but it's not really flexible because the pressed coordinate is hard\sphinxhyphen{}coded. If the buttons are not at y=100, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style\_pressed}} won't work as expected. Translations can be used to solve this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}y}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}translate\PYGZus{}y}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}normal}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Translation is applied from the current position of the object.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Percentage values can be used in translations as well. The percentage is relative to the size of the object (and not to the size of the parent). For example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_pct(50)}} will move the object with half of its width/height.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The translation is applied after the layouts are calculated. Therefore, even laid out objects' position can be translated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The translation actually moves the object. That means it makes the scrollbars and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} sized objects react to the position change.


\subsection{Transformation}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:transformation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarly to position, an object's size can be changed relative to the current size as well.
The transformed width and height are added on both sides of the object. This means a 10 px transformed width makes the object 2x10 pixels wider.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike position translation, the size transformation doesn't make the object "really" larger. In other words scrollbars, layouts, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} will not react to the transformed size.
Hence, size transformation is "only" a visual effect.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This code enlarges a button when it's pressed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}transform\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}transform\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}pressed}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Min and Max size}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:min-and-max-size}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarly to CSS, LVGL also supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\sphinxhyphen{}width}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\sphinxhyphen{}width}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\sphinxhyphen{}height}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\sphinxhyphen{}height}}. These are limits preventing an object's size from becoming smaller/larger than these values.
They are especially useful if the size is set by percentage or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}y}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{200}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}pct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+c1}{//Limit the  height to 200 px}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Percentage values can be used as well which are relative to the size of the parent's content area.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}y}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}pct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}pct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+c1}{//Limit the height to half parent height}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Layout}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:layout}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:id2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layouts can update the position and size of an object's children. They can be used to automatically arrange the children into a line or column, or in much more complicated forms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The position and size set by the layout overwrites the "normal" x, y, width, and height settings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There is only one function that is the same for every layout: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_layout(obj, <LAYOUT\_NAME>)}} sets the layout on an object.
For further settings of the parent and children see the documentation of the given layout.


\subsubsection{Built\sphinxhyphen{}in layout}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:built-in-layout}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL comes with two very powerful layouts:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flexbox

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grid

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both are heavily inspired by the CSS layouts with the same name.


\subsubsection{Flags}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:flags}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are some flags that can be used on objects to affect how they behave with layouts:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_HIDDEN}} Hidden objects are ignored in layout calculations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_IGNORE\_LAYOUT}} The object is simply ignored by the layouts. Its coordinates can be set as usual.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_FLOATING}} Same as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_IGNORE\_LAYOUT}} but the object with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_FLOATING}} will be ignored in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} calculations.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These flags can be added/removed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add/clear\_flag(obj, FLAG);}}


\subsubsection{Adding new layouts}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:adding-new-layouts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL can be freely extended by a custom layout like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{uint32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{MY\PYGZus{}LAYOUT}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{n}{MY\PYGZus{}LAYOUT} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}layout\PYGZus{}register}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}layout\PYGZus{}update}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{user\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}layout\PYGZus{}update}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{user\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
	\PYG{c+cm}{/*Will be called automatically if it\PYGZsq{}s required to reposition/resize the children of \PYGZdq{}obj\PYGZdq{} */}	
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Custom style properties can be added which can be retrieved and used in the update callback. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{uint32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{MY\PYGZus{}PROP}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}MY\PYGZus{}PROP} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}register\PYGZus{}prop}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kr}{inline} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}prop}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k+kt}{uint32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{value}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}value\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{v} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{num} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int32\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{value}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}prop}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}MY\PYGZus{}PROP}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{v}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{overview/coords:examples}}
\sphinxstepscope


\section{Styles}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:styles}}\label{\detokenize{overview/style::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Styles} are used to set the appearance of objects. Styles in lvgl are heavily inspired by CSS. The concept in a nutshell is as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A style is an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_t}} variable which can hold properties like border width, text color and so on. It's similar to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{class}} in CSS.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles can be assigned to objects to change their appearance. Upon assignment, the target part (\sphinxstyleemphasis{pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}element} in CSS) and target state (\sphinxstyleemphasis{pseudo class}) can be specified.
For example one can add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style\_blue}} to the knob of a slider when it's in pressed state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The same style can be used by any number of objects.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles can be cascaded which means multiple styles may be assigned to an object and each style can have different properties.
Therefore, not all properties have to be specified in a style. LVGL will search for a property until a style defines it or use a default if it's not specified by any of the styles.
For example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style\_btn}} can result in a default gray button and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style\_btn\_red}} can add only a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{background\sphinxhyphen{}color=red}} to overwrite the background color.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The most recently added style has higher precedence. This means if a property is specified in two styles the newest style in the object will be used.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Some properties (e.g. text color) can be inherited from a parent(s) if it's not specified in an object.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Objects can also have local styles with higher precedence than "normal" styles.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike CSS (where pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}classes describe different states, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:focus}}), in LVGL a property is assigned to a given state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Transitions can be applied when the object changes state.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{States}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:states}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The objects can be in the combination of the following states:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}} (0x0000) Normal, released state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_CHECKED}} (0x0001) Toggled or checked state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUSED}} (0x0002) Focused via keypad or encoder or clicked via touchpad/mouse

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUS\_KEY}} (0x0004) Focused via keypad or encoder but not via touchpad/mouse

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_EDITED}} (0x0008) Edit by an encoder

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_HOVERED}} (0x0010) Hovered by mouse (not supported now)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_PRESSED}} (0x0020) Being pressed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_SCROLLED}} (0x0040) Being scrolled

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DISABLED}} (0x0080) Disabled state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_USER\_1}} (0x1000) Custom state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_USER\_2}} (0x2000) Custom state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_USER\_3}} (0x4000) Custom state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_USER\_4}} (0x8000) Custom state

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An object can be in a combination of states such as being focused and pressed at the same time. This is represented as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUSED | LV\_STATE\_PRESSED}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A style can be added to any state or state combination.
For example, setting a different background color for the default and pressed states.
If a property is not defined in a state the best matching state's property will be used. Typically this means the property with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}} is used.˛
If the property is not set even for the default state the default value will be used. (See later)

\sphinxAtStartPar
But what does the "best matching state's property" really mean?
States have a precedence which is shown by their value (see in the above list). A higher value means higher precedence.
To determine which state's property to use let's take an example. Imagine the background color is defined like this:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}}: white

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_PRESSED}}: gray

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUSED}}: red

\end{itemize}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initially the object is in the default state, so it's a simple case: the property is perfectly defined in the object's current state as white.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the object is pressed there are 2 related properties: default with white (default is related to every state) and pressed with gray.
The pressed state has 0x0020 precedence which is higher than the default state's 0x0000 precedence, so gray color will be used.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the object is focused the same thing happens as in pressed state and red color will be used. (Focused state has higher precedence than default state).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the object is focused and pressed both gray and red would work, but the pressed state has higher precedence than focused so gray color will be used.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It's possible to set e.g. rose color for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_PRESSED | LV\_STATE\_FOCUSED}}.
In this case, this combined state has 0x0020 + 0x0002 = 0x0022 precedence, which is higher than the pressed state's precedence so rose color would be used.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the object is in the checked state there is no property to set the background color for this state. So for lack of a better option, the object remains white from the default state's property.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some practical notes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The precedence (value) of states is quite intuitive, and it's something the user would expect naturally. E.g. if an object is focused the user will still want to see if it's pressed, therefore the pressed state has a higher precedence.
If the focused state had a higher precedence it would overwrite the pressed color.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want to set a property for all states (e.g. red background color) just set it for the default state. If the object can't find a property for its current state it will fall back to the default state's property.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use ORed states to describe the properties for complex cases. (E.g. pressed + checked + focused)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It might be a good idea to use different style elements for different states.
For example, finding background colors for released, pressed, checked + pressed, focused, focused + pressed, focused + pressed + checked, etc. states is quite difficult.
Instead, for example, use the background color for pressed and checked states and indicate the focused state with a different border color.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Cascading styles}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:cascading-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It's not required to set all the properties in one style. It's possible to add more styles to an object and have the latter added style modify or extend appearance.
For example, create a general gray button style and create a new one for red buttons where only the new background color is set.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is much like in CSS when used classes are listed like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<div class=".btn .btn\sphinxhyphen{}red">}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles added later have precedence over ones set earlier. So in the gray/red button example above, the normal button style should be added first and the red style second.
However, the precedence of the states are still taken into account.
So let's examine the following case:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the basic button style defines dark\sphinxhyphen{}gray color for the default state and light\sphinxhyphen{}gray color for the pressed state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the red button style defines the background color as red only in the default state

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In this case, when the button is released (it's in default state) it will be red because a perfect match is found in the most recently added style (red).
When the button is pressed the light\sphinxhyphen{}gray color is a better match because it describes the current state perfectly, so the button will be light\sphinxhyphen{}gray.


\subsection{Inheritance}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:inheritance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Some properties (typically those related to text) can be inherited from the parent object's styles.
Inheritance is applied only if the given property is not set in the object's styles (even in default state).
In this case, if the property is inheritable, the property's value will be searched in the parents until an object specifies a value for the property. The parents will use their own state to determine the value.
So if a button is pressed, and the text color comes from here, the pressed text color will be used.


\subsection{Forced value inheritance/default value}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:forced-value-inheritance-default-value}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sometimes you may want to force a child object to use the parent's value for a given style property. To do this you can use
one of the following (depending on what type of style you're using):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cm}{/* regular style */}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}prop\PYGZus{}meta}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}TEXT\PYGZus{}COLOR}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}PROP\PYGZus{}META\PYGZus{}INHERIT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+cm}{/* local style */}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}local\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}prop\PYGZus{}meta}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{child}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}TEXT\PYGZus{}COLOR}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}PROP\PYGZus{}META\PYGZus{}INHERIT}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}MAIN}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This acts like a value has been set on the style, so setting the value of the property afterwards will remove the flag.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You may also want to force the default value of a property to be used, without needing to hardcode it in your application.
To do this you can use the same API but with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STYLE\_PROP\_META\_INITIAL}} instead. In future versions of LVGL, this
will use the value based upon the current theme, but for now it just selects the internal default regardless of theme.


\subsection{Parts}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:parts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Objects can be composed of \sphinxstyleemphasis{parts} which may each have their own styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following predefined parts exist in LVGL:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} A background like rectangle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}}  The scrollbar(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} Indicator, e.g. for slider, bar, switch, or the tick box of the checkbox

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_KNOB}} Like a handle to grab to adjust a value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SELECTED}} Indicate the currently selected option or section

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}} Used if the widget has multiple similar elements (e.g. table cells)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_TICKS}} Ticks on scales e.g. for a chart or meter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_CURSOR}} Mark a specific place e.g. text area's or chart's cursor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_CUSTOM\_FIRST}} Custom part identifiers can be added starting from here.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/slider::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Slider}}}} has three parts:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Background

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Indicator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Knob

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This means all three parts of the slider can have their own styles. See later how to add styles to objects and parts.


\subsection{Initialize styles and set/get properties}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:initialize-styles-and-set-get-properties}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles are stored in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_t}} variables. Style variables should be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{static}}, global or dynamically allocated.
In other words they cannot be local variables in functions which are destroyed when the function exits.
Before using a style it should be initialized with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_init(\&my\_style)}}.
After initializing a style, properties can be added or changed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Property set functions looks like this: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_set\_<property\_name>(\&style, <value>);}} For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hex}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mh}{0x115588}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}opa}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}OPA\PYGZus{}50}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}border\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}border\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}black}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}plaette\PYGZus{}main}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PALETTE\PYGZus{}RED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}opa}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}OPA\PYGZus{}COVER}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To remove a property use:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}remove\PYGZus{}prop}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}BG\PYGZus{}COLOR}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To get a property's value from a style:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}value\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{v}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}res\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{res} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}prop}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}BG\PYGZus{}COLOR}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{v}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{res} \PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}RES\PYGZus{}OK}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}	\PYG{c+cm}{/*Found*/}
	\PYG{n}{do\PYGZus{}something}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{v}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{color}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_value\_t}} has 3 fields:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{num}} for integer, boolean and opacity properties

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color}} for color properties

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptr}} for pointer properties

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To reset a style (free all its data) use:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}reset}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Styles can be built as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} too to save RAM:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{const} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}const\PYGZus{}prop\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style1\PYGZus{}props}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
   \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}CONST\PYGZus{}WIDTH}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
   \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}CONST\PYGZus{}HEIGHT}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
   \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}PROP\PYGZus{}INV}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}CONST\PYGZus{}INIT}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{style1\PYGZus{}props}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Later \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} style can be used like any other style but (obviously) new properties can not be added.


\subsection{Add and remove styles to a widget}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:add-and-remove-styles-to-a-widget}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A style on its own is not that useful. It must be assigned to an object to take effect.


\subsubsection{Add styles}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:add-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To add a style to an object use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_style(obj, \&style, <selector>)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<selector>}} is an OR\sphinxhyphen{}ed value of parts and state to which the style should be added. Some examples:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN | LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_PRESSED}}: The main part in pressed state. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} can be omitted

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}}: The scrollbar part in the default state. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}} can be omitted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR | LV\_STATE\_SCROLLED}}: The scrollbar part when the object is being scrolled

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} Same as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN | LV\_STATE\_DEFAULT}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR | LV\_STATE\_PRESSED | LV\_STATE\_CHECKED}} The indicator part when the object is pressed and checked at the same time.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_style}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}      				  \PYG{c+cm}{/*Default button style*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{btn\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}  \PYG{c+cm}{/*Overwrite only some colors to red when pressed*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Remove styles}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:remove-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To remove all styles from an object use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_remove\_style\_all(obj)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To remove specific styles use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_remove\_style(obj, style, selector)}}. This function will remove \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style}} only if the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{selector}} matches with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{selector}} used in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_style}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style}} can be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} to check only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{selector}} and remove all matching styles. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{selector}} can use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_ANY}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ANY}} values to remove the style from any state or part.


\subsubsection{Report style changes}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:report-style-changes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If a style which is already assigned to an object changes (i.e. a property is added or changed), the objects using that style should be notified. There are 3 options to do this:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you know that the changed properties can be applied by a simple redraw (e.g. color or opacity changes) just call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_invalidate(obj)}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_invalidate(lv\_scr\_act())}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If more complex style properties were changed or added, and you know which object(s) are affected by that style call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_refresh\_style(obj, part, property)}}.
To refresh all parts and properties use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_refresh\_style(obj, LV\_PART\_ANY, LV\_STYLE\_PROP\_ANY)}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To make LVGL check all objects to see if they use a style and refresh them when needed, call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_report\_style\_change(\&style)}}. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} all objects will be notified about a style change.

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Get a property's value on an object}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:get-a-property-s-value-on-an-object}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To get a final value of property \sphinxhyphen{} considering cascading, inheritance, local styles and transitions (see below) \sphinxhyphen{} property get functions like this can be used:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_style\_<property\_name>(obj, <part>)}}.
These functions use the object's current state and if no better candidate exists they return a default value.  
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{color} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}MAIN}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Local styles}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:local-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to "normal" styles, objects can also store local styles. This concept is similar to inline styles in CSS (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<div style="color:red">}}) with some modification.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Local styles are like normal styles, but they can't be shared among other objects. If used, local styles are allocated automatically, and freed when the object is deleted.
They are useful to add local customization to an object.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike in CSS, LVGL local styles can be assigned to states (\sphinxstyleemphasis{pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}classes}) and parts (\sphinxstyleemphasis{pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}elements}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set a local property use functions like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_style\_<property\_name>(obj, <value>, <selector>);}}  
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{slider}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}INDICATOR} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}FOCUSED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Properties}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:properties}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the full list of style properties click {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/style-props::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{here}}}}.


\subsubsection{Typical background properties}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:typical-background-properties}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the documentation of the widgets you will see sentences like "The widget uses the typical background properties". These "typical background properties" are the ones related to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Background

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Border

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Outline

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shadow

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Padding

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Width and height transformation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
X and Y translation

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Transitions}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:transitions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, when an object changes state (e.g. it's pressed) the new properties from the new state are set immediately. However, with transitions it's possible to play an animation on state change.
For example, on pressing a button its background color can be animated to the pressed color over 300 ms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameters of the transitions are stored in the styles. It's possible to set
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the time of the transition

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the delay before starting the transition

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the animation path (also known as the timing or easing function)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the properties to animate

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The transition properties can be defined for each state. For example, setting a 500 ms transition time in the default state means that when the object goes to the default state a 500 ms transition time is applied.
Setting a 100 ms transition time in the pressed state causes a 100 ms transition when going to the pressed state.
This example configuration results in going to the pressed state quickly and then going back to default slowly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To describe a transition an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_transition\_dsc\_t}} variable needs to be initialized and added to a style:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cm}{/*Only its pointer is saved so must static, global or dynamically allocated */}
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k}{const} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}prop\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{trans\PYGZus{}props}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
											\PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}BG\PYGZus{}OPA}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STYLE\PYGZus{}BG\PYGZus{}COLOR}\PYG{p}{,}
											\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{c+cm}{/*End marker*/}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}transition\PYGZus{}dsc\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{trans1}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}transition\PYGZus{}dsc\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{trans1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{trans\PYGZus{}props}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}anim\PYGZus{}path\PYGZus{}ease\PYGZus{}out}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{duration\PYGZus{}ms}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{delay\PYGZus{}ms}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}transition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{trans1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Opacity, Blend modes and Transformations}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:opacity-blend-modes-and-transformations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opa}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blend\_mode}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform\_angle}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform\_zoom}} properties are set to their non\sphinxhyphen{}default value LVGL creates a snapshot about the widget and all its children in order to blend the whole widget with the set opacity, blend mode and transformation properties.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These properties have this effect only on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MAIN}} part of the widget.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The created snapshot is called "intermediate layer" or simply "layer". If only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opa}} and/or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blend\_mode}} is set to a non\sphinxhyphen{}default value LVGL can build the layer from smaller chunks. The size of these chunks can be configured by the following properties in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LAYER\_SIMPLE\_BUF\_SIZE}}: {[}bytes{]} the optimal target buffer size. LVGL will try to allocate this size of memory.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LAYER\_SIMPLE\_FALLBACK\_BUF\_SIZE}}: {[}bytes{]}  used if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LAYER\_SIMPLE\_BUF\_SIZE}} couldn't be allocated.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If transformation properties were also used the layer can not be rendered in chunks, but one larger memory needs to be allocated. The required memory depends on the angle, zoom and pivot parameters, and the size of the area to redraw, but it's never larger than the size of the widget (including the extra draw size used for shadow, outline, etc).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the widget can fully cover the area to redraw, LVGL creates an RGB layer (which is faster to render and uses less memory). If the opposite case ARGB rendering needs to be used. A widget might not cover its area if it has radius, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bg\_opa != 255}}, has shadow, outline, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The click area of the widget is also transformed accordingly.

\subsection{Themes}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:themes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Themes are a collection of styles. If there is an active theme LVGL applies it on every created widget.
This will give a default appearance to the UI which can then be modified by adding further styles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every display can have a different theme. For example, you could have a colorful theme on a TFT and monochrome theme on a secondary monochrome display.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set a theme for a display, two steps are required:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize a theme

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assign the initialized theme to a display.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Theme initialization functions can have different prototypes. This example shows how to set the "default" theme:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}theme\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{th} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}theme\PYGZus{}default\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{display}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+cm}{/*Use the DPI, size, etc from this display*/}
                                        \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}COLOR\PYGZus{}PALETTE\PYGZus{}BLUE}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}COLOR\PYGZus{}PALETTE\PYGZus{}CYAN}\PYG{p}{,}   \PYG{c+cm}{/*Primary and secondary palette*/}
                                        \PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Light or dark mode*/}
                                        \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}font\PYGZus{}montserrat\PYGZus{}10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}font\PYGZus{}montserrat\PYGZus{}14}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}font\PYGZus{}montserrat\PYGZus{}18}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*Small, normal, large fonts*/}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}disp\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}theme}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{display}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{th}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*Assign the theme to the display*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The included themes are enabled in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}. If the default theme is enabled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_THEME\_DEFAULT 1}} LVGL automatically initializes and sets it when a display is created.


\subsubsection{Extending themes}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style:extending-themes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Built\sphinxhyphen{}in themes can be extended.
If a custom theme is created, a parent theme can be selected. The parent theme's styles will be added before the custom theme's styles.
Any number of themes can be chained this way. E.g. default theme \sphinxhyphen{}> custom theme \sphinxhyphen{}> dark theme.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_theme\_set\_parent(new\_theme, base\_theme)}} extends the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base\_theme}} with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new\_theme}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There is an example for it below.

\section{Style properties}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:style-properties}}\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props::doc}}

\subsection{Size and position}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:size-and-position}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Properties related to size, position, alignment and layout of the objects.


\subsubsection{width}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:width}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the width of object. Pixel, percentage and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the width of the parent's content area.




\subsubsection{min\_width}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:min-width}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets a minimal width. Pixel and percentage values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the width of the parent's content area.




\subsubsection{max\_width}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:max-width}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets a maximal width. Pixel and percentage values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the width of the parent's content area.




\subsubsection{height}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:height}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the height of object. Pixel, percentage and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} can be used. Percentage values are relative to the height of the parent's content area.




\subsubsection{min\_height}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:min-height}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets a minimal height. Pixel and percentage values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the width of the parent's content area.




\subsubsection{max\_height}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:max-height}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets a maximal height. Pixel and percentage values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the height of the parent's content area.




\subsubsection{x}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:x}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the X coordinate of the object considering the set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align}}. Pixel and percentage values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the width of the parent's content area.




\subsubsection{y}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:y}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the Y coordinate of the object considering the set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align}}. Pixel and percentage values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the height of the parent's content area.




\subsubsection{align}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:align}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the alignment which tells from which point of the parent the X and Y coordinates should be interpreted. The possible values are: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_DEFAULT}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_TOP\_LEFT/MID/RIGHT}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_BOTTOM\_LEFT/MID/RIGHT}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_LEFT/RIGHT\_MID}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_CENTER}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_DEFAULT}} means \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_TOP\_LEFT}} with LTR base direction and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ALIGN\_TOP\_RIGHT}} with RTL base direction.




\subsubsection{transform\_width}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:transform-width}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Make the object wider on both sides with this value. Pixel and percentage (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_pct(x)}}) values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the object's width.




\subsubsection{transform\_height}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:transform-height}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Make the object higher on both sides with this value. Pixel and percentage (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_pct(x)}}) values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the object's height.




\subsubsection{translate\_x}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:translate-x}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Move the object with this value in X direction. Applied after layouts, aligns and other positioning. Pixel and percentage (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_pct(x)}}) values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the object's width.




\subsubsection{translate\_y}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:translate-y}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Move the object with this value in Y direction. Applied after layouts, aligns and other positioning. Pixel and percentage (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_pct(x)}}) values can be used. Percentage values are relative to the object's height.




\subsubsection{transform\_zoom}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:transform-zoom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Zoom an objects. The value 256 (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_ZOOM\_NONE}}) means normal size, 128 half size, 512 double size, and so on




\subsubsection{transform\_angle}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:transform-angle}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rotate an objects. The value is interpreted in 0.1 degree units. E.g. 450 means 45 deg.




\subsubsection{transform\_pivot\_x}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:transform-pivot-x}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the pivot point's X coordinate for transformations. Relative to the object's top left corner'




\subsubsection{transform\_pivot\_y}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:transform-pivot-y}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the pivot point's Y coordinate for transformations. Relative to the object's top left corner'




\subsection{Padding}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:padding}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Properties to describe spacing between the parent's sides and the children and among the children. Very similar to the padding properties in HTML.


\subsubsection{pad\_top}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:pad-top}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the padding on the top. It makes the content area smaller in this direction.




\subsubsection{pad\_bottom}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:pad-bottom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the padding on the bottom. It makes the content area smaller in this direction.




\subsubsection{pad\_left}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:pad-left}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the padding on the left. It makes the content area smaller in this direction.




\subsubsection{pad\_right}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:pad-right}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the padding on the right. It makes the content area smaller in this direction.




\subsubsection{pad\_row}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:pad-row}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the padding between the rows. Used by the layouts.




\subsubsection{pad\_column}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:pad-column}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets the padding between the columns. Used by the layouts.




\subsection{Background}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:background}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Properties to describe the background color and image of the objects.


\subsubsection{bg\_color}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-color}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the background color of the object.




\subsubsection{bg\_opa}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-opa}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the opacity of the background. Value 0, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_0}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_TRANSP}} means fully transparent, 255, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_100}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_COVER}} means fully covering, other values or LV\_OPA\_10, LV\_OPA\_20, etc means semi transparency.




\subsubsection{bg\_grad\_color}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-grad-color}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the gradient color of the background. Used only if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{grad\_dir}} is not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRAD\_DIR\_NONE}}




\subsubsection{bg\_grad\_dir}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-grad-dir}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the direction of the gradient of the background. The possible values are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRAD\_DIR\_NONE/HOR/VER}}.




\subsubsection{bg\_main\_stop}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-main-stop}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the point from which the background color should start for gradients. 0 means to top/left side, 255 the bottom/right side, 128 the center, and so on




\subsubsection{bg\_grad\_stop}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-grad-stop}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the point from which the background's gradient color should start. 0 means to top/left side, 255 the bottom/right side, 128 the center, and so on




\subsubsection{bg\_grad}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-grad}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the gradient definition. The pointed instance must exist while the object is alive. NULL to disable. It wraps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BG\_GRAD\_COLOR}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BG\_GRAD\_DIR}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BG\_MAIN\_STOP}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BG\_GRAD\_STOP}} into one descriptor and allows creating gradients with more colors too.




\subsubsection{bg\_dither\_mode}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-dither-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the dithering mode of the gradient of the background. The possible values are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DITHER\_NONE/ORDERED/ERR\_DIFF}}.




\subsubsection{bg\_img\_src}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-img-src}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set a background image. Can be a pointer to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_dsc\_t}}, a path to a file or an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_...}}




\subsubsection{bg\_img\_opa}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-img-opa}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the opacity of the background image. Value 0, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_0}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_TRANSP}} means fully transparent, 255, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_100}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_COVER}} means fully covering, other values or LV\_OPA\_10, LV\_OPA\_20, etc means semi transparency.




\subsubsection{bg\_img\_recolor}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-img-recolor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set a color to mix to the background image.




\subsubsection{bg\_img\_recolor\_opa}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-img-recolor-opa}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the intensity of background image recoloring. Value 0, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_0}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_TRANSP}} means no mixing, 255, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_100}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_COVER}} means full recoloring, other values or LV\_OPA\_10, LV\_OPA\_20, etc are interpreted proportionally.




\subsubsection{bg\_img\_tiled}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:bg-img-tiled}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If enabled the background image will be tiled. The possible values are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\subsubsection{border\_width}

The animation template for the object's animation. Should be a pointer to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_anim\_t}}. The animation parameters are widget specific, e.g. animation time could be the E.g. blink time of the cursor on the text area or scroll time of a roller. See the widgets' documentation to learn more.




\subsubsection{anim\_time}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The animation time in milliseconds. Its meaning is widget specific. E.g. blink time of the cursor on the text area or scroll time of a roller. See the widgets' documentation to learn more.




\subsubsection{anim\_speed}
\label{\detokenize{overview/style-props:anim-speed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The animation speed in pixel/sec. Its meaning is widget specific. E.g. scroll speed of label. See the widgets' documentation to learn more.

An initialized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_transition\_dsc\_t}} to describe a transition.

\section{Scroll}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:scroll}}\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll::doc}}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In LVGL scrolling works very intuitively: if an object is outside its parent content area (the size without padding), the parent becomes scrollable and scrollbar(s) will appear. That's it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any object can be scrollable including \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_t}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btn}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter}}, etc

\sphinxAtStartPar
The object can either be scrolled horizontally or vertically in one stroke; diagonal scrolling is not possible.


\subsubsection{Scrollbar}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:scrollbar}}

\paragraph{Mode}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Scrollbars are displayed according to a configured \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}}. The following \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}}s exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SCROLLBAR\_MODE\_OFF}}  Never show the scrollbars

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SCROLLBAR\_MODE\_ON}}  Always show the scrollbars

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SCROLLBAR\_MODE\_ACTIVE}} Show scroll bars while an object is being scrolled

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SCROLLBAR\_MODE\_AUTO}}  Show scroll bars when the content is large enough to be scrolled

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_scrollbar\_mode(obj, LV\_SCROLLBAR\_MODE\_...)}} sets the scrollbar mode on an object.


\paragraph{Styling}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:styling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The scrollbars have their own dedicated part, called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}}. For example a scrollbar can turn to red like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}red}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}SCROLLBAR}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An object goes to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_SCROLLED}} state while it's being scrolled. This allows adding different styles to the scrollbar or the object itself when scrolled.
This code makes the scrollbar blue when the object is scrolled:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}blue}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}init}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}blue}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}bg\PYGZus{}color}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}blue}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}blue}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style\PYGZus{}blue}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}SCROLLED} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}SCROLLBAR}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the base direction of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}} is RTL (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BASE\_DIR\_RTL}}) the vertical scrollbar will be placed on the left.
Note that, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base\_dir}} style property is inherited. Therefore, it can be set directly on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}} part of an object
or on the object's or any parent's main part to make a scrollbar inherit the base direction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_left/right/top/bottom}} sets the spacing around the scrollbars and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} sets the scrollbar's width.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following events are related to scrolling:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCROLL\_BEGIN}} Scrolling begins. The event parameter is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} or an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_anim\_t *}} with a scroll animation descriptor that can be modified if required.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCROLL\_END}} Scrolling ends.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCROLL}} Scroll happened. Triggered on every position change.
Scroll events

\end{itemize}
