\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:basic-example}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
TODO


\subsection{Features of scrolling}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:features-of-scrolling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Besides, managing "normal" scrolling there are many interesting and useful additional features.


\subsubsection{Scrollable}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:scrollable}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It's possible to make an object non\sphinxhyphen{}scrollable with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_clear\_flag(obj, LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLLABLE)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}scrollable objects can still propagate the scrolling (chain) to their parents.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The direction in which scrolling happens can be controlled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_scroll\_dir(obj, LV\_DIR\_...)}}.
The following values are possible for the direction:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_TOP}} only scroll up

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_LEFT}} only scroll left

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_BOTTOM}} only scroll down

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_RIGHT}} only scroll right

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_HOR}} only scroll horizontally

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_VER}} only scroll vertically

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_ALL}} scroll any directions

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
OR\sphinxhyphen{}ed values are also possible. E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_TOP | LV\_DIR\_LEFT}}.


\subsubsection{Scroll chain}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:scroll-chain}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If an object can't be scrolled further (e.g. its content has reached the bottom\sphinxhyphen{}most position) additional scrolling is propagated to its parent. If the parent can be scrolled in that direction than it will be scrolled instead.
It continues propagating to the grandparent and grand\sphinxhyphen{}grandparents as well.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The propagation on scrolling is called "scroll chaining" and it can be enabled/disabled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_CHAIN\_HOR/VER}} flag.
If chaining is disabled the propagation stops on the object and the parent(s) won't be scrolled.


\subsubsection{Scroll momentum}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:scroll-momentum}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the user scrolls an object and releases it, LVGL can emulate inertial momentum for the scrolling. It's like the object was thrown and scrolling slows down smoothly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scroll momentum can be enabled/disabled with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_MOMENTUM}} flag.


\subsubsection{Elastic scroll}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:elastic-scroll}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normally an object can't be scrolled past the extremeties of its content. That is the top side of the content can't be below the top side of the object.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_ELASTIC}} a fancy effect is added when the user "over\sphinxhyphen{}scrolls" the content. The scrolling slows down, and the content can be scrolled inside the object.
When the object is released the content scrolled in it will be animated back to the valid position.


\subsubsection{Snapping}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:snapping}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The children of an object can be snapped according to specific rules when scrolling ends. Children can be made snappable individually with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SNAPPABLE}} flag.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An object can align snapped children in four ways:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SCROLL\_SNAP\_NONE}} Snapping is disabled. (default)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SCROLL\_SNAP\_START}} Align the children to the left/top side of a scrolled object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SCROLL\_SNAP\_END}} Align the children to the right/bottom side of a scrolled object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SCROLL\_SNAP\_CENTER}} Align the children to the center of a scrolled object

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Snap alignment is set with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_scroll\_snap\_x/y(obj, LV\_SCROLL\_SNAP\_...)}}:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Under the hood the following happens:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
User scrolls an object and releases the screen

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL calculates where the scroll would end considering scroll momentum

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL finds the nearest scroll point

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL scrolls to the snap point with an animation

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Scroll one}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:scroll-one}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The "scroll one" feature tells LVGL to allow scrolling only one snappable child at a time.
This requires making the children snappable and setting a scroll snap alignment different from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SCROLL\_SNAP\_NONE}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This feature can be enabled by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_ONE}} flag.


\subsubsection{Scroll on focus}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:scroll-on-focus}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Imagine that there a lot of objects in a group that are on a scrollable object. Pressing the "Tab" button focuses the next object but it might be outside the visible area of the scrollable object.
If the "scroll on focus" feature is enabled LVGL will automatically scroll objects to bring their children into view.
The scrolling happens recursively therefore even nested scrollable objects are handled properly.
The object will be scrolled into view even if it's on a different page of a tabview.


\subsection{Scroll manually}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:scroll-manually}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following API functions allow manual scrolling of objects:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_scroll\_by(obj, x, y, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}} scroll by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}} values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_scroll\_to(obj, x, y, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}} scroll to bring the given coordinate to the top left corner

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_scroll\_to\_x(obj, x, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}} scroll to bring the given coordinate to the left side

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_scroll\_to\_y(obj, y, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}} scroll to bring the given coordinate to the top side

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
From time to time you may need to retrieve the scroll position of an element, either to restore it later, or to display dynamically some elements according to the current scroll.
Here is an example to see how to combine scroll event and store the scroll top position.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{int} \PYG{n}{scroll\PYGZus{}value} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{store\PYGZus{}scroll\PYGZus{}value\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
  \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{screen} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}target}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
  \PYG{n}{scroll\PYGZus{}value} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}scroll\PYGZus{}top}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{screen}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
  \PYG{n}{printf}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZpc{}d pixels are scrolled out on the top}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{scroll\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{container} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{container}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{store\PYGZus{}scroll\PYGZus{}value\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}SCROLL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Scrool coordinates can be retrieve from differents axes with these functions:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_scroll\_x(obj)}} Get the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} coordinate of object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_scroll\_y(obj)}} Get the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}} coordinate of object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_scroll\_top(obj)}} Get the scroll coordinate from the top

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_scroll\_bottom(obj)}} Get the scroll coordinate from the bottom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_scroll\_left(obj)}} Get the scroll coordinate from the left

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_scroll\_right(obj)}} Get the scroll coordinate from the right

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Self size}
\label{\detokenize{overview/scroll:self-size}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self size is a property of an object. Normally, the user shouldn't use this parameter but if a custom widget is created it might be useful.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In short, self size establishes the size of an object's content. To understand it better take the example of a table.
Let's say it has 10 rows each with 50 px height. So the total height of the content is 500 px. In other words the "self height" is 500 px.
If the user sets only 200 px height for the table LVGL will see that the self size is larger and make the table scrollable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This means not only the children can make an object scrollable but a larger self size will too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL uses the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_GET\_SELF\_SIZE}} event to get the self size of an object. Here is an example to see how to handle the event:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{event\PYGZus{}code} \PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}GET\PYGZus{}SELF\PYGZus{}SIZE}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
	\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}point\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{p} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}param}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

  \PYG{c+c1}{//If x or y \PYGZlt{} 0 then it doesn\PYGZsq{}t neesd to be calculated now}
  \PYG{k}{if}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{x} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{x} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{200}\PYG{p}{;}	\PYG{c+c1}{//Set or calculate the self width}
  \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

  \PYG{k}{if}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{y} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{y} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{;}	\PYG{c+c1}{//Set or calculate the self height}
  \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

    \PYG{n}{btn} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cont}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{label}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Button }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n+nb}{str}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Update the buttons position manually for first*}
    \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{event\PYGZus{}send}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cont}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{EVENT}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{SCROLL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Be sure the fist button is in the middle}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}lv.obj.scroll\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}view(cont.get\PYGZus{}child(0), lv.ANIM.OFF)}
    \PYG{n}{cont}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}child}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{scroll\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{ANIM}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{OFF}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{sphinxuseclass}


\sphinxstepscope


\section{Layers}
\label{\detokenize{overview/layer:layers}}\label{\detokenize{overview/layer::doc}}

\subsection{Order of creation}
\label{\detokenize{overview/layer:order-of-creation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, LVGL draws new objects on top of old objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, assume we add a button to a parent object named button1 and then another button named button2. Then button1 (along with its child object(s)) will be in the background and can be covered by button2 and its children.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxincludegraphics{{layers}.png}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a screen*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{scr} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}load}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{scr}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}          \PYG{c+cm}{/*Load the screen*/}

\PYG{c+cm}{/*Create 2 buttons*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{btn1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{scr}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}         \PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a button on the screen*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}fit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}                   \PYG{c+cm}{/*Enable automatically setting the size according to content*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}pos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{60}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{40}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}              	   \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set the position of the button*/}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{btn2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{scr}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}         \PYG{c+cm}{/*Copy the first button*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}pos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{180}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{80}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}                    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set the position of the button*/}

\PYG{c+cm}{/*Add labels to the buttons*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{label1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}	\PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a label on the first button*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Button 1}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}          	\PYG{c+cm}{/*Set the text of the label*/}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{label2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}  	\PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a label on the second button*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Button 2}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}            	\PYG{c+cm}{/*Set the text of the label*/}

\PYG{c+cm}{/*Delete the second label*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}del}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Change order}
\label{\detokenize{overview/layer:change-order}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are four explicit ways to bring an object to the foreground:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_move\_foreground(obj)}} to bring an object to the foreground. Similarly, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_move\_background(obj)}} to move it to the background.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_move\_to\_index(obj, idx)}} to move an object to a given index in the order of children. (0: backgroud, child\_num \sphinxhyphen{} 1: foreground, <0: count from the top, to move forward (up): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_move\_to\_index(obj, lv\_obj\_get\_index(obj) \sphinxhyphen{} 1)}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_swap(obj1, obj2)}} to swap the relative layer position of two objects.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_parent(obj, new\_parent)}} is used, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{obj}} will be on the foreground of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new\_parent}}.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Top and sys layers}
\label{\detokenize{overview/layer:top-and-sys-layers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL uses two special layers named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_top}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_sys}}.
Both are visible and common on all screens of a display. \sphinxstylestrong{They are not, however, shared among multiple physical displays.} The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_top}} is always on top of the default screen (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_scr\_act()}}), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_sys}} is on top of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_top}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_top}} can be used by the user to create some content visible everywhere. For example, a menu bar, a pop\sphinxhyphen{}up, etc. If the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{click}} attribute is enabled, then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_top}} will absorb all user clicks and acts as a modal.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}flag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}top}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}OBJ\PYGZus{}FLAG\PYGZus{}CLICKABLE}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_sys}} is also used for similar purposes in LVGL. For example, it places the mouse cursor above all layers to be sure it's always visible.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Events}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:events}}\label{\detokenize{overview/event::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Events are triggered in LVGL when something happens which might be interesting to the user, e.g. when an object
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
is clicked

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
is scrolled

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
has its value changed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
is redrawn, etc.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Add events to the object}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:add-events-to-the-object}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The user can assign callback functions to an object to see its events. In practice, it looks like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{btn} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}btn\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{btn}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}CLICKED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}   \PYG{c+cm}{/*Assign an event callback*/}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{event}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{printf}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Clicked}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CLICKED}} means that only the click event will call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{my\_event\_cb}}. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event:event-codes}]{\emph{list of event codes}}} for all the options.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_ALL}} can be used to receive all events.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The last parameter of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_event\_cb}} is a pointer to any custom data that will be available in the event. It will be described later in more detail.

\sphinxAtStartPar
More events can be added to an object, like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}CLICKED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb\PYGZus{}2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb\PYGZus{}3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}ALL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}		\PYG{c+cm}{/*No filtering, receive all events*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Even the same event callback can be used on an object with different \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{user\_data}}. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{increment\PYGZus{}on\PYGZus{}click}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}CLICKED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{num1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{increment\PYGZus{}on\PYGZus{}click}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}CLICKED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{num2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The events will be called in the order as they were added.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other objects can use the same \sphinxstyleemphasis{event callback}.


\subsection{Remove event(s) from an object}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:remove-event-s-from-an-object}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Events can be removed from an object with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_remove\_event\_cb(obj, event\_cb)}} function or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_remove\_event\_dsc(obj, event\_dsc)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{event\_dsc}} is a pointer returned by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_event\_cb}}.


\subsection{Event codes}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:event-codes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The event codes can be grouped into these categories:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Input device events

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Drawing events

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Other events

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Special events

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Custom events

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All objects (such as Buttons/Labels/Sliders etc.) regardless their type receive the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Input device}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Drawing} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Other} events.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Special events} are specific to a particular widget type. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/index::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{widgets' documentation}}}} to learn when they are sent,

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Custom events} are added by the user and are never sent by LVGL.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following event codes exist:


\subsubsection{Input device events}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:input-device-events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_PRESSED}}      An object has been pressed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_PRESSING}}     An object is being pressed (called continuously while pressing)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_PRESS\_LOST}}   An object is still being pressed but slid cursor/finger off of the object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SHORT\_CLICKED}}    An object was pressed for a short period of time, then released. Not called if scrolled.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_LONG\_PRESSED}} An object has been pressed for at least the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{long\_press\_time}} specified in the input device driver.  Not called if scrolled.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_LONG\_PRESSED\_REPEAT}}  Called after \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{long\_press\_time}} in every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{long\_press\_repeat\_time}} ms.  Not called if scrolled.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CLICKED}}      Called on release if an object did not scroll (regardless of long press)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_RELEASED}}     Called in every case when an object has been released

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCROLL\_BEGIN}} Scrolling begins. The event parameter is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} or an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_anim\_t *}} with a scroll animation descriptor that can be modified if required.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCROLL\_END}}   Scrolling ends.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCROLL}}       An object was scrolled

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_GESTURE}}      A gesture is detected. Get the gesture with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_indev\_get\_gesture\_dir(lv\_indev\_get\_act());}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_KEY}}          A key is sent to an object. Get the key with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_indev\_get\_key(lv\_indev\_get\_act());}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_FOCUSED}}      An object is focused

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DEFOCUSED}}    An object is unfocused

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_LEAVE}}        An object is unfocused but still selected

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_HIT\_TEST}}     Perform advanced hit\sphinxhyphen{}testing. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_hit\_test\_info\_t * a = lv\_event\_get\_hit\_test\_info(e)}} and check if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a\sphinxhyphen{}>point}} can click the object or not. If not set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a\sphinxhyphen{}>res = false}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Drawing events}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:drawing-events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_COVER\_CHECK}} Check if an object fully covers an area. The event parameter is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_cover\_check\_info\_t *}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_REFR\_EXT\_DRAW\_SIZE}}  Get the required extra draw area around an object (e.g. for a shadow). The event parameter is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_coord\_t *}} to store the size. Only overwrite it with a larger value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_MAIN\_BEGIN}} Starting the main drawing phase.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_MAIN}}   Perform the main drawing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_MAIN\_END}}   Finishing the main drawing phase

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_POST\_BEGIN}} Starting the post draw phase (when all children are drawn)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_POST}}   Perform the post draw phase (when all children are drawn)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_POST\_END}}   Finishing the post draw phase (when all children are drawn)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} Starting to draw a part. The event parameter is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_draw\_dsc\_t *}}. Learn more {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/drawing::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{here}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}}   Finishing to draw a part. The event parameter is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_draw\_dsc\_t *}}. Learn more {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/drawing::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{here}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_...}} events it's not allowed to adjust the widgets' properties. E.g. you can not call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_width()}}.
In other words only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get}} functions can be called.


\subsubsection{Other events}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:other-events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DELETE}}       Object is being deleted

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CHILD\_CHANGED}}    Child was removed/added

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CHILD\_CREATED}}    Child was created, always bubbles up to all parents

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CHILD\_DELETED}}    Child was deleted, always bubbles up to all parents

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SIZE\_CHANGED}}    Object coordinates/size have changed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_STYLE\_CHANGED}}    Object's style has changed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_BASE\_DIR\_CHANGED}} The base dir has changed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_GET\_SELF\_SIZE}}    Get the internal size of a widget

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCREEN\_UNLOAD\_START}} A screen unload started, fired immediately when lv\_scr\_load/lv\_scr\_load\_anim is called

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCREEN\_LOAD\_START}} A screen load started, fired when the screen change delay is expired

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCREEN\_LOADED}}    A screen was loaded, called when all animations are finished

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_SCREEN\_UNLOADED}}  A screen was unloaded, called when all animations are finished

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Special events}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:special-events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}}    The object's value has changed (i.e. slider moved)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_INSERT}}       Text is being inserted into the object. The event data is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char *}} being inserted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_REFRESH}}      Notify the object to refresh something on it (for the user)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_READY}}        A process has finished

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CANCEL}}       A process has been canceled

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Custom events}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:custom-events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any custom event codes can be registered by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uint32\_t MY\_EVENT\_1 = lv\_event\_register\_id();}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
They can be sent to any object with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_send(obj, MY\_EVENT\_1, \&some\_data)}}


\subsection{Sending events}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:sending-events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To manually send events to an object, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_send(obj, <EVENT\_CODE> \&some\_data)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, this can be used to manually close a message box by simulating a button press (although there are simpler ways to do this):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cm}{/*Simulate the press of the first button (indexes start from zero)*/}
\PYG{k+kt}{uint32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{btn\PYGZus{}id} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}send}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{mbox}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}VALUE\PYGZus{}CHANGED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{btn\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Refresh event}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:refresh-event}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_REFRESH}} is a special event because it's designed to let the user notify an object to refresh itself. Some examples:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
notify a label to refresh its text according to one or more variables (e.g. current time)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
refresh a label when the language changes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enable a button if some conditions are met (e.g. the correct PIN is entered)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
add/remove styles to/from an object if a limit is exceeded, etc

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Fields of lv\_event\_t}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:fields-of-lv-event-t}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_t}} is the only parameter passed to the event callback and it contains all data about the event. The following values can be gotten from it:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_code(e)}} get the event code

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_current\_target(e)}} get the object to which an event was sent. I.e. the object whose event handler is being called.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_target(e)}} get the object that originally triggered the event (different from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_target}} if {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event:event-bubbling}]{\emph{event bubbling}}} is enabled)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_user\_data(e)}} get the pointer passed as the last parameter of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_event\_cb}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_param(e)}} get the parameter passed as the last parameter of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_send}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Event bubbling}
\label{\detokenize{overview/event:event-bubbling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_flag(obj, LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_EVENT\_BUBBLE)}} is enabled all events will be sent to an object's parent too. If the parent also has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_EVENT\_BUBBLE}} enabled the event will be sent to its parent and so on.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{target} parameter of the event is always the current target object, not the original object. To get the original target call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_original\_target(e)}} in the event handler.

\label{\detokenize{overview/event:examples}}

        \PYG{n}{label}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{The last button event:}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}CLICKED}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{elif} \PYG{n}{code} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{EVENT}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{LONG\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{label}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{The last button event:}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}LONG\PYGZus{}PRESSED}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Input devices}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:input-devices}}\label{\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An input device usually means:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pointer\sphinxhyphen{}like input device like touchpad or mouse

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keypads like a normal keyboard or simple numeric keypad

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Encoders with left/right turn and push options

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
External hardware buttons which are assigned to specific points on the screen

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before reading further, please read the {[}Porting{]}(/porting/indev) section of Input devices
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Pointers}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:pointers}}

\subsubsection{Cursor}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:cursor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pointer input devices (like a mouse) can have a cursor.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{mouse\PYGZus{}indev} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}drv\PYGZus{}register}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{indev\PYGZus{}drv}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}IMG\PYGZus{}DECLARE}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{mouse\PYGZus{}cursor\PYGZus{}icon}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}                          \PYG{c+cm}{/*Declare the image source.*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{cursor\PYGZus{}obj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}       \PYG{c+cm}{/*Create an image object for the cursor */}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}src}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cursor\PYGZus{}obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{mouse\PYGZus{}cursor\PYGZus{}icon}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}             \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set the image source*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}cursor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{mouse\PYGZus{}indev}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{cursor\PYGZus{}obj}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}               \PYG{c+cm}{/*Connect the image  object to the driver*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the cursor object should have \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_clear\_flag(cursor\_obj, LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CLICKABLE)}}.
For images, \sphinxstyleemphasis{clicking} is disabled by default.


\subsubsection{Gestures}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:gestures}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pointer input devices can detect basic gestures. By default, most of the widgets send the gestures to its parent, so finally the gestures can be detected on the screen object in a form of an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_GESTURE}} event. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{my\PYGZus{}event}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
  \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{screen} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}current\PYGZus{}target}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
  \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}dir\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{dir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}gesture\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}indev\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
  \PYG{k}{switch}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dir}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{k}{case} \PYG{n+nl}{LV\PYGZus{}DIR\PYGZus{}LEFT}\PYG{p}{:}
      \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}
      \PYG{k}{break}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{k}{case} \PYG{n+nl}{LV\PYGZus{}DIR\PYGZus{}RIGHT}\PYG{p}{:}
      \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}
      \PYG{k}{break}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{k}{case} \PYG{n+nl}{LV\PYGZus{}DIR\PYGZus{}TOP}\PYG{p}{:}
      \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}
      \PYG{k}{break}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{k}{case} \PYG{n+nl}{LV\PYGZus{}DIR\PYGZus{}BOTTOM}\PYG{p}{:}
      \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}
      \PYG{k}{break}\PYG{p}{;}
  \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{screen1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}event}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}GESTURE}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To prevent passing the gesture event to the parent from an object use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_clear\_flag(obj, LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_GESTURE\_BUBBLE)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, gestures are not triggered if an object is being scrolled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you did some action on a gesture you can call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_indev\_wait\_release(lv\_indev\_get\_act())}} in the event handler to prevent LVGL sending further input device related events.


\subsection{Keypad and encoder}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:keypad-and-encoder}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can fully control the user interface without a touchpad or mouse by using a keypad or encoder(s). It works similar to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{TAB} key on the PC to select an element in an application or a web page.


\subsubsection{Groups}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:groups}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Objects you want to control with a keypad or encoder need to be added to a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Group}.
In every group there is exactly one focused object which receives the pressed keys or the encoder actions.
For example, if a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}} is focused and you press some letter on a keyboard, the keys will be sent and inserted into the text area.
Similarly, if a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/slider::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Slider}}}} is focused and you press the left or right arrows, the slider's value will be changed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You need to associate an input device with a group. An input device can send key events to only one group but a group can receive data from more than one input device.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To create a group use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_group\_t * g = lv\_group\_create()}} and to add an object to the group use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_group\_add\_obj(g, obj)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To associate a group with an input device use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_indev\_set\_group(indev, g)}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indev}} is the return value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_indev\_drv\_register()}}


\paragraph{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are some predefined keys which have special meaning:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_NEXT} Focus on the next object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_PREV} Focus on the previous object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_ENTER} Triggers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_PRESSED/CLICKED/LONG\_PRESSED}} etc. events

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_UP} Increase value or move upwards

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_DOWN} Decrease value or move downwards

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT} Increase value or move to the right

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_LEFT} Decrease value or move to the left

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_ESC}  Close or exit (E.g. close a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Drop down list}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_DEL}  Delete (E.g. a character on the right in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_BACKSPACE} Delete a character on the left (E.g. in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_HOME} Go to the beginning/top (E.g. in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LV\_KEY\_END} Go to the end (E.g. in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}})

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The most important special keys are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_NEXT/PREV}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT}}.
In your \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{read\_cb}} function, you should translate some of your keys to these special keys to support navigation in a group and interact with selected objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Usually, it's enough to use only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT/RIGHT}} because most objects can be fully controlled with them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With an encoder you should use only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}}.


\paragraph{Edit and navigate mode}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:edit-and-navigate-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Since a keypad has plenty of keys, it's easy to navigate between objects and edit them using the keypad. But encoders have a limited number of "keys" and hence it is difficult to navigate using the default options. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Navigate} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Edit} modes are used to avoid this problem with encoders.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxstyleemphasis{Navigate} mode, an encoder's \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT/RIGHT}} is translated to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_NEXT/PREV}}. Therefore, the next or previous object will be selected by turning the encoder.
Pressing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} will change to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Edit} mode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxstyleemphasis{Edit} mode, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_NEXT/PREV}} is usually used to modify an object.
Depending on the object's type, a short or long press of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} changes back to \sphinxstyleemphasis{Navigate} mode.
Usually, an object which cannot be pressed (like a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/slider::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Slider}}}}) leaves \sphinxstyleemphasis{Edit} mode upon a short click. But with objects where a short click has meaning (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Button}}}}), a long press is required.


\paragraph{Default group}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:default-group}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interactive widgets \sphinxhyphen{} such as buttons, checkboxes, sliders, etc. \sphinxhyphen{} can be automatically added to a default group.
Just create a group with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_group\_t * g = lv\_group\_create();}} and set the default group with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_group\_set\_default(g);}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Don't forget to assign one or more input devices to the default group with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ lv\_indev\_set\_group(my\_indev, g);}}.


\subsubsection{Styling}
\label{\detokenize{overview/indev:styling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If an object is focused either by clicking it via touchpad or focused via an encoder or keypad it goes to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUSED}} state. Hence, focused styles will be applied to it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If an object switches to edit mode it enters the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUSED | LV\_STATE\_EDITED}} states so these style properties will be shown.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a more detailed description read the \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/v7/en/html/overview/style.html}{Style} section.

\section{Displays}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:displays}}\label{\detokenize{overview/display::doc}}
\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The basic concept of a \sphinxstyleemphasis{display} in LVGL is explained in the {[}Porting{]}(/porting/display) section. So before reading further, please read the {[}Porting{]}(/porting/display) section first.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Multiple display support}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:multiple-display-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In LVGL you can have multiple displays, each with their own driver and objects. The only limitation is that every display needs to have the same color depth (as defined in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH}}).
If the displays are different in this regard the rendered image can be converted to the correct format in the drivers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flush\_cb}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Creating more displays is easy: just initialize more display buffers and register another driver for every display.
When you create the UI, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_set\_default(disp)}} to tell the library on which display to create objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Why would you want multi\sphinxhyphen{}display support? Here are some examples:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Have a "normal" TFT display with local UI and create "virtual" screens on VNC on demand. (You need to add your VNC driver).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Have a large TFT display and a small monochrome display.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Have some smaller and simple displays in a large instrument or technology.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Have two large TFT displays: one for a customer and one for the shop assistant.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Using only one display}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:using-only-one-display}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using more displays can be useful but in most cases it's not required. Therefore, the whole concept of multi\sphinxhyphen{}display handling is completely hidden if you register only one display.
By default, the last created (and only) display is used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_scr\_act()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_scr\_load(scr)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_layer\_top()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_layer\_sys()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_HOR\_RES}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_VER\_RES}} are always applied on the most recently created (default) display.
If you pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{disp}} parameter to display related functions the default display will usually be used.
E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_trig\_activity(NULL)}} will trigger a user activity on the default display. (See below in {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/display:Inactivity}]{\emph{Inactivity}}}).


\subsubsection{Mirror display}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:mirror-display}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To mirror the image of a display to another display, you don't need to use multi\sphinxhyphen{}display support. Just transfer the buffer received in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drv.flush\_cb}} to the other display too.


\subsubsection{Split image}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:split-image}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can create a larger virtual display from an array of smaller ones. You can create it as below:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the resolution of the displays to the large display's resolution.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drv.flush\_cb}}, truncate and modify the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area}} parameter for each display.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send the buffer's content to each real display with the truncated area.

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{Screens}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:screens}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every display has its own set of \sphinxhref{overview/object\#screen-the-most-basic-parent}{screens} and the objects on each screen.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Be sure not to confuse displays and screens:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Displays} are the physical hardware drawing the pixels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Screens} are the high\sphinxhyphen{}level root objects associated with a particular display. One display can have multiple screens associated with it, but not vice versa.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Screens can be considered the highest level containers which have no parent.
A screen's size is always equal to its display and their origin is (0;0). Therefore, a screen's coordinates can't be changed, i.e. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_pos()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_size()}} or similar functions can't be used on screens.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A screen can be created from any object type but the two most typical types are {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/img::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Image}}}} (to create a wallpaper).

\sphinxAtStartPar
To create a screen, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_t * scr = lv\_<type>\_create(NULL, copy)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copy}} can be an existing screen copied into the new screen.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To load a screen, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_scr\_load(scr)}}. To get the active screen, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_scr\_act()}}. These functions work on the default display. If you want to specify which display to work on, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_get\_scr\_act(disp)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_load\_scr(disp, scr)}}. A screen can be loaded with animations too. Read more \sphinxhref{object.html\#load-screens}{here}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Screens can be deleted with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_del(scr)}}, but ensure that you do not delete the currently loaded screen.


\subsubsection{Transparent screens}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:transparent-screens}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Usually, the opacity of the screen is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_COVER}} to provide a solid background for its children. If this is not the case (opacity < 100\%) the display's background color or image will be visible.
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/display:display-background}]{\emph{Display background}}} section for more details. If the display's background opacity is also not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_COVER}} LVGL has no solid background to draw.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This configuration (transparent screen and display) could be used to create for example OSD menus where a video is played on a lower layer, and a menu is overlayed on an upper layer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To handle transparent displays, special (slower) color mixing algorithms need to be used by LVGL so this feature needs to enabled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_SCREEN\_TRANSP}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.
The Alpha channel of 32\sphinxhyphen{}bit colors will be 0 where there are no objects and 255 where there are solid objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In summary, to enable transparent screens and displays for OSD menu\sphinxhyphen{}like UIs:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_SCREEN\_TRANSP}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the screen's opacity to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_TRANSP}} e.g. with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_style\_bg\_opa(lv\_scr\_act(), LV\_OPA\_TRANSP, LV\_PART\_MAIN)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the display opacity to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_TRANSP}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_set\_bg\_opa(NULL, LV\_OPA\_TRANSP);}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Features of displays}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:features-of-displays}}

\subsubsection{Inactivity}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:inactivity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A user's inactivity time is measured on each display. Every use of an {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Input device}}}} (if \sphinxhref{/porting/indev\#other-features}{associated with the display}) counts as an activity.
To get time elapsed since the last activity, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_get\_inactive\_time(disp)}}. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} is passed, the lowest inactivity time among all displays will be returned (\sphinxstylestrong{NULL isn't just the default display}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can manually trigger an activity using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_trig\_activity(disp)}}. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{disp}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, the default screen will be used (\sphinxstylestrong{and not all displays}).


\subsubsection{Background}
\label{\detokenize{overview/display:background}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every display has a background color, background image and background opacity properties. They become visible when the current screen is transparent or not positioned to cover the whole display.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The background color is a simple color to fill the display. It can be adjusted with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_set\_bg\_color(disp, color)}};

\sphinxAtStartPar
The display background image is a path to a file or a pointer to an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_dsc\_t}} variable (converted image data) to be used as wallpaper. It can be set with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_set\_bg\_image(disp, \&my\_img)}};
If a background image is configured the background won't be filled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bg\_color}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The opacity of the background color or image can be adjusted with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_set\_bg\_opa(disp, opa)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{disp}} parameter of these functions can be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} to select the default display.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n x current\_dpi/160}} 

\end{description}\end{quote}

\pysiglinewithargsret{\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{overview/display:lv__disp_8h_1a5a5f23760a6625483500522546b659c6}}\DUrole{k}{static}\DUrole{w}{  }\DUrole{k}{inline}\DUrole{w}{  }\DUrole{n}{lv\_coord\_t}\DUrole{w}{  }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\DUrole{n}{lv\_disp\_dpx}}}}{\DUrole{k}{const}\DUrole{w}{  }{\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/display:_CPPv49lv_disp_t}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{n}{lv\_disp\_t}}}}\DUrole{w}{  }\DUrole{p}{*}\DUrole{n,sig-param}{disp}, \DUrole{n}{lv\_coord\_t}\DUrole{w}{  }\DUrole{n,sig-param}{n}}{}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Scale the given number of pixels (a distance or size) relative to a 160 DPI display considering the DPI of the given display. It ensures that e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dpx(100)}} will have the same physical size regardless to the DPI of the display.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n}} \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{} the number of pixels to scale 

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n x current\_dpi/160}} 

\end{description}\end{quote}

\section{Colors}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:colors}}\label{\detokenize{overview/color::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The color module handles all color\sphinxhyphen{}related functions like changing color depth, creating colors from hex code, converting between color depths, mixing colors, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_t}} is used to store a color. Its fields are set according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}. (See below)

\sphinxAtStartPar
You may set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_16\_SWAP}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} to swap bytes of \sphinxstyleemphasis{RGB565} colors. You may need this when sending 16\sphinxhyphen{}bit colors via a byte\sphinxhyphen{}oriented interface like SPI. As 16\sphinxhyphen{}bit numbers are stored in little\sphinxhyphen{}endian format (lower byte at the lower address), the interface will send the lower byte first. However, displays usually need the higher byte first. A mismatch in the byte order will result in highly distorted colors.


\subsection{Creating colors}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:creating-colors}}

\subsubsection{RGB}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:rgb}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create colors from Red, Green and Blue channel values:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{//All channels are 0\PYGZhy{}255}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}make}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{red}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{green}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{blue}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{//From hex code 0x000000..0xFFFFFF interpreted as RED + GREEN + BLUE}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hex}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mh}{0x123456}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{//From 3 digits. Same as lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hex(0x112233)}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hex3}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mh}{0x123}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{HSV}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:hsv}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create colors from Hue, Saturation and Value values:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{//h = 0..359, s = 0..100, v = 0..100}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hsv\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}rgb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{h}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{s}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{v}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{//All channels are 0\PYGZhy{}255}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hsv\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}hsv} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}rgb\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}hsv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{r}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{b}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}


\PYG{c+c1}{//From lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t variable}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hsv\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c\PYGZus{}hsv} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}hsv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{color}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Palette}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:palette}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL includes \sphinxhref{https://vuetifyjs.com/en/styles/colors/\#material-colors}{Material Design's palette} of colors. In this system all named colors have a nominal main color as well as four darker and five lighter variants.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The names of the colors are as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_RED}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_PINK}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_PURPLE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_DEEP\_PURPLE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_INDIGO}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_BLUE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_LIGHT\_BLUE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_CYAN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_TEAL}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_GREEN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_LIGHT\_GREEN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_LIME}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_YELLOW}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_AMBER}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_ORANGE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_DEEP\_ORANGE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_BROWN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_BLUE\_GREY}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PALETTE\_GREY}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To get the main color use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_t c = lv\_palette\_main(LV\_PALETTE\_...)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the lighter variants of a palette color use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_t c = lv\_palette\_lighten(LV\_PALETTE\_..., v)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v}} can be 1..5.
For the darker variants of a palette color use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_t c = lv\_palette\_darken(LV\_PALETTE\_..., v)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v}} can be 1..4.


\subsubsection{Modify and mix colors}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:modify-and-mix-colors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following functions can modify a color:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{// Lighten a color. 0: no change, 255: white}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}lighten}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lvl}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Darken a color. 0: no change, 255: black}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}darken}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}opa\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{lvl}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Lighten or darken a color. 0: black, 128: no change 255: white}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}change\PYGZus{}lightness}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}opa\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{lvl}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}


\PYG{c+c1}{// Mix two colors with a given ratio 0: full c2, 255: full c1, 128: half c1 and half c2}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}mix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{c1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{c2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ratio}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Built\sphinxhyphen{}in colors}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:built-in-colors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_white()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_black()}} return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0xFFFFFF}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0x000000}} respectively.


\subsection{Opacity}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:opacity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To describe opacity the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_opa\_t}} type is created from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uint8\_t}}. Some special purpose defines are also introduced:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_TRANSP}} Value: 0, means no opacity making the color completely transparent

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_10}} Value: 25, means the color covers only a little

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_20 ... OPA\_80}} follow logically

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_90}} Value: 229, means the color near completely covers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_COVER}} Value: 255, means the color completely covers (full opacity)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_*}} defines in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_mix()}} as a mixing \sphinxstyleemphasis{ratio}.


\subsection{Color types}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:color-types}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following variable types are defined by the color module:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color1\_t}} Monochrome color. Also has R, G, B fields for compatibility but they are always the same value (1 byte)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color8\_t}} A structure to store R (3 bit),G (3 bit),B (2 bit) components for 8\sphinxhyphen{}bit colors (1 byte)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color16\_t}} A structure to store R (5 bit),G (6 bit),B (5 bit) components for 16\sphinxhyphen{}bit colors (2 byte)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color32\_t}} A structure to store R (8 bit),G (8 bit), B (8 bit) components for 24\sphinxhyphen{}bit colors (4 byte)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_t}} Equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color1/8/16/24\_t}} depending on the configured color depth setting

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_int\_t}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uint8\_t}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uint16\_t}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uint32\_t}} depending on the color depth setting. Used to build color arrays from plain numbers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_opa\_t}} A simple \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uint8\_t}} type to describe opacity.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_t}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color1\_t}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color8\_t}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color16\_t}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color32\_t}} types have four fields:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ch.red}} red channel

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ch.green}} green channel

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ch.blue}} blue channel

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{full*}} red + green + blue as one number

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set the current color depth in \sphinxstyleemphasis{lv\_conf.h}, by setting the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH}} define to 1 (monochrome), 8, 16 or 32.


\subsubsection{Convert color}
\label{\detokenize{overview/color:convert-color}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can convert a color from the current color depth to another. The converter functions return with a number, so you have to use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{full}} field to map a converted color back into a structure:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{red}   \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mh}{0x38}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{green} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mh}{0x70}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{blue}  \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mh}{0xCC}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color1\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c1}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{c1}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{full} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}to1}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}	\PYG{c+cm}{/*Return 1 for light colors, 0 for dark colors*/}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color8\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c8}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{c8}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{full} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}to8}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}	\PYG{c+cm}{/*Give a 8 bit number with the converted color*/}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color16\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c16}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{c16}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{full} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}to16}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*Give a 16 bit number with the converted color*/}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{c24}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{c32}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{full} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}to32}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}	\PYG{c+cm}{/*Give a 32 bit number with the converted color*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\section{Fonts}
\label{\detokenize{overview/font:fonts}}\label{\detokenize{overview/font::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In LVGL fonts are collections of bitmaps and other information required to render images of individual letters (glyph).
A font is stored in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_font\_t}} variable and can be set in a style's \sphinxstyleemphasis{text\_font} field. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text\PYGZus{}font}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}font\PYGZus{}montserrat\PYGZus{}28}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}  \PYG{c+cm}{/*Set a larger font*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fonts have a \sphinxstylestrong{bpp (bits per pixel)} property. It shows how many bits are used to describe a pixel in a font. The value stored for a pixel determines the pixel's opacity.
This way, with higher \sphinxstyleemphasis{bpp}, the edges of the letter can be smoother. The possible \sphinxstyleemphasis{bpp} values are 1, 2, 4 and 8 (higher values mean better quality).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bpp} property also affects the amount of memory needed to store a font. For example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{bpp = 4} makes a font nearly four times larger compared to \sphinxstyleemphasis{bpp = 1}.


\subsection{Unicode support}
\label{\detokenize{overview/font:unicode-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL supports \sphinxstylestrong{UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8} encoded Unicode characters.
Your editor needs to be configured to save your code/text as UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 (usually this the default) and be sure that, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TXT\_ENC}} is set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TXT\_ENC\_UTF8}} in \sphinxstyleemphasis{lv\_conf.h}. (This is the default value)

\sphinxAtStartPar
To test it try

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{label1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}SYMBOL\PYGZus{}OK}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If all works well, a \(\checkmark\) character should be displayed.

\label{\detokenize{overview/font:special-fonts}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FONT\_MONTSERRAT\_12\_SUBPX}} Same as normal 12 px font but with {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/font:subpixel-rendering}]{\emph{subpixel rendering}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FONT\_MONTSERRAT\_28\_COMPRESSED}} Same as normal 28 px font but stored as a {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/font:compress-fonts}]{\emph{compressed font}}} with 3 bpp

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FONT\_DEJAVU\_16\_PERSIAN\_HEBREW}} 16 px font with normal range + Hebrew, Arabic, Persian letters and all their forms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
