\section{Drawing}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:drawing}}\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
With LVGL, you don't need to draw anything manually. Just create objects (like buttons, labels, arc, etc.), move and change them, and LVGL will refresh and redraw what is required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, it can be useful to have a basic understanding of how drawing happens in LVGL to add customization, make it easier to find bugs or just out of curiosity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The basic concept is to not draw directly onto the display but rather to first draw on an internal draw buffer. When a drawing (rendering) is ready that buffer is copied to the display.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The draw buffer can be smaller than a display's size. LVGL will simply render in "tiles" that fit into the given draw buffer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This approach has two main advantages compared to directly drawing to the display:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It avoids flickering while the layers of the UI are drawn. For example, if LVGL drew directly onto the display, when drawing a \sphinxstyleemphasis{background + button + text}, each "stage" would be visible for a short time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It's faster to modify a buffer in internal RAM and finally write one pixel only once than reading/writing the display directly on each pixel access.
(e.g. via a display controller with SPI interface).

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that this concept is different from "traditional" double buffering where there are two display sized frame buffers:
one holds the current image to show on the display, and rendering happens to the other (inactive) frame buffer, and they are swapped when the rendering is finished.
The main difference is that with LVGL you don't have to store two frame buffers (which usually requires external RAM) but only smaller draw buffer(s) that can easily fit into internal RAM.


\subsection{Mechanism of screen refreshing}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:mechanism-of-screen-refreshing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be sure to get familiar with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{porting/display::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Buffering modes of LVGL}}}} first.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL refreshes the screen in the following steps:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Something happens in the UI which requires redrawing. For example, a button is pressed, a chart is changed, an animation happened, etc.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL saves the changed object's old and new area into a buffer, called an \sphinxstyleemphasis{Invalid area buffer}. For optimization, in some cases, objects are not added to the buffer:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hidden objects are not added.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Objects completely out of their parent are not added.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Areas partially out of the parent are cropped to the parent's area.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Objects on other screens are not added.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DISP\_DEF\_REFR\_PERIOD}} (set in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}) the following happens:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL checks the invalid areas and joins those that are adjacent or intersecting.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Takes the first joined area, if it's smaller than the \sphinxstyleemphasis{draw buffer}, then simply renders the area's content into the \sphinxstyleemphasis{draw buffer}.
If the area doesn't fit into the buffer, draw as many lines as possible to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{draw buffer}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the area is rendered, call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flush\_cb}} from the display driver to refresh the display.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the area was larger than the buffer, render the remaining parts too.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Repeat the same with remaining joined areas.

\end{itemize}

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When an area is redrawn the library searches the top\sphinxhyphen{}most object which covers that area and starts drawing from that object.
For example, if a button's label has changed, the library will see that it's enough to draw the button under the text and it's not necessary to redraw the display under the rest of the button too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The difference between buffering modes regarding the drawing mechanism is the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{One buffer} \sphinxhyphen{} LVGL needs to wait for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_flush\_ready()}} (called from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flush\_cb}}) before starting to redraw the next part.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Two buffers} \sphinxhyphen{}  LVGL can immediately draw to the second buffer when the first is sent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flush\_cb}} because the flushing should be done by DMA (or similar hardware) in the background.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Double buffering} \sphinxhyphen{}  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flush\_cb}} should only swap the addresses of the frame buffers.

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{Masking}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:masking}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Masking} is the basic concept of LVGL's draw engine.
To use LVGL it's not required to know about the mechanisms described here but you might find interesting to know how drawing works under hood.
Knowing about masking comes in handy if you want to customize drawing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To learn about masking let's see the steps of drawing first.
LVGL performs the following steps to render any shape, image or text. It can be considered as a drawing pipeline.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prepare the draw descriptors} Create a draw descriptor from an object's styles (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_rect\_dsc\_t}}).  This gives us the parameters for drawing, for example colors, widths, opacity, fonts, radius, etc.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Call the draw function} Call the draw function with the draw descriptor and some other parameters (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_rect()}}).  It will render the primitive shape to the current draw buffer.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Create masks} If the shape is very simple and doesn't require masks, go to \#5. Otherwise, create the required masks in the draw function. (e.g. a rounded rectangle mask)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Calculate all the added mask} It composites opacity values into a \sphinxstyleemphasis{mask buffer} with the "shape" of the created masks.
E.g. in case of a "line mask" according to the parameters of the mask, keep one side of the buffer as it is (255 by default) and set the rest to 0 to indicate that this side should be removed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Blend a color or image} During blending, masking (make some pixels transparent or opaque), blending modes (additive, subtractive, etc.) and color/image opacity are handled.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL has the following built\sphinxhyphen{}in mask types which can be calculated and applied real\sphinxhyphen{}time:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DRAW\_MASK\_TYPE\_LINE}} Removes a side from a line (top, bottom, left or right). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_line}} uses four instances of it.
Essentially, every (skew) line is bounded with four line masks forming a rectangle.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DRAW\_MASK\_TYPE\_RADIUS}} Removes the inner or outer corners of a rectangle with a radiused transition. It's also used to create circles by setting the radius to large value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_RADIUS\_CIRCLE}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DRAW\_MASK\_TYPE\_ANGLE}} Removes a circular sector. It is used by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_arc}} to remove the "empty" sector.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DRAW\_MASK\_TYPE\_FADE}} Create a vertical fade (change opacity)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DRAW\_MASK\_TYPE\_MAP}} The mask is stored in a bitmap array and the necessary parts are applied

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Masks are used to create almost every basic primitive:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{letters} Create a mask from the letter and draw a rectangle with the letter's color using the mask.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{line} Created from four "line masks" to mask out the left, right, top and bottom part of the line to get a perfectly perpendicular perimeter.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{rounded rectangle} A mask is created real\sphinxhyphen{}time to add a radius to the corners.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{clip corner} To clip overflowing content (usually children) on rounded corners, a rounded rectangle mask is also applied.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{rectangle border} Same as a rounded rectangle but the inner part is masked out too.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{arc drawing} A circular border is drawn but an arc mask is applied too.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ARGB images} The alpha channel is separated into a mask and the image is drawn as a normal RGB image.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Using masks}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:using-masks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every mask type has a related parameter structure to describe the mask's data. The following parameter types exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_line\_param\_t}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_radius\_param\_t}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_angle\_param\_t}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_fade\_param\_t}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_map\_param\_t}}

\end{itemize}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize a mask parameter with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_<type>\_init}}. See \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask.h}} for the whole API.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add the mask parameter to the draw engine with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int16\_t mask\_id = lv\_draw\_mask\_add(\&param, ptr)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptr}} can be any pointer to identify the mask, (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} if unused).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Call the draw functions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Remove the mask from the draw engine with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_remove\_id(mask\_id)}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_remove\_custom(ptr)}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Free the parameter with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_free\_param(\&param)}}.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A parameter can be added and removed any number of times, but it needs to be freed when not required anymore.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_mask\_add}} saves only the pointer of the mask so the parameter needs to be valid while in use.


\subsection{Hook drawing}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:hook-drawing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Although widgets can be easily customized by styles there might be cases when something more custom is required.
To ensure a great level of flexibility LVGL sends a lot of events during drawing with parameters that tell what LVGL is about to draw.
Some fields of these parameters can be modified to draw something else or any custom drawing operations can be added manually.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A good use case for this is the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Button matrix}}}} widget. By default, its buttons can be styled in different states, but you can't style the buttons one by one.
However, an event is sent for every button and you can, for example, tell LVGL to use different colors on a specific button or to manually draw an image on some buttons.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each of these events is described in detail below.


\subsubsection{Main drawing}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:main-drawing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These events are related to the actual drawing of an object. E.g. the drawing of buttons, texts, etc. happens here.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_clip\_area(event)}} can be used to get the current clip area. The clip area is required in draw functions to make them draw only on a limited area.


\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_MAIN\_BEGIN}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-draw-main-begin}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sent before starting to draw an object. This is a good place to add masks manually. E.g. add a line mask that "removes" the right side of an object.


\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_MAIN}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-draw-main}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The actual drawing of an object happens in this event. E.g. a rectangle for a button is drawn here. First, the widgets' internal events are called to perform drawing and after that you can draw anything on top of them.
For example you can add a custom text or an image.


\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_MAIN\_END}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-draw-main-end}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Called when the main drawing is finished. You can draw anything here as well and it's also a good place to remove any masks created in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_MAIN\_BEGIN}}.


\subsubsection{Post drawing}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:post-drawing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Post drawing events are called when all the children of an object are drawn. For example LVGL use the post drawing phase to draw scrollbars because they should be above all of the children.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_clip\_area(event)}} can be used to get the current clip area.


\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_POST\_BEGIN}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-draw-post-begin}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sent before starting the post draw phase. Masks can be added here too to mask out the post drawn content.


\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_POST}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-draw-post}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The actual drawing should happen here.


\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_POST\_END}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-draw-post-end}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Called when post drawing has finished. If masks were not removed in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_MAIN\_END}} they should be removed here.


\subsubsection{Part drawing}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:part-drawing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When LVGL draws a part of an object (e.g. a slider's indicator, a table's cell or a button matrix's button) it sends events before and after drawing that part with some context of the drawing.
This allows changing the parts on a very low level with masks, extra drawing, or changing the parameters that LVGL is planning to use for drawing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In these events an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_draw\_part\_t}} structure is used to describe the context of the drawing. Not all fields are set for every part and widget.
To see which fields are set for a widget refer to the widget's documentation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_draw\_part\_t}} has the following fields:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{// Always set}
\PYG{k}{const} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}area\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{clip\PYGZus{}area}\PYG{p}{;}        \PYG{c+c1}{// The current clip area, required if you need to draw something in the event}
\PYG{k+kt}{uint32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{part}\PYG{p}{;}                      \PYG{c+c1}{// The current part for which the event is sent}
\PYG{k+kt}{uint32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{id}\PYG{p}{;}                        \PYG{c+c1}{// The index of the part. E.g. a button\PYGZsq{}s index on button matrix or table cell index.}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Draw desciptors, set only if related}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}rect\PYGZus{}dsc\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{rect\PYGZus{}dsc}\PYG{p}{;}      \PYG{c+c1}{// A draw descriptor that can be modified to changed what LVGL will draw. Set only for rectangle\PYGZhy{}like parts}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}dsc\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{label\PYGZus{}dsc}\PYG{p}{;}    \PYG{c+c1}{// A draw descriptor that can be modified to changed what LVGL will draw. Set only for text\PYGZhy{}like parts}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}line\PYGZus{}dsc\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}dsc}\PYG{p}{;}      \PYG{c+c1}{// A draw descriptor that can be modified to changed what LVGL will draw. Set only for line\PYGZhy{}like parts}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}dsc\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*}  \PYG{n}{img\PYGZus{}dsc}\PYG{p}{;}       \PYG{c+c1}{// A draw descriptor that can be modified to changed what LVGL will draw. Set only for image\PYGZhy{}like parts}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}draw\PYGZus{}arc\PYGZus{}dsc\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*}  \PYG{n}{arc\PYGZus{}dsc}\PYG{p}{;}       \PYG{c+c1}{// A draw descriptor that can be modified to changed what LVGL will draw. Set only for arc\PYGZhy{}like parts}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Other parameters}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}area\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}area}\PYG{p}{;}              \PYG{c+c1}{// The area of the part being drawn}
\PYG{k}{const} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}point\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{p1}\PYG{p}{;}              \PYG{c+c1}{// A point calculated during drawing. E.g. a point of a chart or the center of an arc.}
\PYG{k}{const} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}point\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{p2}\PYG{p}{;}              \PYG{c+c1}{// A point calculated during drawing. E.g. a point of a chart.}
\PYG{k+kt}{char} \PYG{n}{text}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{16}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}                      \PYG{c+c1}{// A text calculated during drawing. Can be modified. E.g. tick labels on a chart axis.}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}coord\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{radius}\PYG{p}{;}                  \PYG{c+c1}{// E.g. the radius of an arc (not the corner radius).}
\PYG{k+kt}{int32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{value}\PYG{p}{;}                      \PYG{c+c1}{// A value calculated during drawing. E.g. Chart\PYGZsq{}s tick line value.}
\PYG{k}{const} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{sub\PYGZus{}part\PYGZus{}ptr}\PYG{p}{;}          \PYG{c+c1}{// A pointer the identifies something in the part. E.g. chart series.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_draw\_part\_dsc(event)}} can be used to get a pointer to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_draw\_part\_t}}.


\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-draw-part-begin}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Start the drawing of a part. This is a good place to modify the draw descriptors (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}), or add masks.


\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-draw-part-end}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finish the drawing of a part. This is a good place to draw extra content on the part or remove masks added in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}}.


\subsubsection{Others}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:others}}

\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_COVER\_CHECK}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-cover-check}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This event is used to check whether an object fully covers an area or not.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_cover\_area(event)}} returns a pointer to an area to check and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_set\_cover\_res(event, res)}} can be used to set one of these results:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COVER\_RES\_COVER}} the area is fully covered by the object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COVER\_RES\_NOT\_COVER}} the area is not covered by the object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COVER\_RES\_MASKED}} there is a mask on the object, so it does not fully cover the area

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here are some reasons why an object would be unable to fully cover an area:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It's simply not fully in area

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It has a radius

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It doesn't have 100\% background opacity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It's an ARGB or chroma keyed image

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It does not have normal blending mode. In this case LVGL needs to know the colors under the object to apply blending properly

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It's a text, etc

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In short if for any reason the area below an object is visible than the object doesn't cover that area.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before sending this event LVGL checks if at least the widget's coordinates fully cover the area or not. If not the event is not called.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You need to check only the drawing you have added. The existing properties known by a widget are handled in its internal events.
E.g. if a widget has > 0 radius it might not cover an area, but you need to handle \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radius}} only if you will modify it and the widget won't know about it.


\paragraph{LV\_EVENT\_REFR\_EXT\_DRAW\_SIZE}
\label{\detokenize{overview/drawing:lv-event-refr-ext-draw-size}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you need to draw outside a widget, LVGL needs to know about it to provide extra space for drawing.
Let's say you create an event which writes the current value of a slider above its knob. In this case LVGL needs to know that the slider's draw area should be larger with the size required for the text.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can simply set the required draw area with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_set\_ext\_draw\_size(e, size)}}.

\subsection{Arm\sphinxhyphen{}2D GPU}
\label{\detokenize{overview/renderers/arm-2d:arm-2d-gpu}}\label{\detokenize{overview/renderers/arm-2d::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Arm\sphinxhyphen{}2D is not a GPU but \sphinxstylestrong{an abstraction layer for 2D GPUs dedicated to Microcontrollers}. It supports all Cortex\sphinxhyphen{}M processors ranging from Cortex\sphinxhyphen{}M0 to the latest Cortex\sphinxhyphen{}M85.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Arm\sphinxhyphen{}2D is an open\sphinxhyphen{}source project on Github. For more, please refer to: https://github.com/ARM\sphinxhyphen{}software/Arm\sphinxhyphen{}2D.


\subsubsection{How to Use}
\label{\detokenize{overview/renderers/arm-2d:how-to-use}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In general, you can set the macro \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_GPU\_ARM2D}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} to enable Arm\sphinxhyphen{}2D acceleration for LVGL.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are using \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/tree/master/env\_support/cmsis-pack}{CMSIS\sphinxhyphen{}Pack}} to deploy the LVGL. You don't have to define the macro \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_GPU\_ARM2D}} manually, instead, please select the component \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GPU Arm\sphinxhyphen{}2D}} in the \sphinxstylestrong{RTE} dialog. This step will define the macro for us.


\subsubsection{Design Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{overview/renderers/arm-2d:design-considerations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As mentioned before, Arm\sphinxhyphen{}2D is an abstraction layer for 2D GPU; hence if there is no accelerator or dedicated instruction set (such as Helium or ACI) available for Arm\sphinxhyphen{}2D, it provides negligible performance boost for LVGL (sometimes worse) for regular Cortex\sphinxhyphen{}M processors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{We highly recommend you enable Arm\sphinxhyphen{}2D acceleration for LVGL} when:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The target processors are \sphinxstylestrong{Cortex\sphinxhyphen{}M55} and/or \sphinxstylestrong{Cortex\sphinxhyphen{}M85}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The target processors support \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxhref{https://developer.arm.com/documentation/102102/0103/?lang=en}{Helium}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The device vendor provides an arm\sphinxhyphen{}2d compliant driver for their propriotory 2D accelerators and/or customized instruction set.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The target device contains \sphinxhref{https://community.arm.com/arm-community-blogs/b/internet-of-things-blog/posts/arm-corelink-dma-350-next-generation-direct-memory-access-for-endpoint-ai}{DMA\sphinxhyphen{}350}

\end{itemize}

\section{Base object (lv\_obj)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:base-object-lv-obj}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The 'Base Object' implements the basic properties of widgets on a screen, such as:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
coordinates

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
parent object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
children

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
contains the styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
attributes like \sphinxstyleemphasis{Clickable}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Scrollable}, etc.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In object\sphinxhyphen{}oriented thinking, it is the base class from which all other objects in LVGL are inherited.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The functions and functionalities of the Base object can be used with other widgets too. For example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_width(slider, 100)}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Base object can be directly used as a simple widget: it's nothing more than a rectangle. In HTML terms, think of it as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<div>}}.


\subsubsection{Coordinates}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:coordinates}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only a small subset of coordinate settings is described here. To see all the features of LVGL (padding, coordinates in styles, layouts, etc) visit the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/coords::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Coordinates}}}} page.


\paragraph{Size}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:size}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The object size can be modified on individual axes with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_width(obj, new\_width)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_height(obj, new\_height)}}, or both axes can be modified at the same time with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_size(obj, new\_width, new\_height)}}.


\paragraph{Position}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:position}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set the position relative to the parent with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_x(obj, new\_x)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_y(obj, new\_y)}}, or both axes at the same time with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_pos(obj, new\_x, new\_y)}}.


\paragraph{Alignment}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:alignment}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can align the object on its parent with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_align(obj, LV\_ALIGN\_...)}}. After this every x and y setting will be relative to the set alignment mode.
For example, this will shift the object by 10;20 px from the center of its parent:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}ALIGN\PYGZus{}CENTER}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}pos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{//Or in one function}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}ALIGN\PYGZus{}CENTER}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To align one object to another use: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_align\_to(obj\_to\_align, obj\_referece, LV\_ALIGN\_..., x, y)}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example, to align a text below an image: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_align\_to(text, image, LV\_ALIGN\_OUT\_BOTTOM\_MID, 0, 10)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following align types exist:
\sphinxincludegraphics{{align}.png}


\subsubsection{Parents and children}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:parents-and-children}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set a new parent for an object with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_parent(obj, new\_parent)}}. To get the current parent, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_parent(obj)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To get a specific child of a parent use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_child(parent, idx)}}. Some examples for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{idx}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} get the child created first

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} get the child created second

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} get the child created last

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The children can be iterated lke this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{uint32\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{for}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}child\PYGZus{}cnt}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{parent}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
  \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{child} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}child}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{parent}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
  \PYG{c+cm}{/*Do something with child*/}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_index(obj)}} returns the index of the object in its parent. It is equivalent to the number of younger children in the parent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can bring an object to the foreground or send it to the background with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_move\_foreground(obj)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_move\_background(obj)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can change the index of an object in its parent using  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_move\_to\_index(obj, index)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can swap the position of two objects with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_swap(obj1, obj2)}}.


\subsubsection{Display and Screens}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:display-and-screens}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
At the highest level of the LVGL object hierarchy is the \sphinxstyleemphasis{display} which represents the driver for a display device (physical display or simulator). A display can have one or more screens associated with it. Each screen contains a hierarchy of objects for graphical widgets representing a layout that covers the entire display.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When you have created a screen like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_t * screen = lv\_obj\_create(NULL)}}, you can make it active with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_scr\_load(screen)}}. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_scr\_act()}} function gives you a pointer to the active screen.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have multiple displays, it's important to know that the screen functions operate on the most recently created display or the one explicitly selected with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_set\_default}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To get an object's screen use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_screen(obj)}} function.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To set an event callback for an object, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_event\_cb(obj, event\_cb, LV\_EVENT\_..., user\_data)}},

\sphinxAtStartPar
To manually send an event to an object, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_send(obj, LV\_EVENT\_..., param)}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Read the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Event overview}}}} to learn more about events.


\subsubsection{Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be sure to read the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/style::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Style overview}}}}. Here only the most essential functions are described.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A new style can be added to an object with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_style(obj, \&new\_style, selector)}} function.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{selector}} is an ORed combination of part and state(s). E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR | LV\_STATE\_PRESSED}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The base objects use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} style properties and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}} with the typical background style properties.


\subsubsection{Flags}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:flags}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are some attributes which can be enabled/disabled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add/clear\_flag(obj, LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_...)}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_HIDDEN}}  Make the object hidden. (Like it wasn't there at all)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CLICKABLE}}  Make the object clickable by input devices

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CLICK\_FOCUSABLE}}  Add focused state to the object when clicked

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CHECKABLE}}  Toggle checked state when the object is clicked

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLLABLE}}  Make the object scrollable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_ELASTIC}}  Allow scrolling inside but with slower speed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_MOMENTUM}}  Make the object scroll further when "thrown"

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_ONE}} Allow scrolling only one snappable children

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_CHAIN\_HOR}}  Allow propagating the horizontal scroll to a parent

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_CHAIN\_VER}}  Allow propagating the vertical scroll to a parent

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_CHAIN}}  Simple packaging for (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_CHAIN\_HOR | LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_CHAIN\_VER}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_ON\_FOCUS}}  Automatically scroll object to make it visible when focused

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLL\_WITH\_ARROW}}  Allow scrolling the focused object with arrow keys

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SNAPPABLE}} If scroll snap is enabled on the parent it can snap to this object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_PRESS\_LOCK}} Keep the object pressed even if the press slid from the object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_EVENT\_BUBBLE}} Propagate the events to the parent too

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_GESTURE\_BUBBLE}} Propagate the gestures to the parent

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_ADV\_HITTEST}} Allow performing more accurate hit (click) test. E.g. accounting for rounded corners

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_IGNORE\_LAYOUT}} Make the object positionable by the layouts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_FLOATING}} Do not scroll the object when the parent scrolls and ignore layout

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_OVERFLOW\_VISIBLE}} Do not clip the children's content to the parent's boundary

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_LAYOUT\_1}}  Custom flag, free to use by layouts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_LAYOUT\_2}}  Custom flag, free to use by layouts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_WIDGET\_1}}  Custom flag, free to use by widget

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_WIDGET\_2}}  Custom flag, free to use by widget

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_USER\_1}}  Custom flag, free to use by user

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_USER\_2}}  Custom flag, free to use by user

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_USER\_3}}  Custom flag, free to use by user

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_USER\_4}}  Custom flag, free to use by user

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some examples:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cm}{/*Hide on object*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}flag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}OBJ\PYGZus{}FLAG\PYGZus{}HIDDEN}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+cm}{/*Make an object non\PYGZhy{}clickable*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}clear\PYGZus{}flag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}OBJ\PYGZus{}FLAG\PYGZus{}CLICKABLE}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Groups}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:groups}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Input devices overview}}}} to learn more about \sphinxstyleemphasis{Groups}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Objects are added to a \sphinxstyleemphasis{group} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_group\_add\_obj(group, obj)}}, and you can use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_group(obj)}} to see which group an object belongs to.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_is\_focused(obj)}} returns if the object is currently focused on its group or not. If the object is not added to a group, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} will be returned.


\subsubsection{Extended click area}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:extended-click-area}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the objects can be clicked only within their bounding area. However, this can be extended with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_ext\_click\_area(obj, size)}}.


\subsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:id1}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} when the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CHECKABLE}} flag is enabled and the object clicked (on transition to/from the checked state)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/obj:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CHECKABLE}} is enabled, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_UP}} make the object checked, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_DOWN}} make it unchecked.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_SCROLLABLE}} is enabled, but the object is not editable (as declared by the widget class), the arrow keys (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_UP}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_DOWN}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT}}) scroll the object. If the object can only scroll vertically, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT}} will scroll up/down instead, making it compatible with an encoder input device. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Input devices overview}}}} for more on encoder behaviors and the edit mode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\section{Core widgets}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/index:core-widgets}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/index::doc}}
\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Arc (lv\_arc)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:arc-lv-arc}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Arc consists of a background and a foreground arc. The foreground (indicator) can be touch\sphinxhyphen{}adjusted.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}}  Draws a background using the typical background style properties and an arc using the arc style properties. The arc's size and position will respect the \sphinxstyleemphasis{padding} style properties.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} Draws another arc using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{arc} style properties. Its padding values are interpreted relative to the background arc.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_KNOB}} Draws a handle on the end of the indicator using all background properties and padding values. With zero padding the knob size is the same as the indicator's width.
Larger padding makes it larger, smaller padding makes it smaller.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:usage}}

\paragraph{Value and range}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:value-and-range}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A new value can be set using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_value(arc, new\_value)}}.
The value is interpreted in a range (minimum and maximum values) which can be modified with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_range(arc, min, max)}}.
The default range is 0..100.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The indicator arc is drawn on the main part's arc. This if the value is set to maximum the indicator arc will cover the entire "background" arc.
To set the start and end angle of the background arc use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_bg\_angles(arc, start\_angle, end\_angle)}} functions or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_bg\_start/end\_angle(arc, angle)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Zero degrees is at the middle right (3 o'clock) of the object and the degrees are increasing in clockwise direction.
The angles should be in the {[}0;360{]} range.


\paragraph{Rotation}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:rotation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An offset to the 0 degree position can be added with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_rotation(arc, deg)}}.


\paragraph{Mode}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The arc can be one of the following modes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ARC\_MODE\_NORMAL}} The indicator arc is drawn from the minimum value to the current.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ARC\_MODE\_REVERSE}} The indicator arc is drawn counter\sphinxhyphen{}clockwise from the maximum value to the current.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ARC\_MODE\_SYMMETRICAL}} The indicator arc is drawn from the middle point to the current value.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The mode can be set by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_mode(arc, LV\_ARC\_MODE\_...)}} and used only if the angle is set by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_value()}} or the arc is adjusted by finger.


\paragraph{Change rate}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:change-rate}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the arc is pressed the current value will set with a limited speed according to the set \sphinxstyleemphasis{change rate}.
The change rate is defined in degree/second unit and can be set with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_change\_rage(arc, rate)}}


\paragraph{Setting the indicator manually}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:setting-the-indicator-manually}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It's also possible to set the angles of the indicator arc directly with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_angles(arc, start\_angle, end\_angle)}} function or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_set\_start/end\_angle(arc, start\_angle)}}.
In this case the set "value" and "mode" are ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In other words, the angle and value settings are independent. You should exclusively use one or the other. Mixing the two might result in unintended behavior.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To make the arc non\sphinxhyphen{}adjustable, remove the style of the knob and make the object non\sphinxhyphen{}clickable:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}remove\PYGZus{}style}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{arc}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}PART\PYGZus{}KNOB}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}clear\PYGZus{}flag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{arc}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}OBJ\PYGZus{}FLAG\PYGZus{}CLICKABLE}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Advanced hit test}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:advanced-hit-test}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_ADV\_HITTEST}} flag is enabled the arc can be clicked through in the middle. Clicks are recognized only on the ring of the background arc. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_ext\_click\_size()}} makes the sensitive area larger inside and outside with the given number of pixels.


\paragraph{Place another object to the knob}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:place-another-object-to-the-knob}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Another object can be positioned according to the current position of the arc in order to follow the arc's current value (angle).
To do this use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_align\_obj\_to\_angle(arc, obj\_to\_align, radius\_offset)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_arc\_rotate\_obj\_to\_angle(arc, obj\_to\_rotate, radius\_offset)}} can be used to rotate the object to the current value of the arc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It's a typical use case to call these functions in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VALUE\_CHANGED}} event of the arc.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} sent when the arc is pressed/dragged to set a new value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}} are sent with the following types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ARC\_DRAW\_PART\_BACKGROUND}} The background arc.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p1}}: center of the arc

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radius}}: radius of the arc

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arc\_dsc}}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ARC\_DRAW\_PART\_FOREGROUND}} The foreground arc.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p1}}: center of the arc

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radius}}: radius of the arc

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arc\_dsc}}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LV\_ARC\_DRAW\_PART\_KNOB The knob
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_KNOB}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: the area of the knob

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}:

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT/UP}} Increases the value by one.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT/DOWN}} Decreases the value by one.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:example}}

\paragraph{Simple Arc}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/arc:simple-arc}}


\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}


\end{sphinxuseclass}

\subsection{Bar (lv\_bar)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar:bar-lv-bar}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The bar object has a background and an indicator on it. The width of the indicator is set according to the current value of the bar.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Vertical bars can be created if the width of the object is smaller than its height.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Not only the end, but also the start value of the bar can be set, which changes the start position of the indicator.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the bar and it uses the typical background style properties. Adding padding makes the indicator smaller or larger. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anim\_time}} style property sets the animation time if the values set with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ANIM\_ON}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} The indicator itself; also uses all the typical background properties.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar:usage}}

\paragraph{Value and range}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar:value-and-range}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A new value can be set by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_bar\_set\_value(bar, new\_value, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}}.
The value is interpreted in a range (minimum and maximum values) which can be modified with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_bar\_set\_range(bar, min, max)}}.
The default range is 0..100.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The new value in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_bar\_set\_value}} can be set with or without an animation depending on the last parameter (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF}}).


\paragraph{Modes}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar:modes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The bar can be one of the following modes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BAR\_MODE\_NORMAL}} A normal bar as described above

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BAR\_MODE\_SYMMETRICAL}} Draw the indicator from the zero value to current value. Requires a negative minimum range and positive maximum range.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BAR\_MODE\_RANGE}} Allows setting the start value too by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_bar\_set\_start\_value(bar, new\_value, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}}. The start value always has to be smaller than the end value.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}} are sent for the following parts:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BAR\_DRAW\_PART\_INDICATOR}} The indicator of the bar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: area of the indicator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/bar:example}}

\subsection{Button (lv\_btn)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btn:button-lv-btn}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btn::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btn:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Buttons have no new features compared to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}}. They are useful for semantic purposes and have slightly different default settings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Buttons, by default, differ from Base object in the following ways:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Not scrollable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Added to the default group

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default height and width set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btn:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the button. Uses the typical background style properties.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btn:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are no new features compared to {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}}.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btn:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} when the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CHECKABLE}} flag is enabled and the object is clicked. The event happens on transition to/from the checked state.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btn:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the state of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} is translated to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_PRESSED/PRESSING/RELEASED}} etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btn:example}}

\paragraph{Simple Buttons}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btn:simple-buttons}}

\subsection{Button matrix (lv\_btnmatrix)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix:button-matrix-lv-btnmatrix}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Button Matrix object is a lightweight way to display multiple buttons in rows and columns. Lightweight because the buttons are not actually created but just virtually drawn on the fly. This way, one button use only eight extra bytes of memory instead of the \textasciitilde{}100\sphinxhyphen{}150 bytes a normal {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Button}}}} object plus the 100 or so bytes for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Label}}}} object.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Button matrix is added to the default group (if one is set). Besides the Button matrix is an editable object to allow selecting and clicking the buttons with encoder navigation too.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the button matrix, uses the typical background style properties. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_row}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_column}} sets the space between the buttons.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}} The buttons all use the text and typical background style properties except translations and transformations.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix:usage}}

\paragraph{Button's text}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix:button-s-text}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is a text on each button. To specify them a descriptor string array, called \sphinxstyleemphasis{map}, needs to be used.
The map can be set with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_set\_map(btnm, my\_map)}}.
The declaration of a map should look like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char * map{[}{]} = \{"btn1", "btn2", "btn3", NULL\}}}.
Note that the last element has to be either \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} or an empty string (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}})!

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\textbackslash{}n"}} in the map to insert a \sphinxstylestrong{line break}. E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"btn1", "btn2", "\textbackslash{}n", "btn3", ""\}}}. Each line's buttons have their width calculated automatically.
So in the example the first row will have 2 buttons each with 50\% width and a second row with 1 button having 100\% width.


\paragraph{Control buttons}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix:control-buttons}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The buttons' width can be set relative to the other button in the same row with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_set\_btn\_width(btnm, btn\_id, width)}}
E.g. in a line with two buttons: \sphinxstyleemphasis{btnA, width = 1} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{btnB, width = 2}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{btnA} will have 33 \% width and \sphinxstyleemphasis{btnB} will have 66 \% width.
It's similar to how the \sphinxhref{https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex-grow}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flex\sphinxhyphen{}grow}}} property works in CSS.
The width must be in the {[}1..15{]} range and the default width is 1.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the width, each button can be customized with the following parameters:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_HIDDEN}} Makes a button hidden (hidden buttons still take up space in the layout, they are just not visible or clickable)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_NO\_REPEAT}} Disable repeating when the button is long pressed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_DISABLED}} Makes a button disabled Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_DISABLED}} on normal objects

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_CHECKABLE}} Enable toggling of a button. I.e. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_CHECHED}} will be added/removed as the button is clicked

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_CHECKED}} Make the button checked. It will use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_CHECHKED}} styles.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_CLICK\_TRIG}} Enabled: send LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGE on CLICK, Disabled: send LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGE on PRESS

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_POPOVER}} Show the button label in a popover when pressing this key

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_RECOLOR}} Enable recoloring of button texts with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#}}. E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"It's \#ff0000 red\#"}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_CUSTOM\_1}} Custom free to use flag

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_CUSTOM\_2}} Custom free to use flag

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, all flags are disabled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set or clear a button's control attribute, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_set\_btn\_ctrl(btnm, btn\_id, LV\_BTNM\_CTRL\_...)}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_clear\_btn\_ctrl(btnm, btn\_id, LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_...)}} respectively. More \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNM\_CTRL\_...}} values can be OR\sphinxhyphen{}ed

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set/clear the same control attribute for all buttons of a button matrix, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_set\_btn\_ctrl\_all(btnm, LV\_BTNM\_CTRL\_...)}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_clear\_btn\_ctrl\_all(btnm, LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_...)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The set a control map for a button matrix (similarly to the map for the text), use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_set\_ctrl\_map(btnm, ctrl\_map)}}.
An element of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ctrl\_map}} should look like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ctrl\_map{[}0{]} = width | LV\_BTNM\_CTRL\_NO\_REPEAT |  LV\_BTNM\_CTRL\_CHECHKABLE}}.
The number of elements should be equal to the number of buttons (excluding newlines characters).


\paragraph{One check}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix:one-check}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The "One check" feature can be enabled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_set\_one\_checked(btnm, true)}} to allow only one button to be checked at a time.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when a button is pressed/released or repeated after long press. The event parameter is set to the ID of the pressed/released button.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}} are sent for the following types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_DRAW\_PART\_BTN}} The individual buttons.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}:index of the button being drawn

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: the area of teh button

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_get\_selected\_btn(btnm)}} returns the index of the most recently released or focused button or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_BTN\_NONE}} if no such button.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnmatrix\_get\_btn\_text(btnm, btn\_id)}} returns a pointer to the text of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{btn\_id}}th button.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT/UP/LEFT/RIGHT}} To navigate among the buttons to select one

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} To press/release the selected button

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Set a new map. Buttons will be created/deleted according to the map. The button matrix keeps a reference to the map and so the string array must not be deallocated during the life of the matrix. 
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\item[{Parameters}] \leavevmode\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{obj}} \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{} pointer to a button matrix object 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{map}} \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{} pointer a string array. The last string has to be: "". Use "\textbackslash{}n" to make a line break. 

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopmultiline
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the button control map (hidden, disabled etc.) for a button matrix. The control map array will be copied and so may be deallocated after this function returns. 
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\item[{Parameters}] \leavevmode\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{obj}} \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{} pointer to a button matrix object 

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ctrl\_map}} \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{} pointer to an array of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btn\_ctrl\_t}} control bytes. The length of the array and position of the elements must match the number and order of the individual buttons (i.e. excludes newline entries). An element of the map should look like e.g.: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ctrl\_map{[}0{]} = width | LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_NO\_REPEAT | LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_TGL\_ENABLE}} 

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{Canvas (lv\_canvas)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:canvas-lv-canvas}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A Canvas inherits from {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/img::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Image}}}} where the user can draw anything.
Rectangles, texts, images, lines, arcs can be drawn here using lvgl's drawing engine.
Additionally "effects" can be applied, such as rotation, zoom and blur.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} Uses the typical rectangle style properties and image style properties.


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:usage}}

\paragraph{Buffer}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:buffer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Canvas needs a buffer in which stores the drawn image.
To assign a buffer to a Canvas, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_set\_buffer(canvas, buffer, width, height, LV\_IMG\_CF\_...)}}.
Where  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{buffer}} is a static buffer (not just a local variable) to hold the image of the canvas.
For example,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{static lv\_color\_t buffer{[}LV\_CANVAS\_BUF\_SIZE\_TRUE\_COLOR(width, height){]}}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CANVAS\_BUF\_SIZE\_...}} macros help to determine the size of the buffer with different color formats.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The canvas supports all the built\sphinxhyphen{}in color formats like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_TRUE\_COLOR}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_INDEXED\_2BIT}}.
See the full list in the \sphinxhref{/overview/image.html\#color-formats}{Color formats} section.


\paragraph{Indexed colors}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:indexed-colors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_INDEXED\_1/2/4/8}} color formats a palette needs to be
initialized with  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_set\_palette(canvas, 3, LV\_COLOR\_RED)}}. It sets pixels with \sphinxstyleemphasis{index=3} to red.


\paragraph{Drawing}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:drawing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To set a pixel's color on the canvas, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_set\_px\_color(canvas, x, y, LV\_COLOR\_RED)}}.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_INDEXED\_...}}  the index of the color needs to be passed as color.
E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_color\_t c; c.full = 3;}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set a pixel's opacity with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_TRUE\_COLOR\_ALPHA}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_ALPHA\_...}} format on the canvas, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_set\_px\_opa(canvas, x, y, opa)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_fill\_bg(canvas, LV\_COLOR\_BLUE, LV\_OPA\_50)}} fills the whole canvas to blue with 50\% opacity. Note that if the current color format doesn't support colors (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_ALPHA\_2BIT}}) the color will be ignored.
Similarly, if opacity is not supported (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_TRUE\_COLOR}}) it will be ignored.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An array of pixels can be copied to the canvas with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_copy\_buf(canvas, buffer\_to\_copy, x, y, width, height)}}.
The color format of the buffer and the canvas need to match.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To draw something to the canvas use
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_draw\_rect(canvas, x, y, width, heigth, \&draw\_dsc)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_draw\_text(canvas, x, y, max\_width, \&draw\_dsc, txt)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_draw\_img(canvas, x, y, \&img\_src, \&draw\_dsc)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_draw\_line(canvas, point\_array, point\_cnt, \&draw\_dsc)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_draw\_polygon(canvas, points\_array, point\_cnt, \&draw\_dsc)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_draw\_arc(canvas, x, y, radius, start\_angle, end\_angle, \&draw\_dsc)}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_dsc}} is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_rect/label/img/line/arc\_dsc\_t}} variable which should be first initialized with one of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_draw\_rect/label/img/line/arc\_dsc\_init()}} and then modified with the desired colors and other values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The draw function can draw to any color format. For example, it's possible to draw a text to an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_VF\_ALPHA\_8BIT}} canvas and use the result image as a {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/drawing::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{draw mask}}}} later.


\paragraph{Transformations}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:transformations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_transform()}} can be used to rotate and/or scale the image of an image and store the result on the canvas.
The function needs the following parameters:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{canvas}} pointer to a canvas object to store the result of the transformation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{img pointer}} to an image descriptor to transform. Can be the image descriptor of another canvas too (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_get\_img()}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{angle}} the angle of rotation (0..3600), 0.1 deg resolution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{zoom}} zoom factor (256: no zoom, 512: double size, 128: half size);

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{offset\_x}} offset X to tell where to put the result data on destination canvas

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{offset\_y}} offset X to tell where to put the result data on destination canvas

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_x}} pivot X of rotation. Relative to the source canvas. Set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source width / 2}} to rotate around the center

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_y}} pivot Y of rotation. Relative to the source canvas. Set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source height / 2}} to rotate around the center

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{antialias}} true: apply anti\sphinxhyphen{}aliasing during the transformation. Looks better but slower.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that a canvas can't be rotated on itself.  You need a source and destination canvas or image.


\paragraph{Blur}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:blur}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A given area of the canvas can be blurred horizontally with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_blur\_hor(canvas, \&area, r)}} or vertically with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_blur\_ver(canvas, \&area, r)}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{r}} is the radius of the blur (greater value means more intensive burring). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area}} is the area where the blur should be applied (interpreted relative to the canvas).


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No special events are sent by canvas objects.
The same events are sent as for the

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/img::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Images}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:example}}

\paragraph{Drawing on the Canvas and rotate}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/canvas:drawing-on-the-canvas-and-rotate}}


\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}

\end{sphinxuseclass}

\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}CANVAS \PYGZam{}\PYGZam{} LV\PYGZus{}BUILD\PYGZus{}EXAMPLES}

\subsection{Checkbox (lv\_checkbox)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:checkbox-lv-checkbox}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Checkbox object is created from a "tick box" and a label. When the Checkbox is clicked the tick box is toggled.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The is the background of the Checkbox and it uses the text and all the typical background style properties.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_column}} adjusts the spacing between the tickbox and the label

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} The "tick box" is a square that uses all the typical background style properties.
By default, its size is equal to the height of the main part's font. Padding properties make the tick box larger in the respective directions.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Checkbox is added to the default group (if it is set).


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:usage}}

\paragraph{Text}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:text}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The text can be modified with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_checkbox\_set\_text(cb, "New text")}} function and will be dynamically allocated.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set a static text,
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_checkbox\_set\_static\_text(cb, txt)}}. This way, only a pointer to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{txt}} will be stored. The text then shouldn't be deallocated while the checkbox exists.


\paragraph{Check, uncheck, disable}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:check-uncheck-disable}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can manually check, un\sphinxhyphen{}check, and disable the Checkbox by using the common state add/clear function:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}CHECKED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}   \PYG{c+cm}{/*Make the chekbox checked*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}clear\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}CHECKED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*MAke the checkbox unchecked*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}CHECKED} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}STATE\PYGZus{}DISABLED}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*Make the checkbox checked and disabled*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when the checkbox is toggled.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}} are sent for the following types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHECKBOX\_DRAW\_PART\_BOX}} The tickbox of the checkbox
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: the area of the tickbox

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the 'Buttons':
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT/UP}} Go to toggled state if toggling is enabled

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT/DOWN}} Go to non\sphinxhyphen{}toggled state if toggling is  enabled

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} Clicks the checkbox and toggles it

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, as usual, the state of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} is translated to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_PRESSED/PRESSING/RELEASED}} etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:example}}

\paragraph{Simple Checkboxes}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/checkbox:simple-checkboxes}}
