\subsection{Drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list (lv\_dropdown)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:drop-down-list-lv-dropdown}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list allows the user to select one value from a list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list is closed by default and displays a single value or a predefined text.
When activated (by click on the drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list), a list is created from which the user may select one option.
When the user selects a new value, the list is deleted again.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list is added to the default group (if it is set). Besides the Drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list is an editable object to allow selecting an option with encoder navigation too.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Dropdown widget is built from the elements: "button" and "list" (both not related to the button and list widgets)


\paragraph{Button}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:button}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the button. Uses the typical background properties and text properties for the text on it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} Typically an arrow symbol that can be an image or a text (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The button goes to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_CHECKED}} when it's opened.


\paragraph{List}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:list}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The list itself. Uses the typical background properties. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_height}} can be used to limit the height of the list.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}} The scrollbar background, border, shadow properties and width (for its own width) and right padding for the spacing on the right.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SELECTED}} Refers to the currently pressed, checked or pressed+checked option. Also uses the typical background properties.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The list is hidden/shown on open/close. To add styles to it use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_get\_list(dropdown)}}  to get the list object. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t * list = lv\PYGZus{}dropdown\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}list(dropdown) /*Get the list*/
lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}style(list, \PYGZam{}my\PYGZus{}style, ...)           /*Add the styles to the list*/\PYGZcb{}`
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternatively the theme can be extended with the new styles.


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:usage}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:id1}}

\paragraph{Set options}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:set-options}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Options are passed to the drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list as a string with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_set\_options(dropdown, options)}}. Options should be separated by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}n}}. For example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"First\textbackslash{}nSecond\textbackslash{}nThird"}}. This string will be saved in the drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list, so it can in a local variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_add\_option(dropdown, "New option", pos)}} function inserts a new option to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pos}} index.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To save memory the options can set from a static(constant) string too with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_set\_options\_static(dropdown, options)}}.
In this case the options string should be alive while the drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list exists and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_add\_option}} can't be used

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can select an option manually with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_set\_selected(dropdown, id)}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} is the index of an option.


\paragraph{Get selected option}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:get-selected-option}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The get the \sphinxstyleemphasis{index} of the selected option, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_get\_selected(dropdown)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_get\_selected\_str(dropdown, buf, buf\_size)}} copies the \sphinxstyleemphasis{name} of the selected option to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{buf}}.


\paragraph{Direction}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:direction}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The list can be created on any side. The default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_BOTTOM}} can be modified by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_set\_dir(dropdown, LV\_DIR\_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/BOTTOM)}} function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the list would be vertically out of the screen, it will be aligned to the edge.


\paragraph{Symbol}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:symbol}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A symbol (typically an arrow) can be added to the dropdown list with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_set\_symbol(dropdown, LV\_SYMBOL\_...)}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the direction of the drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list is  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_LEFT}} the symbol will be shown on the left, otherwise on the right.


\paragraph{Show selected}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:show-selected}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The main part can either show the selected option or a static text. If a static is set with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_set\_text(dropdown, "Some text")}} it will be shown regardless to th selected option.
If the text is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} the selected option is displayed on the button.


\paragraph{Manually open/close}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:manually-open-close}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To manually open or close the drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_dropdown\_open/close(dropdown)}} function can be used.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apart from the \sphinxhref{../overview/event.html\#generic-events}{Generic events}, the following \sphinxhref{../overview/event.html\#special-events}{Special events} are sent by the drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when the new option is selected or the list is opened/closed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CANCEL}}  Sent when the list is closed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_READY}} Sent when the list is opened

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT/DOWN}} Select the next option.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT/UP}} Select the previous option.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LY\_KEY\_ENTER}} Apply the selected option (Sends \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} event and closes the drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:example}}

\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/dropdown:simple-drop-down-list}}

\subsection{Image (lv\_img)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:image-lv-img}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Images are the basic object to display images from flash (as arrays) or from files. Images can display symbols (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_...}}) too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the \sphinxhref{/overview/image.html\#image-decoder}{Image decoder interface} custom image formats can be supported as well.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} A background rectangle that uses the typical background style properties and the image itself using the image style properties.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:usage}}

\paragraph{Image source}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:image-source}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To provide maximum flexibility, the source of the image can be:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a variable in code (a C array with the pixels).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a file stored externally (e.g. on an SD card).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a text with {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/font::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Symbols}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set the source of an image, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_src(img, src)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To generate a pixel array from a PNG, JPG or BMP image, use the \sphinxhref{https://lvgl.io/tools/imageconverter}{Online image converter tool} and set the converted image with its pointer: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_src(img1, \&converted\_img\_var);}}
To make the variable visible in the C file, you need to declare it with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_DECLARE(converted\_img\_var)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To use external files, you also need to convert the image files using the online converter tool but now you should select the binary output format.
You also need to use LVGL's file system module and register a driver with some functions for the basic file operation. Go to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/file-system::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{File system}}}} to learn more.
To set an image sourced from a file, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_src(img, "S:folder1/my\_img.bin")}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also set a symbol similarly to {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Labels}}}}. In this case, the image will be rendered as text according to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{font} specified in the style.  It enables to use of light\sphinxhyphen{}weight monochrome "letters" instead of real images. You can set symbol like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_src(img1, LV\_SYMBOL\_OK)}}.


\paragraph{Label as an image}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:label-as-an-image}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Images and labels are sometimes used to convey the same thing. For example, to describe what a button does.
Therefore, images and labels are somewhat interchangeable, that is the images can display texts by using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_DUMMY}} as the prefix of the text. For example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_src(img, LV\_SYMBOL\_DUMMY "Some text")}}.


\paragraph{Transparency}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:transparency}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The internal (variable) and external images support 2 transparency handling methods:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Chroma\sphinxhyphen{}keying} \sphinxhyphen{} Pixels with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_CHROMA\_KEY}} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{lv\_conf.h}) color will be transparent.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alpha byte} \sphinxhyphen{} An alpha byte is added to every pixel that contains the pixel's opacity

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Palette and Alpha index}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:palette-and-alpha-index}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Besides the \sphinxstyleemphasis{True color} (RGB) color format, the following formats are supported:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Indexed} \sphinxhyphen{} Image has a palette.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alpha indexed} \sphinxhyphen{} Only alpha values are stored.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These options can be selected in the image converter. To learn more about the color formats, read the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/image::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Images}}}} section.


\paragraph{Recolor}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:recolor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A color can be mixed with every pixel of an image with a given intensity.
This can be useful to show different states (checked, inactive, pressed, etc.) of an image without storing more versions of the same image.
This feature can be enabled in the style by setting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{img\_recolor\_opa}} between \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_TRANSP}} (no recolor, value: 0) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_COVER}} (full recolor, value: 255).
The default value is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OPA\_TRANSP}} so this feature is disabled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The color to mix is set by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{img\_recolor}}.


\paragraph{Auto\sphinxhyphen{}size}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:auto-size}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the width or height of the image object is set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} the object's size will be set according to the size of the image source in the respective direction.


\paragraph{Mosaic}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:mosaic}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the object's size is greater than the image size in any directions, then the image will be repeated like a mosaic.
This allows creation a large image from only a very narrow source.
For example, you can have a \sphinxstyleemphasis{300 x 5} image with a special gradient and set it as a wallpaper using the mosaic feature.


\paragraph{Offset}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:offset}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_offset\_x(img, x\_ofs)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_offset\_y(img, y\_ofs)}}, you can add some offset to the displayed image.
Useful if the object size is smaller than the image source size.
Using the offset parameter a \sphinxhref{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texture\_atlas}{Texture atlas} or a "running image" effect can be created by {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/animation::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Animating}}}} the x or y offset.


\subsubsection{Transformations}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:transformations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_zoom(img, factor)}} the images will be zoomed. Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{256}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_ZOOM\_NONE}} to disable zooming.
A larger value enlarges the images (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{512}} double size), a smaller value shrinks it (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{128}} half size).
Fractional scale works as well. E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{281}} for 10\% enlargement.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To rotate the image use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_angle(img, angle)}}. Angle has 0.1 degree precision, so for 45.8° set 458.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform\_zoom}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform\_angle}} style properties are also used to determine the final zoom and angle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the pivot point of the rotation is the center of the image. It can be changed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_pivot(img, pivot\_x, pivot\_y)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0;0}} is the top left corner.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The quality of the transformation can be adjusted with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_antialias(img, true/false)}}. With enabled anti\sphinxhyphen{}aliasing the transformations are higher quality but slower.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The transformations require the whole image to be available. Therefore indexed images (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_INDEXED\_...}}), alpha only images (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_CF\_ALPHA\_...}}) or images from files can not be transformed.
In other words transformations work only on true color images stored as C array, or if a custom \sphinxhref{/overview/images\#image-edecoder}{Image decoder} returns the whole image.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the real coordinates of image objects won't change during transformation. That is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_get\_width/height/x/y()}} will return the original, non\sphinxhyphen{}zoomed coordinates.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{IMPORTANT}
The transformation of the image is independent of the transformation properties coming from styles. (See \sphinxhref{/overview/style\#opacity-and-transformations}{here}). The main differences are that pure image widget transformation
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
doesn't transform the children of the image widget

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
image is transformed directly without creating an intermediate layer (buffer) to snapshot the widget

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Size mode}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:size-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, when the image is zoomed or rotated the real coordinates of the image object are not changed.
The larger content simply overflows the object's boundaries.
It also means the layouts are not affected the by the transformations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you need the object size to be updated to the transformed size set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_size\_mode(img, LV\_IMG\_SIZE\_MODE\_REAL)}}. (The previous mode is the default and called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMG\_SIZE\_MODE\_VIRTUAL}}).
In this case if the width/height of the object is set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} the object's size will be set to the zoomed and rotated size.
If an explicit size is set then the overflowing content will be cropped.


\paragraph{Rounded image}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:rounded-image}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_style\_radius}} to set radius to an image, and enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_style\_clip\_corner}} to clip the
content to rounded rectangle or circular shape. Please note this will have some negative performance impact to CPU
based renderers.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No special events are sent by image objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:example}}

\paragraph{Image from variable and symbol}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/img:image-from-variable-and-symbol}}


\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}

\subsection{Label (lv\_label)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:label-lv-label}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A label is the basic object type that is used to display text.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}}  Uses all the typical background properties and the text properties.  The padding values can be used to add space between the text and the background.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}} The scrollbar that is shown when the text is larger than the widget's size.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SELECTED}} Tells the style of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/label:text-selection}]{\emph{selected text}}}. Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text\_color}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bg\_color}} style properties can be used.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:usage}}

\paragraph{Set text}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:set-text}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set the text on a label at runtime with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_text(label, "New text")}}.
This will allocate a buffer dynamically, and the provided string will be copied into that buffer.
Therefore, you don't need to keep the text you pass to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_text}} in scope after that function returns.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_text\_fmt(label, "Value: \%d", 15)}} printf formatting can be used to set the text.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Labels are able to show text from a static character buffer.  To do so, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_text\_static(label, "Text")}}.
In this case, the text is not stored in the dynamic memory and the given buffer is used directly instead.
This means that the array can't be a local variable which goes out of scope when the function exits.
Constant strings are safe to use with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_text\_static}} (except when used with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_DOT}}, as it modifies the buffer in\sphinxhyphen{}place), as they are stored in ROM memory, which is always accessible.


\paragraph{Newline}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:newline}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Newline characters are handled automatically by the label object. You can use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}n}} to make a line break. For example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"line1\textbackslash{}nline2\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nline4"}}


\paragraph{Long modes}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:long-modes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the width and height of the label is set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}}. Therefore, the size of the label is automatically expanded to the text size.
Otherwise, if the width or height are explicitly set (using  e.g.\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_width}} or a layout), the lines wider than the label's width can be manipulated according to several long mode policies.
Similarly, the policies can be applied if the height of the text is greater than the height of the label.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_WRAP}} Wrap too long lines. If the height is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} the label's height will be expanded, otherwise the text will be clipped. (Default)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_DOT}} Replaces the last 3 characters from bottom right corner of the label with dots (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_SCROLL}} If the text is wider than the label scroll it horizontally back and forth. If it's higher, scroll vertically. Only one direction is scrolled and horizontal scrolling has higher precedence.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_SCROLL\_CIRCULAR}} If the text is wider than the label scroll it horizontally continuously. If it's higher, scroll vertically. Only one direction is scrolled and horizontal scrolling has higher precedence.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_CLIP}} Simply clip the parts of the text outside the label.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the long mode with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_long\_mode(label, LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_...)}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_DOT}} manipulates the text buffer in\sphinxhyphen{}place in order to add/remove the dots.
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_text}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_array\_text}} are used, a separate buffer is allocated and this implementation detail is unnoticed.
This is not the case with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_text\_static}}. The buffer you pass to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_text\_static}} must be writable if you plan to use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_DOT}}.


\paragraph{Text recolor}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:text-recolor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the text, you can use commands to recolor parts of the text. For example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Write a \#ff0000 red\# word"}}.
This feature can be enabled individually for each label by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_set\_recolor()}} function,
recoloring is only supported when the text wrapped with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#\#ff0000 ... \#}}sintax is in one line,
it is not supported in wrapped text, see example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Line wrap, recoloring and scrolling}}.


\paragraph{Text selection}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:text-selection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If enabled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_TEXT\_SELECTION}} part of the text can be selected. It's similar to when you use your mouse on a PC to select a text.
The whole mechanism (click and select the text as you drag your finger/mouse) is implemented in {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}} and the Label widget only allows manual text selection with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_get\_text\_selection\_start(label, start\_char\_index)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_label\_get\_text\_selection\_start(label, end\_char\_index)}}.


\paragraph{Very long texts}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:very-long-texts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL can efficiently handle very long (e.g. > 40k characters) labels by saving some extra data (\textasciitilde{}12 bytes) to speed up drawing. To enable this feature, set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_TXT\_HINT   1}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.


\paragraph{Custom scrolling animations}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:custom-scrolling-animations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Some aspects of the scrolling animations in long modes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_SCROLL}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_SCROLL\_CIRCULAR}} can be customized by setting the animation property of a style, using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_set\_anim()}}.
Currently, only the start and repeat delay of the circular scrolling animation can be customized. If you need to customize another aspect of the scrolling animation, feel free to open an \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/issues}{issue on Github} to request the feature.


\paragraph{Symbols}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:symbols}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The labels can display symbols alongside letters (or on their own). Read the {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/font::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Font}}}} section to learn more about the symbols.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No special events are sent by the Label.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:example}}

\paragraph{Line wrap, recoloring and scrolling}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/label:line-wrap-recoloring-and-scrolling}}

\subsection{Line (lv\_line)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line:line-lv-line}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Line object is capable of drawing straight lines between a set of points.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} uses all the typical background properties and line style properties.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line:usage}}

\paragraph{Set points}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line:set-points}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The points have to be stored in an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_point\_t}} array and passed to the object by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_line\_set\_points(lines, point\_array, point\_cnt)}} function.


\paragraph{Auto\sphinxhyphen{}size}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line:auto-size}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the Line's width and height are set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}}. This means it will automatically set its size to fit all the points. If the size is set explicitly, parts on the line may not be visible.


\paragraph{Invert y}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line:invert-y}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{y == 0} point is in the top of the object. It might be counter\sphinxhyphen{}intuitive in some cases so the y coordinates can be inverted with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_line\_set\_y\_invert(line, true)}}. In this case,  \sphinxstyleemphasis{y == 0} will be the bottom of the object.
\sphinxstyleemphasis{y invert} is disabled by default.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the \sphinxhref{../overview/event.html\#generic-events}{Generic events} are sent by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/line:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Roller (lv\_roller)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller:roller-lv-roller}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Roller allows you to simply select one option from a list by scrolling.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the roller uses all the typical background properties and text style properties. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style\_text\_line\_space}} adjusts the space between the options.
When the Roller is scrolled and doesn't stop exactly on an option it will scroll to the nearest valid option automatically in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anim\_time}} milliseconds as specified in the style.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SELECTED}} The selected option in the middle. Besides the typical background properties it uses the text style properties to change the appearance of the text in the selected area.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller:usage}}

\paragraph{Set options}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller:set-options}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Options are passed to the Roller as a string with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_roller\_set\_options(roller, options, LV\_ROLLER\_MODE\_NORMAL/INFINITE)}}. The options should be separated by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}n}}. For example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"First\textbackslash{}nSecond\textbackslash{}nThird"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_ROLLER\_MODE\_INFINITE}} makes the roller circular.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can select an option manually with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_roller\_set\_selected(roller, id, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}}, where \sphinxstyleemphasis{id} is the index of an option.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the roller has a lot of options then especially in infinite mode the rendered options of the display might look scrambled. In this case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_LARGE\_COORD}} should be enabled in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}


\paragraph{Get selected option}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller:get-selected-option}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To get the \sphinxstyleemphasis{index} of the currently selected option use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_roller\_get\_selected(roller)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_roller\_get\_selected\_str(roller, buf, buf\_size)}} will copy the name of the selected option to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{buf}}.


\paragraph{Visible rows}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller:visible-rows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of visible rows can be adjusted with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_roller\_set\_visible\_row\_count(roller, num)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function calculates the height with the current style. If the font, line space, border width, etc. of the roller changes this function needs to be called again.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when a new option is selected.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/roller:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT/DOWN}} Select the next option

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT/UP}} Select the previous option

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LY\_KEY\_ENTER}} Apply the selected option (Send \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} event)

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Slider (lv\_slider)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:slider-lv-slider}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Slider object looks like a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/bar::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Bar}}}} supplemented with a knob. The knob can be dragged to set a value. Just like Bar, Slider can be vertical or horizontal.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the slider. Uses all the typical background style properties. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{padding}} makes the indicator smaller in the respective direction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} The indicator that shows the current state of the slider. Also uses all the typical background style properties.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_KNOB}} A rectangle (or circle) drawn at the current value. Also uses all the typical background properties to describe the knob(s). By default, the knob is square (with an optional corner radius) with side length equal to the smaller side of the slider. The knob can be made larger with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{padding}} values. Padding values can be asymmetric too.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:usage}}

\paragraph{Value and range}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:value-and-range}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To set an initial value use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_slider\_set\_value(slider, new\_value, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}}.  The animation time is set by the styles' \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anim\_time}} property.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To specify the range (min, max values), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_slider\_set\_range(slider, min , max)}} can be used.


\paragraph{Modes}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:modes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The slider can be one of the following modes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SLIDER\_MODE\_NORMAL}} A normal slider as described above

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SLIDER\_SYMMETRICAL}} Draw the indicator form the zero value to current value. Requires negative minimum range and positive maximum range.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SLIDER\_RANGE}} Allows setting the start value too by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_bar\_set\_start\_value(bar, new\_value, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}}. The start value has to be always smaller than the end value.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The mode can be changed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_slider\_set\_mode(slider, LV\_SLIDER\_MODE\_...)}}


\paragraph{Knob\sphinxhyphen{}only mode}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:knob-only-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normally, the slider can be adjusted either by dragging the knob, or by clicking on the slider bar.
In the latter case the knob moves to the point clicked and slider value changes accordingly. In some cases it is desirable to set the slider to react on dragging the knob only. This feature is enabled by adding the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_ADV\_HITTEST}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_flag(slider, LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_ADV\_HITTEST)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The extended click area (set by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_ext\_click\_area(slider, value)}}) increases to knob's click area.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent while the slider is being dragged or changed with keys. The event is sent continuously while the slider is being dragged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_RELEASED}} Sent when the slider has just been released.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}} are sent for the following parts.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SLIDER\_DRAW\_PART\_KNOB}} The main (right) knob of the slider
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_KNOB}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: area of the indicator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}: 0

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SLIDER\_DRAW\_PART\_KNOB}}  The left knob of the slider
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_KNOB}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: area of the indicator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}: 1

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/bar::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Bar}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_UP/RIGHT}} Increment the slider's value by 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_DOWN/LEFT}} Decrement the slider's value by 1

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:example}}

\paragraph{Simple Slider}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/slider:simple-slider}}

\subsection{Switch (lv\_switch)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/switch:switch-lv-switch}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/switch::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/switch:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Switch looks like a little slider and can be used to turn something on and off.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/switch:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the switch uses all the typical background style properties. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{padding}} makes the indicator smaller in the respective direction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} The indicator that shows the current state of the switch. Also uses all the typical background style properties.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_KNOB}} A rectangle (or circle) drawn at left or right side of the indicator. Also uses all the typical background properties to describe the knob(s). By default, the knob is square (with an optional corner radius) with side length equal to the smaller side of the slider. The knob can be made larger with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{padding}} values. Padding values can be asymmetric too.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/switch:usage}}

\paragraph{Change state}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/switch:change-state}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The switch uses the standard \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_CHECKED}} state.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To get the current state of the switch (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} being on), use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_has\_state(switch, LV\_STATE\_CHECKED)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_state(switch, LV\_STATE\_CHECKED)}} to turn it on, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_clear\_state(switch, LV\_STATE\_CHECKED)}} to turn it off.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/switch:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when the switch changes state.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/switch:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_UP/RIGHT}} Turns on the slider

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_DOWN/LEFT}} Turns off the slider

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} Toggles the switch

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/switch:example}}

\subsection{Table (lv\_table)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:table-lv-table}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tables, as usual, are built from rows, columns, and cells containing texts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Table object is very lightweight because only the texts are stored. No real objects are created for cells but they are just drawn on the fly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Table is added to the default group (if it is set). Besides the Table is an editable object to allow selecting a cell with encoder navigation too.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the table uses all the typical background style properties.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}} The cells of the table also use all the typical background style properties and the text properties.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:usage}}

\paragraph{Set cell value}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:set-cell-value}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The cells can store only text so numbers need to be converted to text before displaying them in a table.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_table\_set\_cell\_value(table, row, col, "Content")}}. The text is saved by the table so it can be even a local variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Line breaks can be used in the text like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Value\textbackslash{}n60.3"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
New rows and columns are automatically added is required


\paragraph{Rows and Columns}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:rows-and-columns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To explicitly set number of rows and columns use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_table\_set\_row\_cnt(table, row\_cnt)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_table\_set\_col\_cnt(table, col\_cnt)}}


\paragraph{Width and Height}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:width-and-height}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The width of the columns can be set with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_table\_set\_col\_width(table, col\_id, width)}}. The overall width of the Table object will be set to the sum of columns widths.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The height is calculated automatically from the cell styles (font, padding etc) and the number of rows.


\paragraph{Merge cells}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:merge-cells}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cells can be merged horizontally with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_table\_add\_cell\_ctrl(table, row, col, LV\_TABLE\_CELL\_CTRL\_MERGE\_RIGHT)}}. To merge more adjacent cells call this function for each cell.


\paragraph{Scroll}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:scroll}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the label's width or height is set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT}} that size will be used to show the whole table in the respective direction.
E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_size(table, LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT, LV\_SIZE\_CONTENT)}} automatically sets the table size to show all the columns and rows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the width or height is set to a smaller number than the "intrinsic" size then the table becomes scrollable.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when a new cell is selected with keys.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}} are sent for the following types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TABLE\_DRAW\_PART\_CELL}} The individual cells of the table
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: area of the indicator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}: current row × col count + current column

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the Tables:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT/LEFT/UP/DOWN/}} Select a cell.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, as usual, the state of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} is translated to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_PRESSED/PRESSING/RELEASED}} etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_table\_get\_selected\_cell(table, \&row, \&col)}} can be used to get the currently selected cell. Row and column will be set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TABLE\_CELL\_NONE}} no cell is selected.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/table:example}}

\paragraph{Simple table}

\subsection{Text area (lv\_textarea)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:text-area-lv-textarea}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Text Area is a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} with a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Label}}}} and a cursor on it.
Texts or characters can be added to it.
Long lines are wrapped and when the text becomes long enough the Text area can be scrolled.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One line mode and password modes are supported.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the text area. Uses all the typical background style properties and the text related style properties including \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text\_align}} to align the text to the left, right or center.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}} The scrollbar that is shown when the text is too long.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SELECTED}} Determines the style of the \sphinxhref{/widgets/core/label.html\#text-selection}{selected text}. Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text\_color}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bg\_color}} style properties can be used. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bg\_color}} should be set directly on the label of the text area.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_CURSOR}} Marks the position where the characters are inserted. The cursor's area is always the bounding box of the current character.
A block cursor can be created by adding a background color and background opacity to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_CURSOR}}'s style. The create line cursor leave the cursor transparent and set a left border.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anim\_time}} style property sets the cursor's blink time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_TEXTAREA\_PLACEHOLDER}} Unique to Text Area, allows styling the placeholder text.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:usage}}

\paragraph{Add text}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:add-text}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can insert text or characters to the current cursor's position with:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_add\_char(textarea, 'c')}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_add\_text(textarea, "insert this text")}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To add wide characters like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{'á'}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{'ß'}} or CJK characters use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_add\_text(ta, "á")}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_text(ta, "New text")}} changes the whole text.


\paragraph{Placeholder}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:placeholder}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A placeholder text can be specified \sphinxhyphen{} which is displayed when the Text area is empty \sphinxhyphen{} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_placeholder\_text(ta, "Placeholder text")}}


\paragraph{Delete character}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:delete-character}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To delete a character from the left of the current cursor position use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_del\_char(textarea)}}.
To delete from the right use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_del\_char\_forward(textarea)}}


\paragraph{Move the cursor}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:move-the-cursor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The cursor position can be modified directly like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_cursor\_pos(textarea, 10)}}.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} position means "before the first characters",
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TA\_CURSOR\_LAST}} means "after the last character"

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can step the cursor with
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_cursor\_right(textarea)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_cursor\_left(textarea)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_cursor\_up(textarea)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_cursor\_down(textarea)}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_cursor\_click\_pos(textarea, true)}} is applied the cursor will jump to the position where the Text area was clicked.


\paragraph{Hide the cursor}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:hide-the-cursor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The cursor is always visible, however it can be a good idea to style it to be visible only in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_STATE\_FOCUSED}} state.


\paragraph{One line mode}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:one-line-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Text area can be configured to be on a single line with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_one\_line(textarea, true)}}.
In this mode the height is set automatically to show only one line, line break characters are ignored, and word wrap is disabled.


\paragraph{Password mode}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:password-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The text area supports password mode which can be enabled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_password\_mode(textarea, true)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, if the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{•}} (\sphinxhref{http://www.fileformat.info/info/unicode/char/2022/index.htm}{Bullet, U+2022}) character exists in the font, the entered characters are converted to it after some time or when a new character is entered. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{•}} does not exist in the font, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}} will be used. You can override the default character with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_password\_bullet(textarea, "x")}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In password mode \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_get\_text(textarea)}} returns the actual text entered, not the bullet characters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The visibility time can be adjusted with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TEXTAREA\_DEF\_PWD\_SHOW\_TIME)}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.


\paragraph{Accepted characters}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:accepted-characters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set a list of accepted characters with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_accepted\_chars(textarea, "0123456789.+\sphinxhyphen{}")}}.
Other characters will be ignored.


\paragraph{Max text length}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:max-text-length}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The maximum number of characters can be limited with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_max\_length(textarea, max\_char\_num)}}


\paragraph{Very long texts}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:very-long-texts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If there is a very long text in the Text area (e.g. > 20k characters), scrolling and drawing might be slow.
However, by enabling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_TXT\_HINT   1}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} the performance can be hugely improved.
This will save some additional information about the label to speed up its drawing.
Using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LABEL\_LONG\_TXT\_HINT}} the scrolling and drawing will as fast as with "normal" short texts.


\paragraph{Select text}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:select-text}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any part of the text can be selected if enabled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_text\_selection(textarea, true)}}.
This works much like when you select text on your PC with your mouse.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_INSERT}} Sent right before a character or text is inserted.
The event parameter is the text about to be inserted. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_textarea\_set\_insert\_replace(textarea, "New text")}} replaces the text to insert.
The new text cannot be in a local variable which is destroyed when the event callback exists. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}} means do not insert anything.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when the content of the text area has been changed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_READY}} Sent when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} is pressed (or sent) to a one line text area.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT}} Move the cursor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Any character}} Add the character to the current cursor position

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:example}}

\label{\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea:simple-text-area}}

\section{Extra widgets}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Animation Image (lv\_animimg)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/animimg:animation-image-lv-animimg}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/animimg::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/animimg:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The animation image is similar to the normal 'Image' object. The only difference is that instead of one source image, you set an array of multiple source images.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify a duration and repeat count.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/animimg:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} A background rectangle that uses the typical background style properties and the image itself using the image style properties.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/animimg:usage}}

\paragraph{Image sources}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/animimg:image-sources}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To set the image in a state, use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_animimg\_set\_src(imgbtn, dsc{[}{]}, num)}}.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/animimg:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No special events are sent by image objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the Base object too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/animimg:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No Keys are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\subsection{Calendar (lv\_calendar)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:calendar-lv-calendar}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{From v8.1 the header is added directly into the Calendar widget and the API of the headers has been changed.}


\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Calendar object is a classic calendar which can:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
show the days of any month in a 7x7 matrix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Show the name of the days

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
highlight the current day (today)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
highlight any user\sphinxhyphen{}defined dates

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Calendar is added to the default group (if it is set). Calendar is an editable object which allow selecting and clicking the dates with encoder navigation too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To make the Calendar flexible, by default it doesn't show the current year or month. Instead, there are optional "headers" that can be attached to the calendar.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Calendar is composed of 3 widegets
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Container: A rectangle which is a container for the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Header} and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Days}. Uses only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} where all the background related style properties are working.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Days: It's a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Button matrix}}}} object under the hood to arrange the days into a matrix. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_get\_btnmatrix(calendar)}} can be used to get it.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the calendar. Uses all the background related style properties.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}} Refers to the dates and day names. Button matrix control flags are set to differentiate the buttons and a custom drawer event is added modify the properties of the buttons as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
day names have no border, no background and drawn with a gray color

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
days of the previous and next month have \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_DISABLED}} flag

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
today has a thicker border with the theme's primary color

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
highlighted days have some opacity with the theme's primary color.

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Header: Not created by default, the details are up to the given header.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Some functions use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_date\_t}} type which is a structure with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{year}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{month}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{day}} fields.


\paragraph{Current date}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:current-date}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To set the current date (today), use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_set\_today\_date(calendar, year, month, day)}} function. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{month}} needs to be in 1..12 range and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{day}} in 1..31 range.


\paragraph{Shown date}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:shown-date}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To set the shown date, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_set\_shown\_date(calendar, year, month)}};


\paragraph{Highlighted days}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:highlighted-days}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The list of highlighted dates should be stored in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_date\_t}} array loaded by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_set\_highlighted\_dates(calendar, highlighted\_dates, date\_num)}}.
Only the array's pointer will be saved so the array should be a static or global variable.


\paragraph{Name of the days}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:name-of-the-days}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The name of the days can be adjusted with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_set\_day\_names(calendar, day\_names)}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{day\_names}} looks like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char * day\_names{[}7{]} = \{"Su", "Mo", ...\};}}
Only the pointer of the day names is saved so the elements should be static, global or constant variables.


\paragraph{Custom year list}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:custom-year-list}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sets a custom year list with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_header\_dropdown\_set\_year\_list(calendar, years\_list)}}
where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{years\_list}} is a pointer to the custom years list. It can be a constant string
like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{static const char * years = "2023\textbackslash{}n2022\textbackslash{}n2021\textbackslash{}n2020\textbackslash{}n2019";}},
or can be generated dynamically into a buffer as well.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent if a date is clicked. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_get\_pressed\_date(calendar, \&date)}} set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date}} to the date currently being pressed. Returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_RES\_OK}} if there is a valid pressed date, else \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_RES\_INV}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT/UP/LEFT/RIGHT}} To navigate among the buttons to dates

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} To press/release the selected date

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Headers}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:headers}}

\paragraph{Arrow buttons}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:arrow-buttons}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_header\_arrow\_create(calendar)}} creates a header that contains a left and right arrow on the sides and a text with the current year and month between them.


\paragraph{Drop\sphinxhyphen{}down}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:drop-down}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_calendar\_header\_dropdown\_create(calendar)}} creates a header that contains 2 drop\sphinxhyphen{}drown lists: one for the year and another for the month.

\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/calendar:example}}
