\subsection{Chart (lv\_chart)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:chart-lv-chart}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Charts are a basic object to visualize data points. Currently \sphinxstyleemphasis{Line} charts (connect points with lines and/or draw points on them) and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bar} charts are supported.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Charts can have:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
division lines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2 y axis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
axis ticks and texts on ticks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cursors

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
scrolling and zooming

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the chart. Uses all the typical background and \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} (for the division lines) related style properties. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Padding} makes the series area smaller. For column charts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_column}} sets the space between the columns of the adjacent indices.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}} The scrollbar used if the chart is zoomed. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}}'s documentation for details.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}} Refers to the line or bar series.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line chart: The \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} properties are used by the lines. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{height}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bg\_color}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radius}} is used to set the appearance of points.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bar chart: The typical background properties are used to style the bars. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_column}} sets the space between the columns on the same index.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} Refers to the points on line and scatter chart (small circles or squares).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_CURSOR}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Line} properties are used to style the cursors.  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{height}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bg\_color}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radius}} are used to set the appearance of points.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_TICKS}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Line} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Text} style properties are used to style the ticks

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:usage}}

\paragraph{Chart type}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:chart-type}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following data display types exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_TYPE\_NONE}}  Do not display any data. Can be used to hide the series.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_TYPE\_LINE}}  Draw lines between the data points and/or points (rectangles or circles) on the data points.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_TYPE\_BAR}} \sphinxhyphen{} Draw bars.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_TYPE\_SCATTER}} \sphinxhyphen{} X/Y chart drawing point's and lines between the points. .

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the display type with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_type(chart, LV\_CHART\_TYPE\_...)}}.


\paragraph{Data series}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:data-series}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can add any number of series to the charts by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_add\_series(chart, color, axis)}}. This allocates an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_series\_t}} structure which contains the chosen \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color}} and an array for the data points.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} can have the following values:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_AXIS\_PRIMARY\_Y}} Left axis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_AXIS\_SECONDARY\_Y}} Right axis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_AXIS\_PRIMARY\_X}} Bottom axis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_AXIS\_SECONDARY\_X}} Top axis

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} tells which axis's range should be used te scale the values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_ext\_y\_array(chart, ser, value\_array)}} makes the chart use an external array for the given series.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_array}} should look like this: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_coord\_t * value\_array{[}num\_points{]}}}. The array size needs to be large enough to hold all the points of that series.
The array's pointer will be saved in the chart so it needs to be global, static or dynamically allocated.
Note: you should call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_refresh(chart)}} after the external data source has been updated to update the chart.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value array of a series can be obtained with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_get\_y\_array(chart, ser)}}, which can be used with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ext\_array}} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{normal array}s.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_TYPE\_SCATTER}} type  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_ext\_x\_array(chart, ser, value\_array)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_get\_x\_array(chart, ser)}} can be used as well.


\paragraph{Modify the data}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:modify-the-data}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You have several options to set the data of series:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the values manually in the array like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ser1\sphinxhyphen{}>points{[}3{]} = 7}} and refresh the chart with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_refresh(chart)}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_value\_by\_id(chart, ser, id, value)}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} is the index of the point you wish to update.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_next\_value(chart, ser, value)}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize all points to a given value with: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_all\_value(chart, ser, value)}}.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_POINT\_NONE}} as value to make the library skip drawing that point, column, or line segment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_TYPE\_SCATTER}} type  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_value\_by\_id2(chart, ser, id, value)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_next\_value2(chart, ser, x\_valuem y\_value)}} can be used as well.


\paragraph{Update modes}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:update-modes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_next\_value}} can behave in two ways depending on \sphinxstyleemphasis{update mode}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_UPDATE\_MODE\_SHIFT}} Shift old data to the left and add the new one to the right.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_UPDATE\_MODE\_CIRCULAR}} \sphinxhyphen{} Add the new data in circular fashion, like an ECG diagram.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The update mode can be changed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_update\_mode(chart, LV\_CHART\_UPDATE\_MODE\_...)}}.


\paragraph{Number of points}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:number-of-points}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of points in the series can be modified by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_point\_count(chart, point\_num)}}. The default value is 10.
Note: this also affects the number of points processed when an external buffer is assigned to a series, so you need to be sure the external array is large enough.


\subparagraph{Handling large number of points}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:handling-large-number-of-points}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On line charts, if the number of points is greater than the pixels horizontally, the Chart will draw only vertical lines to make the drawing of large amount of data effective.
If there are, let's say, 10 points to a pixel, LVGL searches the smallest and the largest value and draws a vertical lines between them to ensure no peaks are missed.


\paragraph{Vertical range}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:vertical-range}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify the minimum and maximum values in y\sphinxhyphen{}direction with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_range(chart, axis, min, max)}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} can be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_AXIS\_PRIMARY}} (left axis) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_AXIS\_SECONDARY}} (right axis).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value of the points will be scaled proportionally. The default range is: 0..100.


\paragraph{Division lines}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:division-lines}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of horizontal and vertical division lines can be modified by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_div\_line\_count(chart, hdiv\_num, vdiv\_num)}}.
The default settings are 3 horizontal and 5 vertical division lines.
If there is a visible border on a side and no padding on that side, the division line would be drawn on top of the border and therefore it won't be drawn.


\paragraph{Override default start point for series}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:override-default-start-point-for-series}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want a plot to start from a point other than the default which is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{point{[}0{]}}} of the series, you can set an alternative
index with the function \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_x\_start\_point(chart, ser, id)}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} is the new index position to start plotting from.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_UPDATE\_MODE\_SHIFT}} also changes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start\_point}}.


\paragraph{Tick marks and labels}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:tick-marks-and-labels}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ticks and labels can be added to the axis with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_axis\_tick(chart, axis, major\_len, minor\_len, major\_cnt, minor\_cnt, label\_en, draw\_size)}}.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} can be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_AXIS\_X/PRIMARY\_Y/SECONDARY\_Y}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{major\_len}} is the length of major ticks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{minor\_len}} is the length of minor ticks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{major\_cnt}} is the number of major ticks on the axis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{minor\_cnt}} in the number of minor ticks between two major ticks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_en}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: enable label drawing on major ticks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_size}} extra size required to draw the tick and labels (start with 20 px and increase if the ticks/labels are clipped)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Zoom}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:zoom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The chart can be zoomed independently in x and y directions with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_zoom\_x(chart, factor)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_zoom\_y(chart, factor)}}.
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor}} is 256 there is no zoom. 512 means double zoom, etc. Fractional values are also possible but < 256 value is not allowed.


\paragraph{Cursor}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:cursor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A cursor can be added with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_cursor\_t * c1 = lv\_chart\_add\_cursor(chart, color, dir);}}.
The possible values of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dir}}  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_NONE/RIGHT/UP/LEFT/DOWN/HOR/VER/ALL}} or their OR\sphinxhyphen{}ed values to tell in which direction(s) should the cursor be drawn.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_cursor\_pos(chart, cursor, \&point)}} sets the position of the cursor.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pos}} is a pointer to an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_point\_t}} variable. E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_point\_t point = \{10, 20\};}}. If the chart is scrolled the cursor will remain in the same place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_get\_point\_pos\_by\_id(chart, series, id, \&point\_out)}} gets the coordinate of a given point. It's useful to place the cursor at a given point.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_set\_cursor\_point(chart, cursor, series, point\_id)}} sticks the cursor at a point. If the point's position changes (new value or scrolling) the cursor will move with the point.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/chart:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when a new point is clicked pressed.  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_chart\_get\_pressed\_point(chart)}} returns the zero\sphinxhyphen{}based index of the pressed point.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}} are sent with the following types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_DRAW\_PART\_DIV\_LINE\_INIT}}  Used before/after drawn the div lines to add masks to any extra drawings. The following fields are set:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_dsc}}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_DRAW\_PART\_DIV\_LINE\_HOR}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_DRAW\_PART\_DIV\_LINE\_VER}} Used for each horizontal and vertical division lines.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}: index of the line

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p2}}: points of the line

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_dsc}}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_DRAW\_PART\_LINE\_AND\_POINT}} Used on line and scatter charts for lines and points.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}: index of the point

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}: value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}th point

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p2}}: points of the line

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: area of the point

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub\_part\_ptr}}: pointer to the series

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_DRAW\_PART\_BAR}} Used on bar charts for the rectangles.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}: index of the point

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}: value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}th point

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: area of the point

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}:

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub\_part\_ptr}}: pointer to the series

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_DRAW\_PART\_CURSOR}}  Used on cursor lines and points.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_CURSOR}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p2}}: points of the line

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: area of the points

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_DRAW\_PART\_TICK\_LABEL}}  Used on tick lines and labels.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_TICKS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}: axis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}: value of the tick

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} converted to decimal or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} for minor ticks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_dsc}},

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_dsc}},

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Color wheel (lv\_colorwheel)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:color-wheel-lv-colorwheel}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As its name implies \sphinxstyleemphasis{Color wheel} allows the user to select a color. The Hue, Saturation and Value of the color can be selected separately.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Long pressing the object, the color wheel will change to the next parameter of the color (hue, saturation or value). A double click will reset the current parameter.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arc\_width}} is used to set the width of the color wheel

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_KNOB}} A rectangle (or circle) drawn on the current value. It uses all the rectangle like style properties and padding to make it larger than the width of the arc.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:usage}}

\paragraph{Create a color wheel}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:create-a-color-wheel}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_colorwheel\_create(parent, knob\_recolor)}} creates a new color wheel. With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{knob\_recolor=true}} the knob's background color will be set to the current color.


\paragraph{Set color}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:set-color}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The color can be set manually with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_colorwheel\_set\_hue/saturation/value(colorwheel, x)}} or all at once with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_colorwheel\_set\_hsv(colorwheel, hsv)}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_colorwheel\_set\_color(colorwheel, rgb)}}


\paragraph{Color mode}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:color-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The current color mode can be manually selected with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_colorwheel\_set\_mode(colorwheel, LV\_COLORWHEEL\_MODE\_HUE/SATURATION/VALUE)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The color mode can be fixed (so as to not change with long press) using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_colorwheel\_set\_mode\_fixed(colorwheel, true)}}


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent if a new color is selected.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_UP}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT}} Increment the current parameter's value by 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_DOWN}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT}} Decrement the current parameter's value by 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} A long press will show the next mode. Double click to reset the current parameter.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:example}}

\paragraph{Simple Colorwheel}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/colorwheel:simple-colorwheel}}


\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}


\end{sphinxuseclass}

\subsection{Image button (lv\_imgbtn)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:image-button-lv-imgbtn}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Image button is very similar to the simple 'Button' object. The only difference is that it displays user\sphinxhyphen{}defined images in each state instead of drawing a rectangle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set a left, right and center image, and the center image will be repeated to match the width of the object.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} Refers to the image(s). If background style properties are used, a rectangle will be drawn behind the image button.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:usage}}

\paragraph{Image sources}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:image-sources}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To set the image in a state, use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_imgbtn\_set\_src(imgbtn, LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_..., src\_left, src\_center, src\_right)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The image sources work the same as described in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/img::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Image object}}}} except that "Symbols" are not supported by the Image button.
Any of the sources can \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The possible states are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_RELEASED}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_PRESSED}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_DISABLED}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_CHECKED\_RELEASED}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_CHECKED\_PRESSED}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_CHECKED\_DISABLED}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you set sources only in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_RELEASED}}, these sources will be used in other states too.
If you set e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_PRESSED}} they will be used in pressed state instead of the released images.


\paragraph{States}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:states}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead of the regular \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add/clear\_state()}} functions the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_imgbtn\_set\_state(imgbtn, LV\_IMGBTN\_STATE\_...)}} functions should be used to manually set a state.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when the button is toggled.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT/UP}}  Go to toggled state if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CHECKABLE}} is enabled.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT/DOWN}}  Go to non\sphinxhyphen{}toggled state if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CHECKABLE}} is enabled.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} Clicks the button

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:example}}

\paragraph{Simple Image button}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/imgbtn:simple-image-button}}

\subsection{Keyboard (lv\_keyboard)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:keyboard-lv-keyboard}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Keyboard object is a special {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Button matrix}}}} with predefined keymaps and other features to realize a virtual keyboard to write texts into a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}}.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarly to Button matrices Keyboards consist of 2 part:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The main part. Uses all the typical background properties

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}} The buttons. Also uses all typical background properties as well as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{text} properties.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:usage}}

\paragraph{Modes}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:modes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Keyboards have the following modes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEYBOARD\_MODE\_TEXT\_LOWER}}  Display lower case letters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEYBOARD\_MODE\_TEXT\_UPPER}}  Display upper case letters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEYBOARD\_MODE\_TEXT\_SPECIAL}} Display special characters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEYBOARD\_MODE\_NUMBER}} Display numbers, +/\sphinxhyphen{} sign, and decimal dot

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEYBOARD\_MODE\_USER\_1}} through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEYBOARD\_MODE\_USER\_4}} User\sphinxhyphen{}defined modes.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TEXT}} modes' layout contains buttons to change mode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set the mode manually, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_keyboard\_set\_mode(kb, mode)}}. The default mode is  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEYBOARD\_MODE\_TEXT\_UPPER}}.


\paragraph{Assign Text area}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:assign-text-area}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can assign a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}} to the Keyboard to automatically put the clicked characters there.
To assign the text area, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_keyboard\_set\_textarea(kb, ta)}}.


\paragraph{Key Popovers}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:key-popovers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To enable key popovers on press, like on common Android and iOS keyboards, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_keyboard\_set\_popovers(kb, true)}}. The default control maps are preconfigured to only show the popovers on keys that produce a symbol and not on e.g. space. If you use a custom keymap, set the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BTNMATRIX\_CTRL\_POPOVER}} flag for all keys that you want to show a popover.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that popovers for keys in the top row will draw outside the widget boundaries. To account for this, reserve extra free space on top of the keyboard or ensure that the keyboard is added \sphinxstyleemphasis{after} any widgets adjacent to its top boundary so that the popovers can draw over those.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The popovers currently are merely a visual effect and don't allow selecting additional characters such as accents yet.


\paragraph{New Keymap}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:new-keymap}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can specify a new map (layout) for the keyboard with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_keyboard\_set\_map(kb, map)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_keyboard\_set\_ctrl\_map(kb, ctrl\_map)}}.
Learn more about the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Button matrix}}}} object.
Keep in mind that using following keywords will have the same effect as with the original map:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_OK}} Apply.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_CLOSE}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_KEYBOARD}} Close.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_BACKSPACE}} Delete on the left.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_LEFT}} Move the cursor left.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_RIGHT}} Move the cursor right.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SYMBOL\_NEW\_LINE}} New line.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{"ABC"} Load the uppercase map.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{"abc"} Load the lower case map.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{"1\#"} Load the lower case map.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when the button is pressed/released or repeated after long press. The event data is set to the ID of the pressed/released button.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_READY}} \sphinxhyphen{} The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Ok} button is clicked.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CANCEL}} \sphinxhyphen{} The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Close} button is clicked.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The keyboard has a \sphinxstylestrong{default event handler} callback called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_keyboard\_def\_event\_cb}}, which handles the button pressing, map changing, the assigned text area, etc. You can remove it and replace it with a custom event handler if you wish.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In 8.0 and newer, adding an event handler to the keyboard does not remove the default event handler.
This behavior differs from v7, where adding an event handler would always replace the previous one.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_RIGHT/UP/LEFT/RIGHT}} To navigate among the buttons and select one.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} To press/release the selected button.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard:examples}}

\subsection{LED (lv\_led)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led:led-lv-led}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LEDs are rectangle\sphinxhyphen{}like (or circle) object whose brightness can be adjusted. With lower brightness the colors of the LED become darker.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LEDs have only one main part, called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LED\_PART\_MAIN}} and it uses all the typical background style properties.


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led:usage}}

\paragraph{Color}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led:color}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set the color of the LED with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_led\_set\_color(led, lv\_color\_hex(0xff0080))}}.
This will be used as background color, border color, and shadow color.


\paragraph{Brightness}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led:brightness}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set their brightness with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_led\_set\_bright(led, bright)}}. The brightness should be between 0 (darkest) and 255 (lightest).


\paragraph{Toggle}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led:toggle}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_led\_on(led)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_led\_off(led)}} to set the brightness to a predefined ON or OFF value. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_led\_toggle(led)}} toggles between the ON and OFF state.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}} is sent for the following types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_LED\_DRAW\_PART\_RECTANGLE}} The main rectangle. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_DRAW\_PART\_RECTANGLE}} is not sent by the base object.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rect\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_area}}: the area of the rectangle

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/led:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\subsection{List (lv\_list)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list:list-lv-list}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The List is basically a rectangle with vertical layout to which Buttons and Texts can be added


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Background}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The main part of the list that uses all the typical background properties

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_SCROLLBAR}} The scrollbar. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base objects}}}} documentation for details.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Buttons and Texts}
See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Button}}}}'s and {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Label}}}}'s documentation.


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list:usage}}

\paragraph{Buttons}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list:buttons}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_list\_add\_btn(list, icon, text)}} adds a full\sphinxhyphen{}width button with an icon \sphinxhyphen{} that can be an image or symbol \sphinxhyphen{} and a text.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The text starts to scroll horizontally if it's too long.


\paragraph{Texts}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list:texts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_list\_add\_text(list, text)}} adds a text.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No special events are sent by the List, but sent by the Button as usual.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/list:example}}

\subsection{Menu (lv\_menu)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:menu-lv-menu}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The menu widget can be used to easily create multi\sphinxhyphen{}level menus. It handles the traversal between pages automatically.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The menu widget is built from the following objects:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Main container: lv\_menu\_main\_cont
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Main header: lv\_menu\_main\_header\_cont
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Back btn: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_btn}}}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Back btn icon: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/img::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_img}}}}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Main page: lv\_menu\_page

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sidebar container: lv\_menu\_sidebar\_cont
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sidebar header: lv\_menu\_sidebar\_header\_cont
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Back btn: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_btn}}}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Back btn icon: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/img::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_img}}}}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sidebar page: lv\_menu\_page

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:usage}}

\paragraph{Create a menu}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:create-a-menu}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_create(parent)}} creates a new empty menu.


\paragraph{Header mode}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:header-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following header modes exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_MENU\_HEADER\_TOP\_FIXED}} Header is positioned at the top.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_MENU\_HEADER\_TOP\_UNFIXED}} Header is positioned at the top and can be scrolled out of view.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_MENU\_HEADER\_BOTTOM\_FIXED}} Header is positioned at the bottom.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set header modes with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_set\_mode\_header(menu, LV\_MENU\_HEADER...)}}.


\paragraph{Root back button mode}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:root-back-button-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following root back button modes exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_MENU\_ROOT\_BACK\_BTN\_DISABLED}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_MENU\_ROOT\_BACK\_BTN\_ENABLED}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can set root back button modes with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_set\_mode\_root\_back\_btn(menu, LV\_MENU\_ROOT\_BACK\_BTN...)}}.


\paragraph{Create a menu page}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:create-a-menu-page}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_page\_create(menu, title)}} creates a new empty menu page.
You can add any widgets to the page.


\paragraph{Set a menu page in the main area}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:set-a-menu-page-in-the-main-area}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Once a menu page has been created, you can set it to the main area with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_set\_page(menu, page)}}. NULL to clear main and clear menu history.


\paragraph{Set a menu page in the sidebar}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:set-a-menu-page-in-the-sidebar}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Once a menu page has been created, you can set it to the sidebar with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_set\_sidebar\_page(menu, page)}}. NULL to clear sidebar.


\paragraph{Linking between menu pages}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:linking-between-menu-pages}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For instance, you have created a btn obj in the main page. When you click the btn obj, you want it to open up a new page, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_set\_load\_page\_event(menu, obj, new page)}}.


\paragraph{Create a menu container, section, separator}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:create-a-menu-container-section-separator}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following objects can be created so that it is easier to style the menu:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_cont\_create(parent page)}} creates a new empty container.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_section\_create(parent page)}} creates a new empty section.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_separator\_create(parent page)}} creates a separator.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when a page is shown.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_get\_cur\_main\_page(menu)}} returns a pointer to menu page that is currently displayed in main.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_get\_cur\_sidebar\_page(menu)}} returns a pointer to menu page that is currently displayed in sidebar.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_CLICKED}} Sent when a back btn in a header from either main or sidebar is clicked. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_EVENT\_BUBBLE}} is enabled on the buttons so you can add events to the menu itself.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_menu\_back\_btn\_is\_root(menu, btn)}} to check if btn is root back btn

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No keys are handled by the menu widget.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/menu:example}}

\subsection{Meter (lv\_meter)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:meter-lv-meter}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Meter widget can visualize data in very flexible ways. It can show arcs, needles, ticks lines and labels.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The background of the Meter. Uses the typical background properties.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_TICKS}} The tick lines a labels using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{text} style properties.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_INDICATOR}} The needle line or image using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{line} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{img} style properties, as well as the background properties to draw a square (or circle) on the pivot of the needles. Padding makes the square larger.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}} The arcs using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{arc} properties.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:usage}}

\paragraph{Add a scale}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:add-a-scale}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
First a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Scale} needs to be added to the Meter with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_scale\_t * scale = lv\_meter\_add\_scale(meter)}}.
The Scale has minor and major ticks and labels on the major ticks. Later indicators (needles, arcs, tick modifiers) can be added to the meter

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any number of scales can be added to Meter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The minor tick lines can be configured with: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_set\_scale\_ticks(meter, scale, tick\_count, line\_width, tick\_length, tick\_color)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To add major tick lines use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_set\_scale\_major\_ticks(meter, scale, nth\_major, tick\_width, tick\_length, tick\_color, label\_gap)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nth\_major}} to specify how many minor ticks to skip to draw a major tick.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Labels are added automatically on major ticks with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_gap}} distance from the ticks with text proportionally to the values of the tick line.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_set\_scale\_range(meter, scale, min, max, angle\_range, rotation)}} sets the value and angle range of the scale.


\paragraph{Add indicators}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:add-indicators}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Indicators need to be added to a Scale and their value is interpreted in the range of the Scale.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All the indicator add functions return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_indicator\_t *}}.


\subparagraph{Needle line}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:needle-line}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indic = lv\_meter\_add\_needle\_line(meter, scale, line\_width, line\_color, r\_mod)}} adds a needle line to a Scale. By default, the length of the line is the same as the scale's radius but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{r\_mod}} changes the length.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_set\_indicator\_value(meter, indic, value)}} sets the value of the indicator.


\subparagraph{Needle image}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:needle-image}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indic = lv\_meter\_add\_needle\_img(meter, scale, img\_src, pivot\_x, pivot\_y)}} sets an image that will be used as a needle. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{img\_src}} should be a needle pointing to the right like this \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}O\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}>}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_x}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_y}} sets the pivot point of the rotation relative to the top left corner of the image.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_set\_indicator\_value(meter, inidicator, value)}} sets the value of the indicator.


\subparagraph{Arc}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:arc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indic = lv\_meter\_add\_arc(meter, scale, arc\_width, arc\_color, r\_mod)}} adds an arc indicator. By default, the radius of the arc is the same as the scale's radius but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{r\_mod}} changes the radius.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_set\_indicator\_start\_value(meter, indic, value)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_set\_indicator\_end\_value(meter, inidicator, value)}} sets the value of the indicator.


\subparagraph{Scale lines (ticks)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:scale-lines-ticks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indic = lv\_meter\_add\_scale\_lines(meter, scale, color\_start, color\_end, local, width\_mod)}} adds an indicator that modifies the ticks lines.
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{local}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} the ticks' color will be faded from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_start}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_end}} in the indicator's  start and end value range.
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{local}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_start}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_end}} will be mapped to the start and end value of the scale and only a "slice" of that color gradient will be visible in the indicator's start and end value range.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width\_mod}} modifies the width of the tick lines.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_set\_indicator\_start\_value(meter, inidicator, value)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter\_set\_indicator\_end\_value(meter, inidicator, value)}} sets the value of the indicator.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_BEGIN}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_DRAW\_PART\_END}} is sent for the following types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_METER\_DRAW\_PART\_ARC}} The arc indicator
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub\_part\_ptr}}: pointer to the indicator

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arc\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radius}}: radius of the arc

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p1}} center of the arc

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_METER\_DRAW\_PART\_NEEDLE\_LINE}} The needle lines
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p2}} points of the line

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub\_part\_ptr}}: pointer to the indicator

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_METER\_DRAW\_PART\_NEEDLE\_IMG}}  The needle images
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_ITEMS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p2}} points of the line

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{img\_dsc}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub\_part\_ptr}}: pointer to the indicator

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_METER\_DRAW\_PART\_TICK}} The tick lines and labels
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_TICKS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}: the value of the line

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} converted to decimal or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} on minor lines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_dsc}}: label draw descriptor or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} on minor lines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_dsc}}:

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}: the index of the line

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Base object}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/meter:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No keys are handled by the Meter widget.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\subsection{Message box (lv\_msgbox)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:message-box-lv-msgbox}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Message boxes act as pop\sphinxhyphen{}ups.
They are built from a background container, a title, an optional close button, a text and optional buttons.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The text will be broken into multiple lines automatically and the height will be set automatically to include the text and the buttons.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The message box can be modal (blocking clicks on the rest of the screen) or not modal.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The message box is built from other widgets, so you can check these widgets' documentation for details.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Background: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Close button: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_btn}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Title and text: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_label}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Buttons: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_btnmatrix}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:usage}}

\paragraph{Create a message box}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:create-a-message-box}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msgbox\_create(parent, title, txt, btn\_txts{[}{]}, add\_close\_btn)}} creates a message box.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parent}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} the message box will be modal. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{title}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{txt}} are strings for the title and the text.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{btn\_txts{[}{]}}} is an array with the buttons' text. E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char * btn\_txts{[}{]} = \{"Ok", "Cancel", NULL\}}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_close\_btn}} can be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} to add/don't add a close button.


\paragraph{Get the parts}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:get-the-parts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The building blocks of the message box can be obtained using the following functions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n+nf}{lv\PYGZus{}msgbox\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}title}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{mbox}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n+nf}{lv\PYGZus{}msgbox\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}close\PYGZus{}btn}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{mbox}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n+nf}{lv\PYGZus{}msgbox\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{mbox}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n+nf}{lv\PYGZus{}msgbox\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}btns}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{mbox}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Close the message box}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:close-the-message-box}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msgbox\_close(msgbox)}} closes (deletes) the message box.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} is sent by the buttons if one of them is clicked. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_EVENT\_BUBBLE}} is enabled on the buttons so you can add events to the message box itself.
In the event handler, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_target(e)}} will return the button matrix and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_event\_get\_current\_target(e)}} will return the message box. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msgbox\_get\_active\_btn(msgbox)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msgbox\_get\_active\_btn\_text(msgbox)}} can be used to get the index and text of the clicked button.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keys have effect on the close button and button matrix. You can add them manually to a group if required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/msgbox:example}}

\subsection{Span (lv\_span)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:span-lv-span}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A spangroup is the object that is used to display rich text. Different from the label object, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{spangroup}} can render text styled with different fonts, colors, and sizes into the spangroup object.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:parts-and-styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_PART\_MAIN}} The spangroup has only one part.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:usage}}

\paragraph{Set text and style}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:set-text-and-style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The spangroup object uses span to describe text and text style. so, first we need to create \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{span}} descriptor using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_span\_t * span = lv\_spangroup\_new\_span(spangroup)}}. Then use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_span\_set\_text(span, "text")}} to set text. The style of the span is configured as with a normal style object by using its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{style}} member, eg:\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_set\_text\_color(\&span\sphinxhyphen{}>style, lv\_palette\_main(LV\_PALETTE\_RED))}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If spangroup object \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode != LV\_SPAN\_MODE\_FIXED}} you must call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spangroup\_refr\_mode()}} after you have modified \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{span}} style(eg:set text, changed the font size, del span).


\paragraph{Retrieving a span child}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:retrieving-a-span-child}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Spangroups store their children differently from normal objects, so normal functions for getting children won't work.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spangroup\_get\_child(spangroup, id)}} will return a pointer to the child span at index \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}. In addition, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} can be negative to index from the end of the spangroup where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} is the youngest child, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}} is second youngest, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_span\_t* span = lv\_spangroup\_get\_child(spangroup, 0)}} will return the first child of the spangroup. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_span\_t* span = lv\_spangroup\_get\_child(spangroup, \sphinxhyphen{}1)}} will return the last (or most recent) child.


\paragraph{Child Count}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:child-count}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the function \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spangroup\_get\_child\_cnt(spangroup)}} to get back the number of spans the group is maintaining.

\sphinxAtStartPar
e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uint32\_t size = lv\_spangroup\_get\_child\_cnt(spangroup)}}


\paragraph{Text align}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:text-align}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
like label object, the spangroup can be set to one the following modes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TEXT\_ALIGN\_LEFT}} Align text to left.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TEXT\_ALIGN\_CENTER}} Align text to center.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TEXT\_ALIGN\_RIGHT}} Align text to right.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TEXT\_ALIGN\_AUTO}} Align text auto.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
use function \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spangroup\_set\_align(spangroup, LV\_TEXT\_ALIGN\_CENTER)}} to set text align.


\paragraph{Modes}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:modes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The spangroup can be set to one of the following modes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SPAN\_MODE\_FIXED}} fixes the object size.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SPAN\_MODE\_EXPAND}} Expand the object size to the text size but stay on a single line.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SPAN\_MODE\_BREAK}} Keep width, break the too long lines and auto expand height.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spangroup\_set\_mode(spangroup, LV\_SPAN\_MODE\_BREAK)}} to set object mode.


\paragraph{Overflow}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:overflow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The spangroup can be set to one of the following modes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SPAN\_OVERFLOW\_CLIP}} truncates the text at the limit of the area.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_SPAN\_OVERFLOW\_ELLIPSIS}} will display an ellipsis(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{...}}) when text overflows the area.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spangroup\_set\_overflow(spangroup, LV\_SPAN\_OVERFLOW\_CLIP)}} to set object overflow mode.


\paragraph{first line indent}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:first-line-indent}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spangroup\_set\_indent(spangroup, 20)}} to set the indent of the first line. All modes support pixel units, in addition to LV\_SPAN\_MODE\_FIXED and LV\_SPAN\_MODE\_BREAK mode supports percentage units too.


\paragraph{lines}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:lines}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spangroup\_set\_lines(spangroup, 10)}} to set the maximum number of lines to be displayed in LV\_SPAN\_MODE\_BREAK mode, negative values indicate no limit.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No special events are sent by this widget.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:example}}

\paragraph{Span with custom styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/span:span-with-custom-styles}}


\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}

\subsection{Spinbox (lv\_spinbox)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinbox:spinbox-lv-spinbox}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinbox::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinbox:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Spinbox contains a number as text which can be increased or decreased by \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} or API functions.
Under the hood the Spinbox is a modified {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}}.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinbox:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The parts of the Spinbox are identical to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}}.


\paragraph{Value, range and step}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinbox:value-range-and-step}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_set\_value(spinbox, 1234)}} sets a new value on the Spinbox.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_increment(spinbox)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_decrement(spinbox)}} increments/decrements the value of the Spinbox according to the currently selected digit.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_set\_range(spinbox, \sphinxhyphen{}1000, 2500)}} sets a range. If the value is changed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_set\_value}}, by \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys},\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_increment/decrement}} this range will be respected.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_set\_step(spinbox, 100)}} sets which digits to change on increment/decrement. Only multiples of ten can be set, and not for example 3.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_set\_cursor\_pos(spinbox, 1)}} sets the cursor to a specific digit to change on increment/decrement. For example position '0' sets the cursor to the least significant digit.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If an encoder is used as input device, the selected digit is shifted to the right by default whenever the encoder button is clicked. To change this behaviour to shifting to the left, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_set\_digit\_step\_direction(spinbox, LV\_DIR\_LEFT)}} can be used


\paragraph{Format}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinbox:format}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_set\_digit\_format(spinbox, digit\_count, separator\_position)}} sets the number format. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{digit\_count}} is the number of digits excluding the decimal separator and the sign.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator\_position}} is the number of digits before the decimal point. If 0, no decimal point is displayed.


\paragraph{Rollover}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinbox:rollover}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinbox\_set\_rollover(spinbox, true/false)}} enables/disabled rollover mode. If either the minimum or maximum value is reached with rollover enabled, the value will change to the other limit. If rollover is disabled the value will remain at the minimum or maximum value.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinbox:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when the value has changed.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/textarea::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Text area}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinbox:keys}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_LEFT/RIGHT}} With \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keypad} move the cursor left/right. With \sphinxstyleemphasis{Encoder} decrement/increment the selected digit.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_UP/DOWN}} With \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keypad} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Encoder} increment/decrement the value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_ENTER}} With \sphinxstyleemphasis{Encoder} got the next digit. Jump to the first after the last.

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Spinner (lv\_spinner)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinner:spinner-lv-spinner}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinner::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinner:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Spinner object is a spinning arc over a ring.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinner:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The parts are identical to the parts of {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/arc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_arc}}}}.


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinner:usage}}

\paragraph{Create a spinner}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinner:create-a-spinner}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To create a spinner use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_spinner\_create(parent, spin\_time, arc\_length)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{spin time}} sets the spin time in milliseconds, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arc\_length}} sets the length of the spinning arc in degrees.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinner:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No special events are sent by the Spinner.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the events of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/arc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Arc}}}} too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/spinner:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are processed by the object type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\subsection{Tabview (lv\_tabview)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:tabview-lv-tabview}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Tab view object can be used to organize content in tabs.
The Tab view is built from other widgets:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Main container: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tab buttons: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_btnmatrix}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Container for the tabs: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Content of the tabs: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The tab buttons can be positioned on the top, bottom, left and right side of the Tab view.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A new tab can be selected either by clicking on a tab button or by sliding horizontally on the content.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are no special parts on the Tab view but the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_btnnmatrix}} widgets are used to create the Tab view.


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:usage}}

\paragraph{Create a Tab view}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:create-a-tab-view}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tabview\_create(parent, tab\_pos, tab\_size);}} creates a new empty Tab view.  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tab\_pos}} can be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_TOP/BOTTOM/LEFT/RIGHT}} to position the tab buttons to a side.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tab\_size}} is the height (in case of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_TOP/BOTTOM}}) or width (in case of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_LEFT/RIGHT}}) tab buttons.


\paragraph{Add tabs}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:add-tabs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
New tabs can be added with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tabview\_add\_tab(tabview, "Tab name")}}. This will return a pointer to an {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}} object where the tab's content can be created.


\paragraph{Rename tabs}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:rename-tabs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A tab can be renamed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tabview\_rename\_tab(tabview, tab\_id, "New Name")}}.


\paragraph{Change tab}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:change-tab}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To select a new tab you can:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Click on its tab button

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Slide horizontally

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tabview\_set\_act(tabview, id, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}} function

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Get the parts}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:get-the-parts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tabview\_get\_content(tabview)}} returns the container for the tabs, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tabview\_get\_tab\_btns(tabview)}} returns the Tab buttons object which is a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btnmatrix::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Button matrix}}}}.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when a new tab is selected by sliding or clicking the tab button. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tabview\_get\_tab\_act(tabview)}} returns the zero based index of the current tab.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tabview:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keys have effect only on the tab buttons (Button matrix). Add manually to a group if required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\subsection{Tile view (lv\_tileview)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:tile-view-lv-tileview}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Tile view is a container object whose elements (called \sphinxstyleemphasis{tiles}) can be arranged in grid form.
A user can navigate between the tiles by swiping.
Any direction of swiping can be disabled on the tiles individually to not allow moving from one tile to another.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the Tile view is screen sized, the user interface resembles what you may have seen on smartwatches.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Tile view is built from an {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}} container and {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}} tiles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parts and styles work the same as for {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}}.


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:usage}}

\paragraph{Add a tile}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:add-a-tile}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tileview\_add\_tile(tileview, row\_id, col\_id, dir)}} creates a new tile on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{row\_id}}th row and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{col\_id}}th column.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dir}} can be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_DIR\_LEFT/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM/HOR/VER/ALL}} or OR\sphinxhyphen{}ed values to enable moving to the adjacent tiles into the given direction by swiping.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned value is an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_t *}} on which the content of the tab can be created.


\paragraph{Change tile}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:change-tile}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Tile view can scroll to a tile with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_tile(tileview, tile\_obj, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF)}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_tile\_id(tileviewv, col\_id, row\_id, LV\_ANIM\_ON/OFF);}}


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_VALUE\_CHANGED}} Sent when a new tile loaded by scrolling. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tileview\_get\_tile\_act(tabview)}} can be used to get current tile.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are not handled by the Tile view.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:example}}

\paragraph{Tileview with content}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/tileview:tileview-with-content}}
