\subsection{Window (lv\_win)}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:window-lv-win}}\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win::doc}}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Window is container\sphinxhyphen{}like object built from a header with title and buttons and a content area.


\subsubsection{Parts and Styles}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:parts-and-styles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Window is built from other widgets so you can check their documentation for details:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Background: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Header on the background: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Title on the header: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_label}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Buttons on the header: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/core/btn::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_btn}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Content area on the background: {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/obj::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_obj}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:usage}}

\paragraph{Create a Window}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:create-a-window}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_win\_create(parent, header\_height)}} creates a Window with an empty header.


\paragraph{Title and buttons}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:title-and-buttons}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any number of texts (but typically only one) can be added to the header with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_win\_add\_title(win, "The title")}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Control buttons can be added to the window's header with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_win\_add\_btn(win, icon, btn\_width)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{icon}} can be any image source, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{btn\_width}} is the width of the button.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The title and the buttons will be added in the order the functions are called. So adding a button, a text and two other buttons will result in a button on the left, a title, and 2 buttons on the right.
The width of the title is set to take all the remaining space on the header. In other words: it pushes to the right all the buttons that are added after the title.


\subsubsection{Get the parts}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:get-the-parts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_win\_get\_header(win)}} returns a pointer to the header, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_win\_get\_content(win)}} returns a pointer to the content container to which the content of the window can be added.


\subsubsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No special events are sent by the windows, however events can be added manually to the return value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_win\_add\_btn}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/event::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Events}}}}.


\subsubsection{Keys}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:keys}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxstyleemphasis{Keys} are handled by the window.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Learn more about {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.


\subsubsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:example}}

\paragraph{Simple window}
\label{\detokenize{widgets/extra/win:simple-window}}

\chapter{Layouts}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/index:layouts}}\label{\detokenize{layouts/index::doc}}
\sphinxstepscope


\section{Flex}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:flex}}\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex::doc}}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Flexbox (or Flex for short) is a subset of \sphinxhref{https://css-tricks.com/snippets/css/a-guide-to-flexbox/}{CSS Flexbox}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It can arrange items into rows or columns (tracks), handle wrapping, adjust the spacing between the items and tracks, handle \sphinxstyleemphasis{grow} to make the item(s) fill the remaining space with respect to min/max width and height.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To make an object flex container call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_layout(obj, LV\_LAYOUT\_FLEX)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the flex layout feature of LVGL needs to be globally enabled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_FLEX}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.


\subsection{Terms}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:terms}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tracks: the rows or columns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
main direction: row or column, the direction in which the items are placed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cross direction: perpendicular to the main direction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wrap: if there is no more space in the track a new track is started

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
grow: if set on an item it will grow to fill the remaining space on the track.
The available space will be distributed among items respective to their grow value (larger value means more space)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gap: the space between the rows and columns or the items on a track

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Simple interface}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:simple-interface}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
With the following functions you can set a Flex layout on any parent.


\subsubsection{Flex flow}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:flex-flow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_flex\_flow(obj, flex\_flow)}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The possible values for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flex\_flow}} are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_FLOW\_ROW}} Place the children in a row without wrapping

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_FLOW\_COLUMN}} Place the children in a column without wrapping

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_FLOW\_ROW\_WRAP}} Place the children in a row with wrapping

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_FLOW\_COLUMN\_WRAP}} Place the children in a column with wrapping

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_FLOW\_ROW\_REVERSE}} Place the children in a row without wrapping but in reversed order

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_FLOW\_COLUMN\_REVERSE}} Place the children in a column without wrapping but in reversed order

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_FLOW\_ROW\_WRAP\_REVERSE}} Place the children in a row with wrapping but in reversed order

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_FLOW\_COLUMN\_WRAP\_REVERSE}} Place the children in a column with wrapping but in reversed order

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Flex align}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:flex-align}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To manage the placement of the children use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_flex\_align(obj,  main\_place, cross\_place, track\_cross\_place)}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{main\_place}} determines how to distribute the items in their track on the main axis. E.g. flush the items to the right on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_FLOW\_ROW\_WRAP}}.  (It's called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{justify\sphinxhyphen{}content}} in CSS)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cross\_place}} determines how to distribute the items in their track on the cross axis. E.g. if the items have different height place them to the bottom of the track.  (It's called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align\sphinxhyphen{}items}} in CSS)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{track\_cross\_place}} determines how to distribute the tracks (It's called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align\sphinxhyphen{}content}} in CSS)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The possible values are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_ALIGN\_START}} means left on a horizontally and top vertically. (default)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_ALIGN\_END}} means right on a horizontally and bottom vertically

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_ALIGN\_CENTER}} simply center

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_ALIGN\_SPACE\_EVENLY}} items are distributed so that the spacing between any two items (and the space to the edges) is equal. Does not apply to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{track\_cross\_place}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_ALIGN\_SPACE\_AROUND}} items are evenly distributed in the track with equal space around them.
Note that visually the spaces aren’t equal, since all the items have equal space on both sides.
The first item will have one unit of space against the container edge, but two units of space between the next item because that next item has its own spacing that applies. Not applies to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{track\_cross\_place}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_ALIGN\_SPACE\_BETWEEN}} items are evenly distributed in the track: first item is on the start line, last item on the end line. Not applies to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{track\_cross\_place}}.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Flex grow}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:flex-grow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flex grow can be used to make one or more children fill the available space on the track. When more children have grow parameters, the available space will be distributed proportionally to the grow values.
For example, there is 400 px remaining space and 4 objects with grow:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}} with grow = 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B}} with grow = 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}} with grow = 2

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B}} will have 100 px size, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}} will have 200 px size.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Flex grow can be set on a child with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_flex\_grow(child, value)}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} needs to be > 1 or 0 to disable grow on the child.


\subsection{Style interface}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:style-interface}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All the Flex\sphinxhyphen{}related values are style properties under the hood and you can use them similarly to any other style property. The following flex related style properties exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FLEX\_FLOW}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FLEX\_MAIN\_PLACE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FLEX\_CROSS\_PLACE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FLEX\_TRACK\_PLACE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FLEX\_GROW}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Internal padding}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:internal-padding}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To modify the minimum space flexbox inserts between objects, the following properties can be set on the flex container style:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_row}} Sets the padding between the rows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_column}} Sets the padding between the columns.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These can for example be used if you don't want any padding between your objects: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_style\_set\_pad\_column(\&row\_container\_style,0)}}


\subsection{Other features}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:other-features}}

\subsubsection{RTL}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:rtl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the base direction of the container is set the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BASE\_DIR\_RTL}} the meaning of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_ALIGN\_START}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLEX\_ALIGN\_END}} is swapped on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ROW}} layouts. I.e. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{START}} will mean right.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The items on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ROW}} layouts, and tracks of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{COLUMN}} layouts will be placed from right to left.


\subsubsection{New track}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:new-track}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can force Flex to put an item into a new line with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_add\_flag(child, LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_FLEX\_IN\_NEW\_TRACK)}}.


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/flex:example}}

\section{Grid}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:grid}}\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid::doc}}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Grid layout is a subset of \sphinxhref{https://css-tricks.com/snippets/css/complete-guide-grid/}{CSS Flexbox}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It can arrange items into a 2D "table" that has rows or columns (tracks). The item can span through multiple columns or rows.
The track's size can be set in pixel, to the largest item (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_CONTENT}}) or in "Free unit" (FR) to distribute the free space proportionally.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To make an object a grid container call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_layout(obj, LV\_LAYOUT\_GRID)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the grid layout feature of LVGL needs to be globally enabled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_GRID}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.


\subsection{Terms}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:terms}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
tracks: the rows or columns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
free unit (FR): if set on track's size is set in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FR}} it will grow to fill the remaining space on the parent.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gap: the space between the rows and columns or the items on a track

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Simple interface}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:simple-interface}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
With the following functions you can easily set a Grid layout on any parent.


\subsubsection{Grid descriptors}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:grid-descriptors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
First you need to describe the size of rows and columns. It can be done by declaring 2 arrays and the track sizes in them. The last element must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_TEMPLATE\_LAST}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}coord\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{column\PYGZus{}dsc}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{400}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}GRID\PYGZus{}TEMPLATE\PYGZus{}LAST}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}   \PYG{c+cm}{/*2 columns with 100 and 400 ps width*/}
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}coord\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{row\PYGZus{}dsc}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}GRID\PYGZus{}TEMPLATE\PYGZus{}LAST}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+cm}{/*3 100 px tall rows*/}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set the descriptors on a parent use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_grid\_dsc\_array(obj, col\_dsc, row\_dsc)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Besides simple settings the size in pixel you can use two special values:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_CONTENT}} set the width to the largest children on this track

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_FR(X)}} tell what portion of the remaining space should be used by this track. Larger value means larger space.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Grid items}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:grid-items}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the children are not added to the grid. They need to be added manually to a cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To do this call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_grid\_cell(child, column\_align, column\_pos, column\_span, row\_align, row\_pos, row\_span)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{column\_align}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{row\_align}} determine how to align the children in its cell. The possible values are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_START}} means left on a horizontally and top vertically. (default)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_END}} means right on a horizontally and bottom vertically

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_CENTER}} simply center

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{colum\_pos}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{row\_pos}} means the zero based index of the cell into the item should be placed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{colum\_span}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{row\_span}} means how many tracks should the item involve from the start cell. Must be > 1.


\subsubsection{Grid align}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:grid-align}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If there are some empty space the track can be aligned several ways:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_START}} means left on a horizontally and top vertically. (default)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_END}} means right on a horizontally and bottom vertically

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_CENTER}} simply center

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_SPACE\_EVENLY}} items are distributed so that the spacing between any two items (and the space to the edges) is equal. Not applies to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{track\_cross\_place}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_SPACE\_AROUND}} items are evenly distributed in the track with equal space around them.
Note that visually the spaces aren’t equal, since all the items have equal space on both sides.
The first item will have one unit of space against the container edge, but two units of space between the next item because that next item has its own spacing that applies. Not applies to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{track\_cross\_place}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_SPACE\_BETWEEN}} items are evenly distributed in the track: first item is on the start line, last item on the end line. Not applies to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{track\_cross\_place}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To set the track's alignment use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_set\_grid\_align(obj, column\_align, row\_align)}}.


\subsection{Style interface}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:style-interface}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All the Grid related values are style properties under the hood and you can use them similarly to any other style properties. The following Grid related style properties exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_COLUMN\_DSC\_ARRAY}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_ROW\_DSC\_ARRAY}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_COLUMN\_ALIGN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_ROW\_ALIGN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_CELL\_X\_ALIGN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_CELL\_COLUMN\_POS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_CELL\_COLUMN\_SPAN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_CELL\_Y\_ALIGN}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_CELL\_ROW\_POS}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GRID\_CELL\_ROW\_SPAN}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Internal padding}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:internal-padding}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To modify the minimum space Grid inserts between objects, the following properties can be set on the Grid container style:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_row}} Sets the padding between the rows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad\_column}} Sets the padding between the columns.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Other features}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:other-features}}

\subsubsection{RTL}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:rtl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the base direction of the container is set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BASE\_DIR\_RTL}}, the meaning of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_START}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRID\_ALIGN\_END}} is swapped. I.e. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{START}} will mean right\sphinxhyphen{}most.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The columns will be placed from right to left.


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:example}}

\subsubsection{A simple grid}
\label{\detokenize{layouts/grid:a-simple-grid}}


\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}


\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include} \PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}../../lv\PYGZus{}examples.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}GRID \PYGZam{}\PYGZam{} LV\PYGZus{}BUILD\PYGZus{}EXAMPLES}

\PYG{c+cm}{/**}

\chapter{3rd party libraries}
\label{\detokenize{libs/index:rd-party-libraries}}\label{\detokenize{libs/index::doc}}

\section{File System Interfaces}
\label{\detokenize{libs/fsdrv:file-system-interfaces}}\label{\detokenize{libs/fsdrv::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL has a \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/overview/file-system.html}{File system} module to provide an abstraction layer for various file system drivers.
You still need to provide the drivers and libraries, this extension provides only the bridge between FATFS, LittleFS, STDIO, POSIX, WIN32 and LVGL.


\subsection{Built in wrappers}
\label{\detokenize{libs/fsdrv:built-in-wrappers}}

\subsubsection{FATFS}
\label{\detokenize{libs/fsdrv:fatfs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bridge for \sphinxhref{http://elm-chan.org/fsw/ff/00index\_e.html}{FatFS}. FatFS itself is not part of LVGL, but can be added and initialized externally.


\subsubsection{LittleFS}
\label{\detokenize{libs/fsdrv:littlefs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fs\_littlefs}} uses \sphinxhref{(https://github.com/littlefs-project/littlefs)}{LittleFS} API, the LittleFS library needs other external libraries that handle the mounting of partitions and low\sphinxhyphen{}level accesses, according to the given architecture. The functions for the latter are given to the lfs\_t structure as pointers by an external low\sphinxhyphen{}level library.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There's a convenience function called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fs\_littlefs\_set\_driver(LV\_FS\_LITTLEFS\_LETTER, my\_lfs)}}, specific to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fs\_littlefs}}, to attach a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lfs\_t}} object's pointer to a registered driver\sphinxhyphen{}letter. See its comments for more info.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://components.espressif.com/components/joltwallet/littlefs}{esp\_littlefs} is a wrapper for LittleFS to be used in Espressif ESP\sphinxhyphen{}devices. It handles the mounting and has the low\sphinxhyphen{}level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{littlefs\_api}} functions to read/write/erase blocks that LittleFS library needs. On mounting by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{esp\_littlefs}} the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lfs\_t}} structures are created. You need to get a handle to these to use ESP with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fs\_littlefs}}, as all functions use that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lfs\_t}} in LittleFS to identify the mounted partition.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In case you don't find a special function in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fs\_littlefs}} wrapper, you can look for it in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{esp\_littlefs}} API and use it directly, as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fs\_littlefs}} and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{esp\_littlefs}} APIs can be used side\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}side.


\subsubsection{STDIO}
\label{\detokenize{libs/fsdrv:stdio}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bride to C standard functions on Linux and Windows. For example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fopen}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fread}}, etc.


\subsubsection{POSIX}
\label{\detokenize{libs/fsdrv:posix}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bride to POSIX functions on Linux and Windows. For example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{open}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{read}}, etc.


\subsubsection{WIN32}
\label{\detokenize{libs/fsdrv:win32}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bride to Win32 API function. For example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CreateFileA}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadFile}}, etc.


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{libs/fsdrv:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_FS\_...}} and assign an upper cased letter to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FS\_...\_LETTER}} (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{'S'}}).
After that you can access files using that driver letter. E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"S:path/to/file.txt"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The work directory can be set with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FS\_...\_PATH}}. E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"/home/joe/projects/"}} The actual file/directory paths will be appended to it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Cached reading is also supported if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FS\_...\_CACHE\_SIZE}} is set to not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} value. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fs\_read}} caches this size of data to lower the number of actual reads from the storage.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{BMP decoder}
\label{\detokenize{libs/bmp:bmp-decoder}}\label{\detokenize{libs/bmp::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This extension allows the use of BMP images in LVGL.
This implementation uses \sphinxhref{https://github.com/caj-johnson/bmp-decoder}{bmp\sphinxhyphen{}decoder} library.
The pixels are read on demand (not the whole image is loaded) so using BMP images requires very little RAM.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If enabled in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_BMP}} LVGL will register a new image decoder automatically so BMP files can be directly used as image sources. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}src}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}img}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{S:path/to/picture.bmp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, a file system driver needs to registered to open images from files. Read more about it \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/overview/file-system.html}{here} or just enable one in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_FS\_...}}


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{libs/bmp:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only BMP files are supported and BMP images as C array (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_dsc\_t}}) are not. It's because there is no practical differences between how the BMP files and LVGL's image format stores the image data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
BMP files can be loaded only from file. If you want to store them in flash it's better to convert them to C array with \sphinxhref{https://lvgl.io/tools/imageconverter}{LVGL's image converter}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The BMP files color format needs to match with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH}}. Use GIMP to save the image in the required format.
Both RGB888 and ARGB888 works with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH 32}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Palette is not supported.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because not the whole image is read in can not be zoomed or rotated.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{libs/bmp:example}}

\subsubsection{Open a BMP image from file}
\label{\detokenize{libs/bmp:open-a-bmp-image-from-file}}


\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}


\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include} \PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}../../lv\PYGZus{}examples.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}BMP \PYGZam{}\PYGZam{} LV\PYGZus{}BUILD\PYGZus{}EXAMPLES}

\PYG{c+cm}{/**}
\PYG{c+cm}{ * Open a BMP file from a file}
\PYG{c+cm}{ */}
\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{lv\PYGZus{}example\PYGZus{}bmp\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{img} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{c+cm}{/* Assuming a File system is attached to letter \PYGZsq{}A\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{c+cm}{     * E.g. set LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}FS\PYGZus{}STDIO \PYGZsq{}A\PYGZsq{} in lv\PYGZus{}conf.h */}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}COLOR\PYGZus{}DEPTH == 32}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}src}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{img}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{A:lvgl/examples/libs/bmp/example\PYGZus{}32bit.bmp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{elif LV\PYGZus{}COLOR\PYGZus{}DEPTH == 16}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}src}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{img}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{A:lvgl/examples/libs/bmp/example\PYGZus{}16bit.bmp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{endif}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}center}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{img}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{endif}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}


\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{img} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{img}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\section{JPG decoder}
\label{\detokenize{libs/sjpg:jpg-decoder}}\label{\detokenize{libs/sjpg::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow the use of JPG images in LVGL. Besides that it also allows the use of a custom format, called Split JPG (SJPG), which can be decoded in more optimal way on embedded systems.


\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{libs/sjpg:overview}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supports both normal JPG and the custom SJPG formats.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decoding normal JPG consumes RAM with the size fo the whole uncompressed image (recommended only for devices with more RAM)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
SJPG is a custom format based on "normal" JPG and specially made for LVGL.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
SJPG is 'split\sphinxhyphen{}jpeg' which is a bundle of small jpeg fragments with an sjpg header.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
SJPG size will be almost comparable to the jpg file or might be a slightly larger.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
File read from file and c\sphinxhyphen{}array are implemented.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
SJPEG frame fragment cache enables fast fetching of lines if available in cache.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default the sjpg image cache will be image width * 2 * 16 bytes (can be modified)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the required partion of the JPG and SJPG images are decoded, therefore they can't be zoomed or rotated.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{libs/sjpg:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If enabled in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_SJPG}} LVGL will register a new image decoder automatically so JPG and SJPG files can be directly used as image sources. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}src}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{my\PYGZus{}img}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{S:path/to/picture.jpg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, a file system driver needs to registered to open images from files. Read more about it \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/overview/file-system.html}{here} or just enable one in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_FS\_...}}


\subsection{Converter}
\label{\detokenize{libs/sjpg:converter}}

\subsubsection{Converting JPG to C array}
\label{\detokenize{libs/sjpg:converting-jpg-to-c-array}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use lvgl online tool https://lvgl.io/tools/imageconverter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Color format = RAW, output format = C Array

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Converting JPG to SJPG}
\label{\detokenize{libs/sjpg:converting-jpg-to-sjpg}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
python3 and the PIL library required. (PIL can be installed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pip3 install pillow}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
To create SJPG from JPG:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copy the image to convert into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl/scripts}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cd lvgl/scripts}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{python3 jpg\_to\_sjpg.py image\_to\_convert.jpg}}. It creates both a C files and an SJPG image.

\end{itemize}

        walpaper.sjpg           \PYG{o}{(}bin file\PYG{o}{)}
        walpaper.c              \PYG{o}{(}c array\PYG{o}{)}

All good!

\section{PNG decoder}
\label{\detokenize{libs/png:png-decoder}}\label{\detokenize{libs/png::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow the use of PNG images in LVGL. This implementation uses \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvandeve/lodepng}{lodepng} library.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If enabled in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_PNG}} LVGL will register a new image decoder automatically so PNG files can be directly used as any other image  sources.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, a file system driver needs to registered to open images from files. Read more about it \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/overview/file-system.html}{here} or just enable one in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_FS\_...}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The whole PNG image is decoded so during decoding RAM equals to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{image width x image height x 4}} bytes are required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As it might take significant time to decode PNG images LVGL's \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/overview/image.html\#image-caching}{images caching} feature can be useful.


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{libs/png:example}}

\section{GIF decoder}
\label{\detokenize{libs/gif:gif-decoder}}\label{\detokenize{libs/gif::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow using GIF images in LVGL. Based on https://github.com/lecram/gifdec

\sphinxAtStartPar
When enabled in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_GIF}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_gif\_create(parent)}} can be used to create a gif widget.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_gif\_set\_src(obj, src)}} works very similarly to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_src}}. As source, it also accepts images as variables (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_dsc\_t}}) or files.


\subsection{Convert GIF files to C array}
\label{\detokenize{libs/gif:convert-gif-files-to-c-array}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To convert a GIF file to byte values array use \sphinxhref{https://lvgl.io/tools/imageconverter}{LVGL's online converter}. Select "Raw" color format and "C array" Output format.


\subsection{Use GIF images from file}
\label{\detokenize{libs/gif:use-gif-images-from-file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}gif\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}src}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{S:path/to/example.gif}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, a file system driver needs to be registered to open images from files. Read more about it \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/overview/file-system.html}{here} or just enable one in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_FS\_...}}


\subsection{Memory requirements}
\label{\detokenize{libs/gif:memory-requirements}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To decode and display a GIF animation the following amount of RAM is required:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH 8}}: 3 x image width x image height

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH 16}}: 4 x image width x image height

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_COLOR\_DEPTH 32}}: 5 x image width x image height

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{libs/gif:example}}

\subsubsection{Open a GIF image from file and variable}
\label{\detokenize{libs/gif:open-a-gif-image-from-file-and-variable}}

\section{FreeType support}
\label{\detokenize{libs/freetype:freetype-support}}\label{\detokenize{libs/freetype::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interface to \sphinxhref{https://www.freetype.org/}{FreeType} to generate font bitmaps run time.


\subsection{Install FreeType}
\label{\detokenize{libs/freetype:install-freetype}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download Freetype from \sphinxhref{https://sourceforge.net/projects/freetype/files/}{here}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sudo make install}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Add FreeType to your project}
\label{\detokenize{libs/freetype:add-freetype-to-your-project}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add include path: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/usr/include/freetype2}} (for GCC: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}I/usr/include/freetype2 \sphinxhyphen{}L/usr/local/lib}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add library: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freetype}} (for GCC: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}L/usr/local/lib \sphinxhyphen{}lfreetype}})

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{libs/freetype:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_FREETYPE}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To cache the glyphs from the opened fonts, set  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FREETYPE\_CACHE\_SIZE >= 0}} and then use the following macros for detailed configuration:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FREETYPE\_CACHE\_SIZE}}:maximum memory(bytes) used to cache font bitmap, outline, character maps, etc. 0 means use the system default value, less than 0 means disable cache. Note: that this value does not account for managed FT\_Face and FT\_Size objects.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FREETYPE\_CACHE\_FT\_FACES}}:maximum number of opened FT\_Face objects managed by this cache instance.0 means use the system default value. Only useful when LV\_FREETYPE\_CACHE\_SIZE >= 0.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FREETYPE\_CACHE\_FT\_SIZES}}:maximum number of opened FT\_Size objects managed by this cache instance. 0 means use the system default value. Only useful when LV\_FREETYPE\_CACHE\_SIZE >= 0.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When you are sure that all the used font sizes will not be greater than 256, you can enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FREETYPE\_SBIT\_CACHE}}, which is much more memory efficient for small bitmaps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ft\_font\_init()}} to create FreeType fonts. It returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} to indicate success, at the same time, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{font}} member of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ft\_info\_t}} will be filled with a pointer to an LVGL font, and you can use it like any LVGL font.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Font style supports bold and italic, you can use the following macros to set:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FT\_FONT\_STYLE\_NORMAL}}:default style.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FT\_FONT\_STYLE\_ITALIC}}:Italic style

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FT\_FONT\_STYLE\_BOLD}}:bold style

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
They can be combined.eg:\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FT\_FONT\_STYLE\_BOLD | FT\_FONT\_STYLE\_ITALIC}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, the FreeType extension doesn't use LVGL's file system.
You can simply pass the path to the font as usual on your operating system or platform.


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{libs/freetype:example}}

\subsubsection{Open a front with FreeType}
\label{\detokenize{libs/freetype:open-a-front-with-freetype}}

    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}style\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text\PYGZus{}align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{style}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}TEXT\PYGZus{}ALIGN\PYGZus{}CENTER}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a label with the new style*/}

\section{Tiny TTF font engine}
\label{\detokenize{libs/tiny_ttf:tiny-ttf-font-engine}}\label{\detokenize{libs/tiny_ttf::doc}}

\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{libs/tiny_ttf:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use https://github.com/nothings/stb to render TrueType fonts in LVGL.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When enabled in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_TINY\_TTF}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tiny\_ttf\_create\_data(data, data\_size, font\_size)}} can be used to
create a TTF font instance at the specified font size. You can then
use that font anywhere \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_font\_t}} is accepted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, the TTF or OTF file must be embedded as an array, either in
a header, or loaded into RAM in order to function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_TINY\_TTF\_FILE\_SUPPORT}} is enabled,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tiny\_ttf\_create\_file(path, font\_size)}} will also be available,
allowing tiny\_ttf to stream from a file. The file must remain open the
entire time the font is being used, and streaming on demand may be
considerably slower.

\sphinxAtStartPar
After a font is created, you can change the font size in pixels by using
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tiny\_ttf\_set\_size(font, font\_size)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, a font will use up to 4KB of cache to speed up rendering
glyphs. This maximum can be changed by using
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tiny\_ttf\_create\_data\_ex(data, data\_size, font\_size, cache\_size)}}
or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_tiny\_ttf\_create\_file\_ex(path, font\_size, cache\_size)}} (when
available). The cache size is indicated in bytes.

\section{QR code}
\label{\detokenize{libs/qrcode:qr-code}}\label{\detokenize{libs/qrcode::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
QR code generation with LVGL. Uses \sphinxhref{https://github.com/nayuki/QR-Code-generator}{QR\sphinxhyphen{}Code\sphinxhyphen{}generator} by \sphinxhref{https://github.com/nayuki}{nayuki}.


\subsection{Get started}
\label{\detokenize{libs/qrcode:get-started}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download or clone this repository
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_lib\_qrcode.git}{Download} from GitHub

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clone: git clone https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_lib\_qrcode.git

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Include the library: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#include "lv\_lib\_qrcode/lv\_qrcode.h"}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Test with the following code:

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{const} \PYG{k+kt}{char} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Hello world}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a 100x100 QR code*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{qr} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}qrcode\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hex3}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mh}{0x33f}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}color\PYGZus{}hex3}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mh}{0xeef}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+cm}{/*Set data*/}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}qrcode\PYGZus{}update}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{qr}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{strlen}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{libs/qrcode:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
QR codes with less data are smaller, but they scaled by an integer number to best fit to the given size.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{libs/qrcode:example}}

\section{Lottie player}
\label{\detokenize{libs/rlottie:lottie-player}}\label{\detokenize{libs/rlottie::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allows to use Lottie animations in LVGL. Taken from this \sphinxhref{https://github.com/ValentiWorkLearning/lv\_rlottie}{base repository}

\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL provides the interface to \sphinxhref{https://github.com/Samsung/rlottie}{Samsung/rlottie} library's C API. That is the actual Lottie player is not part of LVGL, it needs to be built separately.


\subsection{Build Rlottie}
\label{\detokenize{libs/rlottie:build-rlottie}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To build Samsung's Rlottie C++14\sphinxhyphen{}compatible compiler and optionally CMake 3.14 or higher is required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To build on desktop you can follow the instructions from Rlottie's \sphinxhref{https://github.com/Samsung/rlottie/blob/master/README}{README}. In the most basic case it looks like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mkdir} \PYG{n}{rlottie\PYGZus{}workdir}
\PYG{n}{cd} \PYG{n}{rlottie\PYGZus{}workdir}
\PYG{n}{git} \PYG{n}{clone} \PYG{n+nl}{https}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{c+c1}{//github.com/Samsung/rlottie.git}
\PYG{n}{mkdir} \PYG{n}{build}
\PYG{n}{cd} \PYG{n}{build}
\PYG{n}{cmake} \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{rlottie}
\PYG{n}{make} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{j}
\PYG{n}{sudo} \PYG{n}{make} \PYG{n}{install}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
And finally add the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}lrlottie}} flag to your linker.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On embedded systems you need to take care of integrating Rlottie to the given build system.


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{libs/rlottie:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can use animation from files or raw data (text). In either case first you need to enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_RLOTTIE}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{height}} of the object be set in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{create} function and the animation will be scaled accordingly.


\subsubsection{Use Rlottie from file}
\label{\detokenize{libs/rlottie:use-rlottie-from-file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To create a Lottie animation from file use:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{lottie} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}rlottie\PYGZus{}create\PYGZus{}from\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{parent}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{width}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{height}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{path/to/lottie.json}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, Rlottie uses the standard STDIO C file API, so you can use the path "normally" and no LVGL specific driver letter is required.


\subsubsection{Use Rlottie from raw string data}
\label{\detokenize{libs/rlottie:use-rlottie-from-raw-string-data}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_example\_rlottie\_approve.c}} contains an example animation in raw format. Instead storing the JSON string a hex array is stored for the following reasons:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
avoid escaping \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"}} in the JSON file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
some compilers don't support very long strings

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl/scripts/filetohex.py}} can be used to convert a Lottie file a hex array. E.g.:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{filetohex}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{py} \PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{to}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{lottie}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{json} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{txt}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To create an animation from raw data:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{extern} \PYG{k}{const} \PYG{k+kt}{uint8\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{lottie\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{lottie} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}rlottie\PYGZus{}create\PYGZus{}from\PYGZus{}raw}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{parent}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{width}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{height}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const} \PYG{k+kt}{char} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{lottie\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Getting animations}
\label{\detokenize{libs/rlottie:getting-animations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lottie is standard and popular format so you can find many animation files on the web.
For example: https://lottiefiles.com/

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also create your own animations with Adobe After Effects or similar software.


\subsection{Controlling animations}
\label{\detokenize{libs/rlottie:controlling-animations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL provides two functions to control the animation mode: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_rlottie\_set\_play\_mode}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_rlottie\_set\_current\_frame}}.
You'll combine your intentions when calling the first method, like in these examples:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{lottie} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}rlottie\PYGZus{}create\PYGZus{}from\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{scr}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{128}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{128}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{test.json}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}center}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lottie}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+c1}{// Pause to a specific frame}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}rlottie\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}current\PYGZus{}frame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lottie}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}rlottie\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}play\PYGZus{}mode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lottie}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}RLOTTIE\PYGZus{}CTRL\PYGZus{}PAUSE}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{c+c1}{// The specified frame will be displayed and then the animation will pause}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Play backward and loop}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}rlottie\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}play\PYGZus{}mode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lottie}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}RLOTTIE\PYGZus{}CTRL\PYGZus{}PLAY} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}RLOTTIE\PYGZus{}CTRL\PYGZus{}BACKWARD} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}RLOTTIE\PYGZus{}CTRL\PYGZus{}LOOP}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Play forward once (no looping)}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}rlottie\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}play\PYGZus{}mode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lottie}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}RLOTTIE\PYGZus{}CTRL\PYGZus{}PLAY} \PYG{o}{|} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}RLOTTIE\PYGZus{}CTRL\PYGZus{}FORWARD}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default animation mode is \sphinxstylestrong{play forward with loop}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you don't enable looping, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_READY}} is sent when the animation can not make more progress without looping.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To get the number of frames in an animation or the current frame index, you can cast the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_t}} instance to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_rlottie\_t}} instance and inspect the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{current\_frame}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_frames}} members.

\section{FFmpeg support}
\label{\detokenize{libs/ffmpeg:ffmpeg-support}}\label{\detokenize{libs/ffmpeg::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://www.ffmpeg.org/}{FFmpeg} A complete, cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform solution to record, convert and stream audio and video.


\subsection{Install FFmpeg}
\label{\detokenize{libs/ffmpeg:install-ffmpeg}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download FFmpeg from \sphinxhref{https://www.ffmpeg.org/download.html}{here}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{./configure \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}disable\sphinxhyphen{}all \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}disable\sphinxhyphen{}autodetect \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}disable\sphinxhyphen{}podpages \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}disable\sphinxhyphen{}asm \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enable\sphinxhyphen{}avcodec \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enable\sphinxhyphen{}avformat \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enable\sphinxhyphen{}decoders \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enable\sphinxhyphen{}encoders \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enable\sphinxhyphen{}demuxers \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enable\sphinxhyphen{}parsers \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enable\sphinxhyphen{}protocol='file' \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enable\sphinxhyphen{}swscale \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enable\sphinxhyphen{}zlib}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sudo make install}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Add FFmpeg to your project}
\label{\detokenize{libs/ffmpeg:add-ffmpeg-to-your-project}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add library: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FFmpeg}} (for GCC: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}lavformat \sphinxhyphen{}lavcodec \sphinxhyphen{}lavutil \sphinxhyphen{}lswscale \sphinxhyphen{}lm \sphinxhyphen{}lz \sphinxhyphen{}lpthread}})

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{libs/ffmpeg:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_FFMPEG}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the examples below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that, the FFmpeg extension doesn't use LVGL's file system.
You can simply pass the path to the image or video as usual on your operating system or platform.


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{libs/ffmpeg:example}}

\section{Snapshot}
\label{\detokenize{others/snapshot:snapshot}}\label{\detokenize{others/snapshot::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Snapshot provides APIs to take snapshot image for LVGL object together with its children. The image will look exactly like the object.


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{others/snapshot:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Simply call API \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_snapshot\_take}} to generate the image descriptor which can be set as image object src using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_src}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note, only below color formats are supported for now:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LV\_IMG\_CF\_TRUE\_COLOR\_ALPHA

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LV\_IMG\_CF\_ALPHA\_1BIT

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LV\_IMG\_CF\_ALPHA\_2BIT

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LV\_IMG\_CF\_ALPHA\_4BIT

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LV\_IMG\_CF\_ALPHA\_8BIT

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Free the Image}
\label{\detokenize{others/snapshot:free-the-image}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The memory \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_snapshot\_take}} uses are dynamically allocated using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_mem\_alloc}}. Use API \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_snapshot\_free}} to free the memory it takes. This will firstly free memory the image data takes, then the image descriptor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Take caution to free the snapshot but not delete the image object. Before free the memory, be sure to firstly unlink it from image object, using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_src(NULL)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_cache\_invalidate\_src(src)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Below code snippet explains usage of this API.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{update\PYGZus{}snapshot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{obj}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{img\PYGZus{}snapshot}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}dsc\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{snapshot} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}img\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}src}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{img\PYGZus{}snapshot}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Use Existing Buffer}
\label{\detokenize{others/snapshot:use-existing-buffer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the snapshot needs update now and then, or simply caller provides memory, use API \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_res\_t lv\_snapshot\_take\_to\_buf(lv\_obj\_t * obj, lv\_img\_cf\_t cf, lv\_img\_dsc\_t * dsc, void * buf, uint32\_t buf\_size);}} for this case. It's caller's responsibility to alloc/free the memory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If snapshot is generated successfully, the image descriptor is updated and image data will be stored to provided \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{buf}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that snapshot may fail if provided buffer is not enough, which may happen when object size changes. It's recommended to use API \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_snapshot\_buf\_size\_needed}} to check the needed buffer size in byte firstly and resize the buffer accordingly.

\section{Monkey}
\label{\detokenize{others/monkey:monkey}}\label{\detokenize{others/monkey::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A simple monkey test. Use random input to stress test the application.


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{others/monkey:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_MONKEY}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
First configure monkey, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_monkey\_config\_t}} to define the configuration structure, set the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{type}} (check {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{input devices}}}} for the supported types), and then set the range of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{period\_range}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{input\_range}}, the monkey will output random operations at random times within this range. Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_monkey\_create}} to create monkey. Finally call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_monkey\_set\_enable(monkey, true)}} to enable monkey.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want to pause the monkey, call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_monkey\_set\_enable(monkey, false)}}. To delete the monkey, call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_monkey\_del(monkey)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{input\_range}} has different meanings in different \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{type}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_INDEV\_TYPE\_POINTER}} No effect, click randomly within the pixels of the screen resolution.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_INDEV\_TYPE\_ENCODER}} The minimum and maximum values ​​of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{enc\_diff}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_INDEV\_TYPE\_BUTTON}} The minimum and maximum values ​​of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{btn\_id}}. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_monkey\_get\_indev()}} to get the input device, and use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_indev\_set\_button\_points()}} to map the key ID to the coordinates.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_INDEV\_TYPE\_KEYPAD}} No effect, Send random {\hyperref[\detokenize{overview/indev::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Keys}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\section{Grid navigation}
\label{\detokenize{others/gridnav:grid-navigation}}\label{\detokenize{others/gridnav::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grid navigation (gridnav for short) is a feature that changes the currently focused child object as arrow keys are pressed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the children are arranged into a grid\sphinxhyphen{}like layout then the up, down, left and right arrows move focus to the nearest sibling
in the respective direction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It doesn't matter how the children are positioned, as only the current x and y coordinates are considered.
This means that gridnav works with manually positioned children, as well as {\hyperref[\detokenize{layouts/flex::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Flex}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{layouts/grid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Grid}}}} layouts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Gridnav also works if the children are arranged into a single row or column.
That makes it useful, for example, to simplify navigation on a {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/extra/list::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{List widget}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Gridnav assumes that the object to which gridnav is added is part of a \sphinxhref{/overview/indev.html\#groups}{group}.
This way, if the object with gridnav is focused, the arrow key presses are automatically forwarded to the object
so that gridnav can process the arrow keys.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To move the focus to the next widget of the group use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_KEY\_NEXT/PREV}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_group\_focus\_next/prev()}} or the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TAB}} key on keyboard as usual.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the container is scrollable and the focused child is out of the view, gridnav will automatically scroll the child into view.


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{others/gridnav:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To add the gridnav feature to an object use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_gridnav\_add(cont, flags)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flags}} control the behavior of gridnav:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRIDNAV\_CTRL\_NONE}} Default settings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRIDNAV\_CTRL\_ROLLOVER}}  If there is no next/previous object in a direction,
the focus goes to the object in the next/previous row (on left/right keys) or first/last row (on up/down keys

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_GRIDNAV\_CTRL\_SCROLL\_FIRST}} If an arrow is pressed and the focused object can be scrolled in that direction
then it will be scrolled instead of going to the next/previous object.  If there is no more room for scrolling the next/previous object will be focused normally

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_gridnav\_remove(cont)}} Removes gridnav from an object.


\subsection{Focusable objects}
\label{\detokenize{others/gridnav:focusable-objects}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An object needs to be clickable or click focusable (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CLICKABLE}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_CLICK\_FOCUSABLE}})
and not hidden (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_OBJ\_FLAG\_HIDDEN}}) to be focusable by gridnav.

\section{Fragment}
\label{\detokenize{others/fragment:fragment}}\label{\detokenize{others/fragment::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fragment is a concept copied from \sphinxhref{https://developer.android.com/guide/fragments}{Android}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It represents a reusable portion of your app's UI. A fragment defines and manages its own layout, has its own lifecycle,
and can handle its own events. Like Android's Fragment that must be hosted by an activity or another fragment, Fragment
in LVGL needs to be hosted by an object, or another fragment. The fragment’s view hierarchy becomes part of, or attaches
to, the host’s view hierarchy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Such concept also has some similarities
to \sphinxhref{https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiviewcontroller}{UiViewController on iOS}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fragment Manager is a manager holding references to fragments attached to it, and has an internal stack to achieve
navigation. You can use fragment manager to build navigation stack, or multi pane application easily.


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{others/fragment:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_FRAGMENT}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.


\subsubsection{Create Fragment Class}
\label{\detokenize{others/fragment:create-fragment-class}}

    \PYG{c+cm}{/* IMPORTANT: don\PYGZsq{}t miss this part */}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}fragment\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{base}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{c+cm}{/* States, object references and data fields for this fragment */}
    \PYG{k}{const} \PYG{k+kt}{char} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{title}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{const} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}fragment\PYGZus{}class\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}cls} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{c+cm}{/* Initialize something needed */}
        \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{constructor\PYGZus{}cb} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}fragment\PYGZus{}ctor}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{c+cm}{/* Create view objects */}
        \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}cb} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}fragment\PYGZus{}create\PYGZus{}obj}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{c+cm}{/* IMPORTANT: size of your fragment struct */}
        \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{instance\PYGZus{}size} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{k}{sizeof}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{struct} \PYG{n+nc}{sample\PYGZus{}fragment\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Use \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fragment\_manager}}}

\section{Messaging}
\label{\detokenize{others/msg:messaging}}\label{\detokenize{others/msg::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Messaging (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg}}) is a classic {[}{]}publisher subscriber{]}(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publish\%E2\%80\%93subscribe\_pattern) implementation for LVGL.


\subsection{IDs}
\label{\detokenize{others/msg:ids}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both the publishers and the subscribers needs to know the message identifiers.
In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg}} these are simple \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uint32\_t}} integers. For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{define MSG\PYGZus{}DOOR\PYGZus{}OPENED             1}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{define MSG\PYGZus{}DOOR\PYGZus{}CLOSED             2}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{define MSG\PYGZus{}USER\PYGZus{}NAME\PYGZus{}CHANGED       100}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{define MSG\PYGZus{}USER\PYGZus{}AVATAR\PYGZus{}CHANGED     101}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can orgnaize the message IDs as you wish.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both parties also need to know about the format of teh payload. E.g. in the above example
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MSG\_DOOR\_OPENED}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MSG\_DOOR\_CLOSED}} has no payload but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MSG\_USER\_NAME\_CHANGED}} can have a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char *}} payload containing the user name, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MSG\_USER\_AVATAR\_CHANGED}} a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const void *}} image source with the new avatar image.


\subsection{Send message}
\label{\detokenize{others/msg:send-message}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Messages can be sent with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg\_send(msg\_id, payload)}}. E.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}send}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{MSG\PYGZus{}USER\PYGZus{}DOOR\PYGZus{}OPENED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}send}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{MSG\PYGZus{}USER\PYGZus{}NAME\PYGZus{}CHANGED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{John Smith}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Subscribe to a message}
\label{\detokenize{others/msg:subscribe-to-a-message}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg\_subscribe(msg\_id, callback, user\_data)}} can be used to subscribe to message.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback should look like this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{user\PYGZus{}name\PYGZus{}subscriber\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{s}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{m}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{c+cm}{/*s: a subscriber obeject, can be used to unscubscribe*/}
    \PYG{c+cm}{/*m: a message object with the msg\PYGZus{}id, payload, and user\PYGZus{}data (set durung subscription)*/}

    \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{k}{do} \PYG{n}{something}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
From \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg\_t}} the followings can be used to get some data:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg\_get\_id(m)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg\_get\_payload(m)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg\_get\_user\_data(m)}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Subscribe with an lv\_obj}
\label{\detokenize{others/msg:subscribe-with-an-lv-obj}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It's quite typical that an LVGL widget is interested in some messages.
To make it simpler \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg\_subsribe\_obj(msg\_id, obj, user\_data)}} can be used.
If a new message is published with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{msg\_id}} an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_MSG\_RECEIVED}} event will be sent to the object.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{user\PYGZus{}name\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{user\PYGZus{}name\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}MSG\PYGZus{}RECEIVED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}subsribe\PYGZus{}obj}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{MSG\PYGZus{}USER\PYGZus{}NAME\PYGZus{}CHANGED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{user\PYGZus{}name\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n}{user\PYGZus{}name\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}target}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}msg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}payload}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{m}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Unsubscribe}
\label{\detokenize{others/msg:unsubscribe}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_msg\_subscribe}} returns a pointer which can be used to unsubscribe:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{s1}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{s1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}subscribe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{MSG\PYGZus{}USER\PYGZus{}DOOR\PYGZus{}OPENED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{some\PYGZus{}callback}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}

\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}unsubscribe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{s1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{others/msg:example}}

\subsubsection{Slider to label messaging}
\label{\detokenize{others/msg:slider-to-label-messaging}}


\begin{sphinxuseclass}{toggle}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{header}


\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include} \PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}../../lv\PYGZus{}examples.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{if LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}MSG \PYGZam{}\PYGZam{} LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}SLIDER \PYGZam{}\PYGZam{} LV\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}LABEL \PYGZam{}\PYGZam{} LV\PYGZus{}BUILD\PYGZus{}EXAMPLES}

\PYG{c+cm}{/*Define a message ID*/}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{define MSG\PYGZus{}NEW\PYGZus{}TEMPERATURE     1}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{slider\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{label\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+cm}{/**}
\PYG{c+cm}{ * A slider sends a message on value change and a label display\PYGZsq{}s that value}
\PYG{c+cm}{ */}
\PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{lv\PYGZus{}example\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}1}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a slider in the center of the display*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{slider} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}slider\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}center}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{slider}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{slider}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{slider\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}VALUE\PYGZus{}CHANGED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Create a label below the slider*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}create}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}scr\PYGZus{}act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{label\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}EVENT\PYGZus{}MSG\PYGZus{}RECEIVED}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}label\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{0\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LV\PYGZus{}ALIGN\PYGZus{}CENTER}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{30}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Subscribe the label to a message. Also use the user\PYGZus{}data to set a format string here.*/}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}subsribe\PYGZus{}obj}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{MSG\PYGZus{}NEW\PYGZus{}TEMPERATURE}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZpc{}d °C}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{slider\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{c+cm}{/*Notify all subscribers (only the label now) that the slider value has been changed*/}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k}{static} \PYG{k+kt}{void} \PYG{n+nf}{label\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}cb}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}obj\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{label} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}target}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
    \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}msg\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}event\PYGZus{}get\PYGZus{}msg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\section{Image font (imgfont)}
\label{\detokenize{others/imgfont:image-font-imgfont}}\label{\detokenize{others/imgfont::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw image in label or span obj with imgfont.
This is often used to display Unicode emoji icons in text.
Supported image formats: determined by LVGL image decoder.


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{others/imgfont:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_IMGFONT}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To create a new imgfont use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_imgfont\_create(height, path\_cb)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{height}} used to indicate the size of a imgfont.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{path\_cb}} Used to get the image path of the specified unicode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_imgfont\_destroy(imgfont)}} to destroy a imgfont that is no longer used.


\subsection{Example}
\label{\detokenize{others/imgfont:example}}
