\section{Pinyin IME}
\label{\detokenize{others/ime_pinyin:pinyin-ime}}\label{\detokenize{others/ime_pinyin::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pinyin IME provides API to provide Chinese Pinyin input method (Chinese input) for keyboard object, which supports 26 key and 9 key input modes. You can think of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin}} as a Pinyin input method plug\sphinxhyphen{}in for keyboard objects.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Normally, an environment where {\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{lv\_keyboard}}}} can run can also run \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin}}. There are two main influencing factors: the size of the font file and the size of the dictionary.



\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin}}为{\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{键盘}}}}组件提供汉语拼音输入法（中文输入）的功能(后文简称为拼音输入法)，支持26键和9键输入模式。您可以将 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin}} 看成是键盘组件的汉语拼音输入法插件。

\sphinxAtStartPar
一般情况下，只要是{\hyperref[\detokenize{widgets/extra/keyboard::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{键盘}}}}组件能运行的环境 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin}} 也能运行。有两个影响因素：字库的大小和词库的大小。




\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{others/ime_pinyin:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_IME\_PINYIN}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
First use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_create(lv\_scr\_act())}} to create a Pinyin input method plug\sphinxhyphen{}in, then use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_set\_keyboard(pinyin\_ime, kb)}} to add the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keyboard}} you created to the Pinyin input method plug\sphinxhyphen{}in.
You can use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_set\_dict(pinyin\_ime, your\_dict)}} to use a custom dictionary (if you don't want to use the built\sphinxhyphen{}in dictionary at first, you can disable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IME\_PINYIN\_USE\_DEFAULT\_DICT}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}, which can save a lot of memory space).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The built\sphinxhyphen{}in thesaurus is customized based on the \sphinxstylestrong{LV\_FONT\_SIMSUN\_16\_CJK} font library, which currently only has more than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1,000}} most common CJK radicals, so it is recommended to use custom fonts and thesaurus.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the process of using the Pinyin input method plug\sphinxhyphen{}in, you can change the keyboard and dictionary at any time.



\sphinxAtStartPar
在 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} 中打开 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_USE\_IME\_PINYIN}}。

\sphinxAtStartPar
首先，使用 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_create(lv\_scr\_act())}} 函数创建一个拼音输入法插件，
然后使用 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_set\_keyboard(pinyin\_ime, kb)}} 函数将您创建的键盘组件添加到插件中。

\sphinxAtStartPar
内置的词库是基于 LVGL 的 \sphinxstylestrong{LV\_FONT\_SIMSUN\_16\_CJK} 字库定制，这个字库目前只有 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1000}} 多个最常见的 CJK 部首，所以建议使用自定义字库和词库。

\sphinxAtStartPar
您可以使用 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_set\_dict(pinyin\_ime, your\_dict)}} 函数来设置使用自定义的词库，如果您一开始就不打算使用内置的词库，建议您在 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} 中将 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IME\_PINYIN\_USE\_DEFAULT\_DICT}} 关闭，这可以节省一些内存空间。




\subsection{Custom dictionary}
\label{\detokenize{others/ime_pinyin:custom-dictionary}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you don't want to use the built\sphinxhyphen{}in Pinyin dictionary, you can use the custom dictionary.
Or if you think that the built\sphinxhyphen{}in phonetic dictionary consumes a lot of memory, you can also use a custom dictionary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Customizing the dictionary is very simple.

\sphinxAtStartPar
First, set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IME\_PINYIN\_USE\_DEFAULT\_DICT}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Then, write a dictionary in the following format.



\sphinxAtStartPar
如果您不想使用内置的词库，可以通过下面的方法自定义词库。

\sphinxAtStartPar
自定义词典非常简单。
首先，在 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} 将 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_IME\_PINYIN\_USE\_DEFAULT\_DICT}} 设置为 0。
然后按照下面的格式编写词库。




\subsubsection{Dictionary format}
\label{\detokenize{others/ime_pinyin:dictionary-format}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The arrangement order of each pinyin syllable is very important. You need to customize your own thesaurus according to the Hanyu Pinyin syllable table. You can read \sphinxhref{https://baike.baidu.com/item/\%E6\%B1\%89\%E8\%AF\%AD\%E6\%8B\%BC\%E9\%9F\%B3\%E9\%9F\%B3\%E8\%8A\%82/9167981}{here} to learn about the Hanyu Pinyin syllables and the syllable table.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Then, write your own dictionary according to the following format:



\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{注意}，各个拼音音节的排列顺序非常重要，您需要按照汉语拼音音节表定制自己的词库，可以阅读\sphinxhref{https://baike.baidu.com/item/\%E6\%B1\%89\%E8\%AF\%AD\%E6\%8B\%BC\%E9\%9F\%B3\%E9\%9F\%B3\%E8\%8A\%82/9167981}{这里}了解\sphinxhref{https://baike.baidu.com/item/\%E6\%B1\%89\%E8\%AF\%AD\%E6\%8B\%BC\%E9\%9F\%B3\%E9\%9F\%B3\%E8\%8A\%82/9167981}{汉语拼音音节}以及\sphinxhref{https://baike.baidu.com/item/\%E6\%B1\%89\%E8\%AF\%AD\%E6\%8B\%BC\%E9\%9F\%B3\%E9\%9F\%B3\%E8\%8A\%82/9167981\#1}{音节表}。

\sphinxAtStartPar
然后，根据下面的格式编写自己的词库：



\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{lv\PYGZus{}100ask\PYGZus{}pinyin\PYGZus{}dict\PYGZus{}t} \PYG{n}{your\PYGZus{}pinyin\PYGZus{}dict}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
            \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{啊阿呵吖}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ai}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{埃挨哎唉哀皑蔼矮碍爱隘癌艾}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{an}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{按安暗岸俺案鞍氨胺厂广庵揞犴铵桉谙鹌埯黯}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ang}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{昂肮盎仰}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ao}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{凹敖熬翱袄傲奥懊澳}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ba}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{芭捌叭吧笆八疤巴拔跋靶把坝霸罢爸扒耙}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{bai}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{白摆佰败拜柏百稗伯}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After writing a dictionary according to the above dictionary format, you only need to call this function to set up and use your dictionary:

\subsection{Input modes}
\label{\detokenize{others/ime_pinyin:input-modes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin}} supports 26 key and 9 key input modes. The mode switching is very simple, just call the function \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_set\_mode}}. If the second parameter of function \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_set\_mode}} is' 1 ', switch to 26 key input mode; if it is' 0', switch to 9 key input mode, and the default is' 1 '.



\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin}} 支持26键和9键输入模式。模式的切换非常简单，只需调用函数 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_set\_mode}} 即可。如果函数 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_ime\_pinyin\_set\_mode}} 的第2个参数为 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} 则切换到 26 键输入模式，如果为 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} 则切换到 9 键输入法模式，默认为 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} 。

\chapter{Contributing}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:contributing}}\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING::doc}}

\section{Introduction}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:introduction}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Join LVGL's community and leave your footprint in the library!

\sphinxAtStartPar
There are a lot of ways to contribute to LVGL even if you are new to the library or even new to programming.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It might be scary to make the first step but you have nothing to be afraid of.
A friendly and helpful community is waiting for you. Get to know like\sphinxhyphen{}minded people and make something great together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
So let's find which contribution option fits you the best and help you join the development of LVGL!

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before getting started here are some guidelines to make contribution smoother:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be kind and friendly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Be sure to read the relevant part of the documentation before posting a question.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ask questions in the \sphinxhref{https://forum.lvgl.io/}{Forum} and use \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/}{GitHub} for development\sphinxhyphen{}related discussions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always fill out the post or issue templates in the Forum or GitHub (or at least provide equivalent information). It makes understanding your contribution or issue easier and you will get a useful response faster.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If possible send an absolute minimal but buildable code example in order to reproduce the issue. Be sure it contains all the required variable declarations, constants, and assets (images, fonts).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxhref{https://github.com/adam-p/markdown-here/wiki/Markdown-Cheatsheet}{Markdown} to format your posts. You can learn it in 10 minutes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Speak about one thing in one issue or topic. It makes your post easier to find later for someone with the same question.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Give feedback and close the issue or mark the topic as solved if your question is answered.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For non\sphinxhyphen{}trivial fixes and features, it's better to open an issue first to discuss the details instead of sending a pull request directly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Please read and follow the Coding style guide.

\end{itemize}


\section{Pull request}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:pull-request}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Merging new code into the lvgl, documentation, blog, examples, and other repositories happen via \sphinxstyleemphasis{Pull requests} (PR for short).
A PR is a notification like "Hey, I made some updates to your project. Here are the changes, you can add them if you want."
To do this you need a copy (called fork) of the original project under your account, make some changes there, and notify the original repository about your updates.
You can see what it looks like on GitHub for LVGL here: \sphinxurl{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/pulls}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To add your changes you can edit files online on GitHub and send a new Pull request from there (recommended for small changes) or
add the updates in your favorite editor/IDE and use git to publish the changes (recommended for more complex updates).


\subsection{From GitHub}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:from-github}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Navigate to the file you want to edit.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Click the Edit button in the top right\sphinxhyphen{}hand corner.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add your changes to the file.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add a commit message on the bottom of the page.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Click the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Propose changes} button.

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{From command line}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:from-command-line}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The instructions describe the main \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} repository but it works the same way for the other repositories.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fork the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl}{lvgl repository}. To do this click the "Fork" button in the top right corner.
It will "copy" the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} repository to your GitHub account (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{https://github.com/<YOUR\_NAME>?tab=repositories}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clone your forked repository.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add your changes. You can create a \sphinxstyleemphasis{feature branch} from \sphinxstyleemphasis{master} for the updates: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{git checkout \sphinxhyphen{}b the\sphinxhyphen{}new\sphinxhyphen{}feature}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Commit and push your changes to the forked \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} repository.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a PR on GitHub from the page of your \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} repository (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{https://github.com/<YOUR\_NAME>/lvgl}}) by clicking the \sphinxstyleemphasis{"New pull request"} button. Don't forget to select the branch where you added your changes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the base branch. It means where you want to merge your update. In the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} repo both the fixes and new features go to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{master}} branch.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Describe what is in the update. An example code is welcome if applicable.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you need to make more changes, just update your forked \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} repo with new commits. They will automatically appear in the PR.

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{Commit message format}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:commit-message-format}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The commit messages format is inspired by \sphinxhref{https://gist.github.com/brianclements/841ea7bffdb01346392c}{Angular Commit Format}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following structure should be used:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{type}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{scope}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{:} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{subject}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{BLANK} \PYG{n}{LINE}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{body}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{BLANK} \PYG{n}{LINE}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{footer}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Possible \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<type>}}s:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fix}} bugfix in the source code.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feat}} new feature

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arch}} architectural changes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{perf}} changes that affect the performance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{example}} anything related to examples (even fixes and new examples)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{docs}} anything related to the documentation (even fixes, formatting, and new pages)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{test}} anything related to tests (new and updated tests or CI actions)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chore}} any minor formatting or style changes that would make the changelog noisy

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<scope>}} is the module, file, or sub\sphinxhyphen{}system that is affected by the commit. It's usually one word and can be chosen freely.
For example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{img}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layout}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{txt}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anim}}. The scope can be omitted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<subject>}} contains a short description of the change:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use the imperative, present tense: "change" not "changed" nor "changes"

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
don't capitalize the first letter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
no dot (.) at the end

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max 90 characters

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<body>}} optional and can be used to describe the details of this change.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<footer>}} shall contain
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the words "BREAKING CHANGE" if the changes break the API

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
reference to the GitHub issue or Pull Request if applicable.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some examples:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{fix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{img}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{:} \PYG{n}{update} \PYG{n}{size} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{a} \PYG{n}{new} \PYG{n}{source} \PYG{n}{is} \PYG{n}{set}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
fix(bar): fix memory leak

The animations weren\PYGZsq{}t deleted in the destructor.

Fixes: \PYGZsh{}1234
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
feat: add span widget

The span widget allows mixing different font sizes, colors and styles.
It\PYGZsq{}s similar to HTML \PYGZlt{}span\PYGZgt{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{docs}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{porting}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{:} \PYG{n}{fix} \PYG{n}{typo}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\section{Developer Certification of Origin (DCO)}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:developer-certification-of-origin-dco}}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To ensure all licensing criteria are met for every repository of the LVGL project, we apply a process called DCO (Developer's Certificate of Origin).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The text of DCO can be read here: \sphinxurl{https://developercertificate.org/}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By contributing to any repositories of the LVGL project you agree that your contribution complies with the DCO.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If your contribution fulfills the requirements of the DCO no further action is needed. If you are unsure feel free to ask us in a comment.


\subsection{Accepted licenses and copyright notices}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:accepted-licenses-and-copyright-notices}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To make the DCO easier to digest, here are some practical guides about specific cases:


\subsubsection{Your own work}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:your-own-work}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The simplest case is when the contribution is solely your own work.
In this case you can just send a Pull Request without worrying about any licensing issues.


\subsubsection{Use code from online source}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:use-code-from-online-source}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the code you would like to add is based on an article, post or comment on a website (e.g. StackOverflow) the license and/or rules of that site should be followed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example in case of StackOverflow a notice like this can be used:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cm}{/* The original version of this code\PYGZhy{}snippet was published on StackOverflow.}
\PYG{c+cm}{ * Post: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/12345}
\PYG{c+cm}{ * Author: http://stackoverflow.com/users/12345/username}
\PYG{c+cm}{ * The following parts of the snippet were changed:}
\PYG{c+cm}{ * \PYGZhy{} Check this or that}
\PYG{c+cm}{ * \PYGZhy{} Optimize performance here and there}
\PYG{c+cm}{ */}
 \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.} \PYG{n}{code} \PYG{n}{snippet} \PYG{n}{here} \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Use MIT licensed code}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:use-mit-licensed-code}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As LVGL is MIT licensed, other MIT licensed code can be integrated without issues.
The MIT license requires a copyright notice be added to the derived work. Any derivative work based on MIT licensed code must copy the original work's license file or text.


\subsubsection{Use GPL licensed code}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:use-gpl-licensed-code}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The GPL license is not compatible with the MIT license. Therefore, LVGL can not accept GPL licensed code.


\section{Ways to contribute}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:ways-to-contribute}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Even if you're just getting started with LVGL there are plenty of ways to get your feet wet.
Most of these options don't even require knowing a single line of LVGL code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Below we have collected some opportunities about the ways you can contribute to LVGL.


\subsection{Give LVGL a Star}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:give-lvgl-a-star}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Show that you like LVGL by giving it star on GitHub!







\sphinxAtStartPar
Star

\sphinxAtStartPar
This simple click makes LVGL more visible on GitHub and makes it more attractive to other people.
So with this, you already helped a lot!


\subsection{Tell what you have achieved}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:tell-what-you-have-achieved}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Have you already started using LVGL in a {\hyperref[\detokenize{get-started/platforms/pc-simulator::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Simulator}}}}, a development board, or on your custom hardware?
Was it easy or were there some obstacles? Are you happy with the result?
Showing your project to others is a win\sphinxhyphen{}win situation because it increases your and LVGL's reputation at the same time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can post about your project on Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, create a YouTube video, and so on.
Only one thing: On social media don't forget to add a link to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{https://lvgl.io}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{https://github.com/lvgl}} and use the hashtag \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#lvgl}}. Thank you! :)

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also open a new topic in the \sphinxhref{https://forum.lvgl.io/c/my-projects/10}{My projects} category of the Forum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxhref{https://blog.lvgl.io}{LVGL Blog} welcomes posts from anyone.
It's a good place to talk about a project you created with LVGL, write a tutorial, or share some nice tricks.
The latest blog posts are shown on the \sphinxhref{https://lvgl.io}{homepage of LVGL} to make your work more visible.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The blog is hosted on GitHub. If you add a post GitHub automatically turns it into a website.
See the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/blog}{README} of the blog repo to see how to add your post.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any of these help to spread the word and familiarize new developers with LVGL.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you don't want to speak about your project publicly, feel free to use \sphinxhref{https://lvgl.io/\#contact}{Contact form} on lvgl.io to private message to us.


\subsection{Write examples}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:write-examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As you learn LVGL you will probably play with the features of widgets. Why not publish your experiments?

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each widgets' documentation contains examples. For instance, here are the examples of the \sphinxhref{/widgets/core/dropdown\#examples}{Drop\sphinxhyphen{}down list} widget.
The examples are directly loaded from the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/tree/master/examples}{lvgl/examples} folder.

\sphinxAtStartPar
So all you need to do is send a {\hyperref[\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:pull-request}]{\emph{Pull request}}} to the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl}{lvgl} repository and follow some conventions:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Name the examples like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_example\_<widget\_name>\_<index>}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Make the example as short and simple as possible.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add comments to explain what the example does.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use 320x240 resolution.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Update \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{index.rst}} in the example's folder with your new example. To see how other examples are added, look in the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/tree/master/examples/widgets}{lvgl/examples/widgets} folder.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Improve the docs}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:improve-the-docs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As you read the documentation you might see some typos or unclear sentences. All the documentation is located in the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/tree/master/docs}{lvgl/docs} folder.
For typos and straightforward fixes, you can simply edit the file on GitHub.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that the documentation is also formatted in \sphinxhref{https://github.com/adam-p/markdown-here/wiki/Markdown-Cheatsheet}{Markdown}.


\subsection{Report bugs}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:report-bugs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
As you use LVGL you might find bugs. Before reporting them be sure to check the relevant parts of the documentation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If it really seems like a bug feel free to open an \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/issues}{issue on GitHub}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When filing the issue be sure to fill out the template. It helps find the root of the problem while avoiding extensive questions and exchanges with other developers.


\subsection{Send fixes}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:send-fixes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The beauty of open\sphinxhyphen{}source software is you can easily dig in to it to understand how it works. You can also fix or adjust it as you wish.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you found and fixed a bug don't hesitate to send a {\hyperref[\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:pull-request}]{\emph{Pull request}}} with the fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In your Pull request please also add a line to \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/blob/master/CHANGELOG}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CHANGELOG.md}}}.


\subsection{Join the conversations in the Forum}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:join-the-conversations-in-the-forum}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
It feels great to know you are not alone if something is not working. It's even better to help others when they struggle with something.

\sphinxAtStartPar
While you were learning LVGL you might have had questions and used the Forum to get answers. As a result, you probably have more knowledge about how LVGL works.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of the best ways to give back is to use the Forum and answer the questions of newcomers \sphinxhyphen{} like you were once.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Just read the titles and if you are familiar with the topic don't hesitate to share your thoughts and suggestions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Participating in the discussions is one of the best ways to become part of the project and get to know like\sphinxhyphen{}minded people!


\subsection{Add features}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:add-features}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have created a cool widget, or added useful feature to LVGL feel free to open a new PR for it.
We collect the optional features (a.k.a. plugins) in \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/tree/master/src/extra}{lvgl/src/extra} folder so if you are interested in adding a new features please use this folder.
The \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/blob/master/src/extra/README}{README} file describes the basics rules of contribution and also lists some ideas.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For further ideas take a look at the {\hyperref[\detokenize{ROADMAP::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc,doc,doc}{Roadmap}}}} page. If you are interested in any of them feel free to share your opinion and/or participate in the implementation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other features which are (still) not on the road map are listed in the \sphinxhref{https://forum.lvgl.io/c/feature-request/9}{Feature request} category of the Forum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When adding a new features the followings also needs to be updated:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Update \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/blob/master/lv\_conf\_template.h}{lv\_conf\_template.h}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add description in the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/tree/master/docs}{docs}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/tree/master/examples}{examples}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Update the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/tree/master/docs/CHANGELOG}{changelog}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Become a maintainer}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:become-a-maintainer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want to become part of the core development team, you can become a maintainer of a repository.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By becoming a maintainer:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You get write access to that repo:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add code directly without sending a pull request

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accept pull requests

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Close/reopen/edit issues

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Your input has higher impact when we are making decisions

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can become a maintainer by invitation, however the following conditions need to met
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Have > 50 replies in the Forum. You can look at your stats \sphinxhref{https://forum.lvgl.io/u?period=all}{here}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Send > 5 non\sphinxhyphen{}trivial pull requests to the repo where you would like to be a maintainer

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you are interested, just send a message (e.g. from the Forum) to the current maintainers of the repository. They will check if the prerequisites are met.
Note that meeting the prerequisites is not a guarantee of acceptance, i.e. if the conditions are met you won't automatically become a maintainer.
It's up to the current maintainers to make the decision.


\subsection{Move your project repository under LVGL organization}
\label{\detokenize{CONTRIBUTING:move-your-project-repository-under-lvgl-organization}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Besides the core \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} repository there are other repos for ports to development boards, IDEs or other environment.
If you ported LVGL to a new platform we can host it under the LVGL organization among the other repos.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This way your project will become part of the whole LVGL project and can get more visibility.
If you are interested in this opportunity just open an \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/issues}{issue in lvgl repo} and tell what you have!

\sphinxAtStartPar
If we agree that your port fit well into the LVGL organization, we will open a repository for your project where you will have admin rights.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To make this concept sustainable there a few rules to follow:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You need to add a README to your repo.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
We expect to maintain the repo to some extent:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Follow at least the major versions of LVGL

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Respond to the issues (in a reasonable time)

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If there is no activity in a repo for 1 year it will be archived

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope

\section{v8.3.0 6 July 2022}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:v8-3-0-6-july-2022}}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:overview}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers} Support transforming (zoom and rotate) any widgets and their children drawn by LVGL. To do this LVGL renders the transformed widgets into a layer and draws that layer as an image applying all the transformations. Layers are also used when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opa}} (not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bg\_opa}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{border\_opa}}, etc) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blend\_mode}} are set. This way nested objects are blended as one layer to avoid color bleeding. See more \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/overview/style.html\#opacity-blend-modes-and-transformations}{here}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{inherit and initial style properties} Besides setting "normal values" for style properties now you can set them to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inherit}} (inherit the parent's value) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{initial}} (set the system default). See more \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/overview/style.html\#forced-value-inheritance-default-value}{here}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NXP\sphinxhyphen{}PXP and VGLITE GPU support} The support for NXP GPUs are added again

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Color font support} You can use emojis and images in texts with this great new features. See more \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/others/imgfont.html}{here}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ARM2D GPU support} Get support for ARM's own GPU.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PubSub messaging} A publisher\sphinxhyphen{}subscriber based messaging system is added to make communication between components easier. See more \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/others/msg.html}{here}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pinyin IME} Add support for Pinyin IME Chinese input. See more \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/others/ime\_pinyin.html}{here}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render\_start\_cb} A new callback is added to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_drv\_t}} to indicate when the rendering starts. It's useful to make synchronization, e.g. wait for a TE signal.

\end{itemize}

\section{v8.2.0 31 January 2022}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:v8-2-0-31-january-2022}}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:id43}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Among many fixes and minor updates these are the most important features in v8.2.0:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Abstract render layer to make it easier to attach external draw engines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_FLAD\_OVERFLOW\_VISIBLE}}. If enabled the children of an object won't be clipped to the boundary of the object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add ffmpeg decoder support to play videos and open a wide variety of image formats

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add font fallback support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add gradient dithering support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add "monkey test"

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add cmsis\sphinxhyphen{}pack support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add Grid navigation (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_gridnav}})

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The GPU support for NXP microcontrollers is still not updated to the new draw architecture. See \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/issues/3052}{\#3052}


\subsection{Breaking Changes}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:breaking-changes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
:warning: feat(fs): add caching option for lv\_fs\sphinxhyphen{}read \sphinxhref{https://github.com/littlevgl/lvgl/pull/2979}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2979}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
:warning: feat(span): lv\_spangroup\_get\_expand\_width() adds a parameter \sphinxhref{https://github.com/littlevgl/lvgl/pull/2968}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2968}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
:warning: arch(draw): allow replacing the draw engine \sphinxhref{https://github.com/littlevgl/lvgl/commit/db53ea925c9502b20f38db0fc30c4ef599bdfc33}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{db53ea9}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
:warning: indexed images are not chroma keyed. Use the alpha chaneel instead.

\end{itemize}

\section{v8.1.0 10 November 2021}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:v8-1-0-10-november-2021}}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:id50}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
v8.1 is a minor release, so besides many fixes it contains a lot of new features too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some of the most important features are
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Built in support for SDL based GPU drawing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Much faster circle drawing in the software renderer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Several \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/master/libs/index.html}{3rd party libraries} are merged directly into LVGL.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add LVGL as an \sphinxhref{https://packages.rt-thread.org/en/detail.html?package=LVGL}{RT\sphinxhyphen{}Thread} and \sphinxhref{https://components.espressif.com/component/lvgl/lvgl}{ESP32} component

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Breaking Changes}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:id51}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
:warning: feat(calendar): add the header directly into the calendar widget \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/commit/2e08f80361a9d7e5b97f49af6afc3549ffbf2758}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2e08f80}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Architectural}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:id52}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
arch add small 3rd party libs to lvgl  \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lvgl/pull/2569}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2569}}}

\end{itemize}

\section{v8.0.0 (01.06.2021)}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:v8-0-0-01-06-2021}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
v8.0 brings many new features like simplified and more powerful scrolling, new layouts inspired by CSS Flexbox and Grid, simplified and improved widgets, more powerful events, hookable drawing, and more.

\sphinxAtStartPar
v8 is a major change and therefore it's not backward compatible with v7.


\subsection{Directory structure}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:directory-structure}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_}} prefix is removed from the folder names

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{docs}} is moved to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} repository

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples}} are moved to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lvgl}} repository

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/extra}} folder for complex widgets:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It makes the core LVGL leaner

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extra}} we can have a lot and specific widgets

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Good place for contributions

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Widget changes}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:widget-changes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_cont}} removed, layout features are moved to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_page}} removed, scroll features are moved to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_objmask}} the same can be achieved by events

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_meter}} added as the union of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_linemeter}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_gauge}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_span}} new widget mimicking HTML \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<span>}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_animing}} new widget for simple slideshow animations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
+ many minor changes and improvements

\end{itemize}


\subsection{New scrolling}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:new-scrolling}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Support "elastic" scrolling when scrolled in

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Support scroll chaining among any objects types (not only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_pages}}s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Remove \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_drag}}. Similar effect can be achieved by setting the position in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_EVENT\_PRESSING}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add snapping

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add snap stop to scroll max 1 snap point

\end{itemize}


\subsection{New layouts}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:new-layouts}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://css-tricks.com/snippets/css/a-guide-to-grid/}{CSS Grid}\sphinxhyphen{}like layout support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://css-tricks.com/snippets/css/a-guide-to-flexbox/}{CSS Flexbox}\sphinxhyphen{}like layout support

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Styles}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:styles}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Optimize and simplify styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
State is saved in the object instead of the style property

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Object size and position can be set in styles too

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Events}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:events}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow adding multiple events to an object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{user\_data}} can be attached to the added events

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Driver changes}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:driver-changes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_disp\_drv\_t}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_indev\_drv\_t}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_fs\_drv\_t}} needs to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{static}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{...disp\_buf...}} is renamed to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{draw\_buf}}. See an initialization example \sphinxhref{https://github.com/lvgl/lv\_sim\_eclipse\_sdl/blob/release/v8.0/main.c\#L128-L141}{here}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No partial update if two screen sized buffers are set

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{disp\_drv\sphinxhyphen{}>full\_refresh = 1}} makes always the whole display redraw.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hor\_res}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ver\_res}} need to be set in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{disp\_drv}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indev\_read\_cb}} returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}. To indicate that there is more that to read set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{data\sphinxhyphen{}>continue\_reading = 1}} in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{read\_cb}}

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Other changes}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:other-changes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Remove the copy parameter from create functions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Simplified File system interface API

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a more generic inheritance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The built\sphinxhyphen{}in themes are reworked

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_align}} now saved the alignment and realigns the object automatically but can't be used to align to other than the parent

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj\_align\_to}} can align to an object but doesn't save the alignment

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_pct(x)}} can be used to set the size and position in percentage

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are many other changes in widgets that are not detailed here. Please refer to the documentation of the widgets.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{New release policy}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:new-release-policy}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
We will follow \sphinxhref{https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/topics/gitlab\_flow.html\#release-branches-with-gitlab-flow}{Release branches with GitLab flow}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Minor releases are expected in every 3\sphinxhyphen{}4 month

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{master}} will always contain the latest changes

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Migrating from v7 to v8}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:migrating-from-v7-to-v8}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
First and foremost, create a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} based on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf\_template.h}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To try the new version it's recommended to use a simulator project and see the examples.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When migrating your project to v8
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Update the drivers are described above

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Update the styles

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Update the events

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the new layouts instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_cont}} features

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_obj}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_page}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the changes in \sphinxhref{https://docs.lvgl.io/8.0/overview/color.html}{Colors}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The other parts are mainly minor renames and refactoring. See the functions' documentation for descriptions.

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\subsection{New features}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:id77}}\begin{itemize}

\section{v7.0.0 (18.05.2020)}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:v7-0-0-18-05-2020}}

\subsection{Documentation}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:documentation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The docs for v7 is available at https://docs.littlevgl.com/v7/en/html/index.html


\subsection{Legal changes}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:legal-changes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The name of the project is changed to LVGL and the new website is on https://lvgl.io

\sphinxAtStartPar
LVGL remains free under the same conditions (MIT license) and a company is created to manage LVGL and offer services.


\subsection{New drawing system}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:new-drawing-system}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Complete rework of LVGL's draw engine to use "masks" for more advanced and higher quality graphical effects.
A possible use\sphinxhyphen{}case of this system is to remove the overflowing content from the rounded edges.
It also allows drawing perfectly anti\sphinxhyphen{}aliased circles, lines, and arcs.
Internally, the drawings happen by defining masks (such as rounded rectangle, line, angle).
When something is drawn the currently active masks can make some pixels transparent.
For example, rectangle borders are drawn by using 2 rectangle masks: one mask removes the inner part and another the outer part.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The API in this regard remained the same but some new functions were added:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_zoom}}: set image object's zoom factor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_angle}}: set image object's angle without using canvas

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_img\_set\_pivot}}: set the pivot point of rotation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The new drawing engine brought new drawing features too. They are highlighted in the "style" section.


\subsection{New style system}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:new-style-system}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The old style system is replaced with a new more flexible and lightweighted one.
It uses an approach similar to CSS: support cascading styles, inheriting properties and local style properties per object.
As part of these updates, a lot of objects were reworked and the APIs have been changed.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
more shadows options: \sphinxstyleemphasis{offset} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{spread}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gradient stop position to shift the gradient area and horizontal gradient

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_BLEND\_MODE\_NORMAL/ADDITIVE/SUBTRACTIVE}} blending modes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{clip corner}: crop the content on the rounded corners

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{text underline} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{strikethrough}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dashed vertical and horizontal lines (\sphinxstyleemphasis{dash gap}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{dash\_width})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{outline}: a border\sphinxhyphen{}like part drawn out of the background. Can have spacing to the background.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{pattern}: display and image in the middle of the background or repeat it

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{value} display a text which is stored in the style. It can be used e.g. as a light\sphinxhyphen{}weighted text on buttons too.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{margin}: similar to \sphinxstyleemphasis{padding} but used to keep space outside the object

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Read the \sphinxhref{https://docs.littlevgl.com/v7/en/html/overview/style.html}{Style} section of the documentation to learn how the new styles system works.


\subsection{GPU integration}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:gpu-integration}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To better utilize GPUs, from this version GPU usage can be integrated into LVGL. In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} any supported GPUs can be enabled with a single configuration option.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Right now, only ST's DMA2D (Chrom\sphinxhyphen{}ART) is integrated. More will in the upcoming releases.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ddlist \sphinxhyphen{}> dropdown

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
btnm \sphinxhyphen{}> btnmatrix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
kb \sphinxhyphen{}> keyboard

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
preload \sphinxhyphen{}> spinner

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lv\_objx folder \sphinxhyphen{}> lv\_widgets

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Reworked and improved object}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:reworked-and-improved-object}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropdown}}: Completely reworked. Now creates a separate list when opened and can be dropped to down/up/left/right.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{body\_draw}} is removed, instead, if its style has a visible background/border/shadow etc it will be drawn. Padding really makes the object larger (not just virtually as before)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arc}}: can draw background too.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{btn}}: doesn't store styles for each state because it's done naturally in the new style system.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{calendar}}: highlight the pressed datum. The used styles are changed: use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CALENDAR\_PART\_DATE}} normal for normal dates, checked for highlighted, focused for today, pressed for the being pressed. (checked+pressed, focused+pressed also work)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart}}: only has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LINE}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{COLUMN}} types because with new styles all the others can be described. LV\_CHART\_PART\_SERIES sets the style of the series. bg\_opa > 0 draws an area in LINE mode. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_PART\_SERIES\_BG}} also added to set a different style for the series area. Padding in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LV\_CHART\_PART\_BG}} makes the series area smaller, and it ensures space for axis labels/numbers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{linemeter}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gauge}}: can have background if the related style properties are set. Padding makes the scale/lines smaller. scale\_border\_width and scale\_end\_border\_width allow to draw an arc on the outer part of the scale lines.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gauge}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_gauge\_set\_needle\_img}} allows use image as needle

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{canvas}}: allow drawing to true color alpha and alpha only canvas, add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_blur\_hor/ver}} and rename \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_rotate}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_canvas\_transform}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{textarea}}: If available in the font use bullet (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{U+2022}}) character in text area password

\end{itemize}


\subsection{New object types}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:new-object-types}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_objmask}}: masks can be added to it. The children will be masked accordingly.

\end{itemize}

\subsection{New release policy}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:id91}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Maintain this Changelog for every release

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Save old major version in new branches. E.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{release/v6}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Merge new features and fixes directly into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{master}} and release a patch or minor releases every 2 weeks.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Migrating from v6 to v7}
\label{\detokenize{CHANGELOG:migrating-from-v6-to-v7}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
First and foremost, create a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf.h}} based on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lv\_conf\_template.h}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To try the new version it suggested using a simulator project and see the examples.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you have a running project, the most difficult part of the migration is updating to the new style system. Unfortunately, there is no better way than manually updating to the new format.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The other parts are mainly minor renames and refactoring as described above.

\end{itemize}
